findings.what: Every 206 from the assets Worker carries an invalid `Content-Range: bytes NaN-NaN/<size>`, and an unsatisfiable Range answers HTTP 500 without CORS headers instead of 416.
findings.evidence: cloudflare/assets-worker/src/index.js:115-122 — `const offset = 'suffix' in r ? object.size - r.suffix : (r.offset ?? 0); const length = 'suffix' in r ? r.suffix : (r.length ?? object.size - offset); headers.set('content-range', `bytes ${offset}-${offset + length - 1}/${object.size}`)`; R2 `get()` at :95 is called with `range: request.headers` and never wrapped. Live 2026-09-27: `curl -H 'Range: bytes=0-99' https://sc-assets.sc-assets-worker.workers.dev/ship-skins/DRAK_Cutlass_Black/elysium.webp` → HTTP/2 206, content-length: 100, content-range: bytes NaN-NaN/10898; `Range: bytes=-50` → 206, content-range: bytes NaN-NaN/10898; `Range: bytes=999999999-` → HTTP/2 500 (17-byte body, no access-control-allow-origin). No `accept-ranges` header anywhere in index.js.
findings.fix: In index.js parse the Range header yourself (single `bytes=a-b`, `bytes=a-`, `bytes=-n`), return 416 with `content-range: bytes */<size>` (+CORS) when the start is >= object.size, pass an explicit `{offset,length}`/`{suffix}` to `env.ASSETS.get`, build Content-Range from those numbers (do not read `object.range` with `'suffix' in r` — R2 apparently returns the key with value undefined), and add `accept-ranges: bytes` to baseHeaders. Extend test/index.test.mjs with a fake bucket that honours `opts.range` and cases for 206 (both forms) and 416.

findings.what: Release builds of the uploader are signed with the public dev telemetry key, so crash / extract-abort / job-diagnostics reports from shipped binaries are rejected by the ingest function whenever the production secret is set — and the rejection is only logged at debug level.
findings.evidence: .github/workflows/data-uploader-build.yml:80-86 build-windows env sets only `SC_API_BASE` and `SC_WEB_BASE` (grep for TELEMETRY_HMAC in that file: 0 hits); .github/workflows/wallpaper-app-build.yml:39 sets `SC_TELEMETRY_HMAC_KEY: ${{ secrets.SC_TELEMETRY_HMAC_KEY }}` for the sibling app; data-uploader/electron.vite.config.ts:74-76 `__SC_TELEMETRY_HMAC_KEY__: JSON.stringify(process.env['SC_TELEMETRY_HMAC_KEY'] ?? 'scc-telemetry-dev-key-v1')` with the comment "CI sets SC_TELEMETRY_HMAC_KEY to the real secret for release builds"; supabase/functions/ingest-telemetry/index.ts:46 `Deno.env.get('TELEMETRY_HMAC_KEY') ?? 'scc-telemetry-dev-key-v1'`; data-uploader/src/main/telemetry-reporter.ts:89-91 a non-2xx reply is `log.debug(...)` only (file transport level is 'info', logging.ts:34, so it never reaches main.log).
findings.fix: Add `SC_TELEMETRY_HMAC_KEY: ${{ secrets.SC_TELEMETRY_HMAC_KEY }}` to the `build-windows` job env in .github/workflows/data-uploader-build.yml (same secret the wallpaper workflow already uses); optionally raise telemetry-reporter.ts:90 to `log.warn` so a 401 from ingest-telemetry is visible in main.log.

findings.what: Deleting a hangar config that has ever been shared or adopted fails: the FK actions `on delete set null` on hangar_share_links.source_config_id and hangar_ship_configs.source_config_id run as UPDATEs that fire the BEFORE UPDATE guard triggers, which reject any change to source_config_id with 42501. deleteConfig(), removeShip() (cascade) and delete-user (cascade) all hit it.
findings.evidence: supabase/migrations/20260920160000_hangar_loadout_sharing.sql:250 `source_config_id uuid references public.hangar_ship_configs(id) on delete set null` + :302-313 `if new.token is distinct from old.token … or new.source_config_id is distinct from old.source_config_id … raise exception 'only revoked_at may be updated on a share link'`; same file :93 self-FK `on delete set null` + :179-181 `if new.source_config_id is distinct from old.source_config_id then raise exception 'source_config_id is immutable'` (v_internal is only set inside the two RPCs, never by an RI action). Client sets it on every link: src/app/hangar/hangar.service.ts:855-863 `.insert({ … source_config_id: config.id`; delete paths: hangar.service.ts:693 `from('hangar_ship_configs').delete().eq('id', id)`, :441 `from('hangar_ships').delete()`, supabase/functions/delete-user/index.ts:142 `auth.admin.deleteUser`. Contradicts the file's own contract :53-56 'existing followers keep following until the owner deletes the source config'. PostgreSQL executes referential actions as ordinary UPDATE/DELETE statements that fire row triggers on the referencing table.
findings.fix: In both trigger functions allow the one-way transition `old.source_config_id is not null and new.source_config_id is null` (and in hangar_ship_configs_share_guard also set follows_owner=false, forked_at=now() on that transition); keep every other change rejected. Alternatively change both FKs to `on delete no action` and null them out explicitly inside a SECURITY DEFINER delete RPC.

findings.what: Share-link bearer tokens are sent to PostHog: the pageview URL keeps the path, so a visit to /hangar/shared/<token> or /shared/loadout/<token> (with statistics consent on) ships the 64-hex share token to eu.i.posthog.com as $current_url.
findings.evidence: src/app/core/analytics.service.ts:189 `return origin + routerUrl.split(/[?#]/)[0];` (only query+fragment stripped; measured: pageviewUrl('/hangar/shared/AbC123?x=1#y') → 'https://x/hangar/shared/AbC123'); src/app/core/analytics.service.ts:175 `this.capture('$pageview', { $current_url: pageviewUrl(routerUrl) });`; routes src/app/app.routes.ts:96 `path: 'shared/loadout/:token'`, :109 `path: 'hangar/shared/:token'`; the token is the whole authorisation of peek/get_shared_loadout (supabase/migrations/20260904020000_social_moderation_sharing.sql:1032 'only with a live 64-hex-char share token')
findings.fix: In src/app/core/analytics.service.ts `pageviewUrl()`, replace the token segment of `/shared/loadout/:token`, `/hangar/shared/:token` (and `/konzept/:id`) with a fixed placeholder such as `:token` before capture; add a case to analytics.service.spec.ts.

findings.what: Patch search recomputes the British/American spelling variants (14 regex tests per token) for every haystack line on every keystroke, with no debounce; measured 176 ms per keystroke over 50 000 lines (2 tokens) — a long task well past the 50 ms mark once 'load all notes' has pulled the full history in.
findings.evidence: src/app/news/patch-search.ts:479-483 `matchesFuzzy … tokens.every((t) => spellingVariants(t).some((v) => hay.includes(v)))` (spellingVariants :443-457 runs SPELLING_PAIRS + 15 regex rules per call); callers per line: src/app/news/patch-find.ts:72,106, src/app/news/patch-dossier.component.ts:729; input bound synchronously src/app/news/patch-board.component.ts:110,567. Bench (node --experimental-strip-types, scratchpad/bench-fuzzy.mts): 176.5 ms vs 82.2 ms with variants memoized.
findings.fix: Memoize `spellingVariants` in a module-level `Map<string, string[]>` in patch-search.ts (tokens are short and bounded by what the user types); optionally hoist `normalizeSearchText` of each outline node into the outline once when it loads.

findings.what: After a deploy the service worker's documented unrecoverable state (a cached asset hash that no longer exists on the server) is never handled: the user keeps a broken shell (missing styles/eager chunks) until a manual reload. RouteLoadRecoveryService only reacts to router NavigationError for lazy route chunks.
findings.evidence: `grep -rn unrecoverable src/` → 0 hits; src/app/core/sw-update.service.ts:56-76 subscribes only `versionUpdates` (`filter(... event.type === 'VERSION_READY')`); `SwUpdate.unrecoverable: Observable<UnrecoverableStateEvent>` exists in node_modules/@angular/service-worker/types/service-worker.d.ts:443. route-load-recovery.service.ts:112-118 handles only `NavigationError` whose error matches MODULE_LOAD_MARKERS.
findings.fix: In `SwUpdateService.init()` add `this.swUpdate.unrecoverable.subscribe(() => this.zone.run(() => this.document.location.reload()))`, guarded by the existing once-per-session `AUTO_RELOAD_FLAG` so it cannot loop; add one spec case in sw-update.service.spec.ts.

findings.what: The Worker test suite never exercises the Range/206 branch, OPTIONS, or an upstream fetch that throws — the fake bucket ignores `opts.range` and never sets `object.range`, which is how the live NaN Content-Range shipped.
findings.evidence: cloudflare/assets-worker/test/index.test.mjs:25-31 — `async get(key, opts = {}) { … const inm = opts.onlyIf?.get?.('if-none-match'); … return { ...meta, body: … } }` (no `range` field on the returned object, `opts.range` unused); describe('fetch') at :60-110 has 200/304/HEAD/fallback-200/fallback-400/405 cases only; `grep -n 'range\|OPTIONS' test/index.test.mjs` → no test names.
findings.fix: In test/index.test.mjs make `fakeBucket.get` honour `opts.range` (slice the bytes, set `range` on the returned object the way R2 does, including a `suffix: undefined` key) and add cases: `Range: bytes=0-3` → 206 + `content-range: bytes 0-3/4`, `bytes=-2` → 206, `bytes=99-` → 416, OPTIONS → 204 with CORS, upstream `fetch` throwing → 502 with CORS.

findings.what: The gate's auth-redirect check only recognises a landing on /login; a route bounced by approvedGuard to /unavailable or by roleGuard to /news (e.g. /admin/feedback under a non-admin test account) is measured and reported under the requested route's name, and a redirected row without findings is never annotated.
findings.evidence: scripts/mobile-gate.mjs:1022-1032 — `const isLogin = (path) => path === '/login' || path.startsWith('/login/'); … if (!isLogin(landedPath)) return null;`; src/app/auth/approved.guard.ts:66 `return router.createUrlTree(['/unavailable'], { queryParams: { redirect: state.url } });`; src/app/auth/role.guard.ts:29 `return router.createUrlTree(['/news']);`; app.routes.ts:361 `path: 'admin/feedback'` under `canActivate: [roleGuard('admin')]` while mobile-gate.config.json auth.routes lists '/admin/feedback' and docs/mobile-gate.md:262 says a plain approved user is a valid account for --auth. Report annotation at :1092 `const redirected = r.finalUrl && r.finalUrl !== (r.path || r.route) ? … : ''` sits inside `if (!errs.length && !warns.length) continue;` (:1087), so a clean bounced row prints nothing.
findings.fix: In authRedirect() flag any landed path that differs from the requested path (path only, query ignored) as `auth-redirect` — not just /login — and add cases to AUTH_REDIRECT_CASES for `/admin/feedback → /news` and `/codex → /unavailable?redirect=…` (expect true) plus `/hangar → /hangar?tab=fleet` (already false); in report() print the `(redirected → …)` note for every row whose finalUrl path differs, before the findings filter; update the auth-redirect row in docs/mobile-gate.md.

findings.what: The Playwright init page's `/__sc-test-session` route fulfils top-level navigations: from any app tab a plain `browser_navigate` to that path renders the minted session JSON (access + refresh token) as the page, and a `browser_snapshot` then puts the tokens into the transcript — the exact leak test-account.md forbids.
findings.evidence: scripts/playwright/test-session.cjs:77-83 — `function isSameOriginCaller(request, origin) { try { return new URL(request.frame().url()).origin === origin; } …` and :127-145 route handler with no `isNavigationRequest()` / `resourceType()` check (`grep -n 'isNavigationRequest\|resourceType' scripts/playwright/test-session.cjs` → none); a navigation from an app page passes whether frame.url() is the previous app page or the new same-origin URL. Body is served as `contentType: 'application/json'` (:140-142), which Chromium renders as text. .claude/deep-knowledge/test-account.md:80 'Never read `sc.auth` … the token stays out of the transcript' relies on convention only.
findings.fix: In the route handler refuse `route.request().isNavigationRequest()` (and accept only `resourceType() === 'xhr'`) with 403 + a log line, extend `fakeRoute()` in scripts/lib/test-account.test.mjs with `isNavigationRequest`/`resourceType` and add a test 'refuses a top-level navigation to the session path'; note in test-account.md that navigating to /__sc-test-session is refused.

findings.what: A cold `codex_armor_rating` call still runs past 3 s on production (first anonymous call answered HTTP 500 after 3.96 s, the second 200 after 3.1 s, warm 0.6–1.9 s); the client maps any error to `null` and the set page hides the Einordnung card without an error state or retry, so the first reader after a cold cache gets a page with no rating and no way to ask again short of a reload.
findings.evidence: Live probe (anon, publishable key, p_class_names=[vgl_armor_light_helmet_01_01_01, srvl_helmet_01_01_01]): `http=500 time=3.962092s` then `http=200 time=3.114883s`, later `0.590959s`–`1.855704s`; baseline `codex_builds?limit=1` 0.70–0.99 s. src/app/codex/codex.service.ts:833 `if (error || !data) return null;` src/app/codex/set/codex-set.component.ts:341-343 `land(this.ratingRows, await this.svc.armorRating(...))` / `land(this.ratingRows, null)`; migration comment 20260926150000:7 "ran past anon's 3 s statement_timeout on a cold one".

findings.what: When the browser loses the WebGL context of the board figure (GPU reset, too many contexts on a long set ⇄ arsenal session), the canvas goes blank while `ready()` stays true, so the SVG fallback stays hidden and the set page shows leader lines pointing at an empty figure.

findings.what: Declining a user topic can silently half-succeed: the status flips to 'declined' first, then the author-facing explanation is inserted without checking the result, so a failed insert leaves a declined topic whose author never sees the note while the admin sees success.

findings.fix: Destructure `const { error: noteErr } = await …insert(…)`; on error set `this.errorMsg.set(noteErr.message)` (same pattern as line 2642), still refresh, and return false so the sheet stays open for a retry.

findings.what: Thread and author-thread load failures are swallowed with no log and no UI signal; because bucketing reads the replies, a silent thread failure can move cards between bands without anyone knowing why.
findings.evidence: src/app/admin/feedback/admin-feedback.component.ts:2167 `if (error) return;` (loadThreads), :2212 `if (error) return;` (loadAuthorThreads); feedbackBucket/isContinuedAfterShip depend on replies (feedback.types.ts:417-449). `grep -rn "console\." src/app/admin` = 0 and src/app/core has no logger service, so nothing records the failure.
findings.fix: Keep the additive behaviour but record it: add a `threadsStale = signal(false)` set on error and cleared on success, render a quiet `adminFeedback.threadsStale` hint under the topbar, and `console.warn('[admin-feedback] threads load failed', error.code)` until a logger exists.

findings.what: A single failed background refresh replaces the whole patch board (monitor, chart, search, stack) with an error card even though the feed is still loaded; the board stays blank until the next successful poll (5 min) or a tab-visibility refresh.
findings.evidence: src/app/news/patch-board.component.ts:72-74 `@if (svc.error(); as err) { <div class="sc-card err">… } @else if (svc.loading() && !svc.feed())` — error wins over a present feed; src/app/news/news.service.ts:193-195 sets `error` on every failed fetchFeed (silent polls included, startPolling :234-238) while `feed` keeps the last payload. news-list.component.ts:175 does it right (`@else if (svc.error())` only when there is no stage).
findings.fix: In patch-board.component.ts change the guard to `@if (svc.error() && !svc.feed(); as err)` so the error card only shows on a cold failure; keep the loaded stack on a failed refresh.

findings.what: None of the news HTTP calls (feed, roadmap, note outlines, stability tables) has a timeout; the app registers only the auth interceptor, so a stalled edge function keeps the skeleton/`pending` state up indefinitely.
findings.evidence: src/app/news/news.service.ts:188 `await firstValueFrom(this.http.get<VerseFeed>(this.endpoint));` src/app/news/roadmap.service.ts:105,187 same pattern; src/app/news/patch-stability.service.ts:535-537 `Promise.all([client.from(...).select('*'), …])`; src/app/app.config.ts:40 `provideHttpClient(withFetch(), withInterceptors([authInterceptor]))` — grep `timeout(` in src/app → 0 hits.
findings.fix: Add `.pipe(timeout(20_000))` (rxjs) to the three HttpClient gets in news.service.ts and roadmap.service.ts, and `AbortSignal.timeout(20_000)` via `.abortSignal()` on the two Supabase queries in patch-stability.service.ts; the existing catch blocks already turn the TimeoutError into the error/unavailable state.

findings.what: Three network error paths in the news module swallow the exception with an empty `catch {}` — a roadmap/outline/stability outage leaves nothing in the console, so a 'the patch board is empty' report cannot be diagnosed from the client.
findings.evidence: src/app/news/roadmap.service.ts:109 `} catch { this.unavailable.set(true); }`, :206 `} catch {` (outline batch); src/app/news/patch-stability.service.ts:95 `} catch { this._unavailable.set(true); }`. Project convention elsewhere: src/app/codex/codex.service.ts:1292 `console.error('[codex] getEntityPayloads chunk failed', kind, error)`.
findings.fix: Bind the error (`catch (err)`) and add `console.warn('[news] roadmap unavailable', err)`, `console.warn('[news] outlines failed', slugs, err)`, `console.warn('[news] stability tables unavailable', err)` before the state flips.

findings.what: Both modal dialogs in the news module (article detail overlay, patch dossier) declare `role="dialog" aria-modal="true"` but never move focus into the dialog, trap it, or restore it on close — a keyboard/screen-reader user stays on the card behind the scrim and Tab walks the page underneath.
findings.evidence: src/app/news/news-list.component.ts:320 `role="dialog" aria-modal="true"`, :1142-1151 `openDetail` only attaches the portal; src/app/news/patch-dossier.component.ts:113 `role="dialog" aria-modal="true"`, :803-813 ngOnInit only wires scroll. `grep -n "\.focus(\|cdkTrapFocus\|FocusTrap" src/app/news/*.ts` → 0 hits; the app has the pattern in src/app/desktop/app-download-menu.component.ts:465-486.
findings.fix: news-list: after `overlayRef.attach`, focus `.nd-back` (afterNextRender) and remember/restore `document.activeElement` in closeDetail; dossier: focus `.close` on init and wrap `.panel` with `cdkTrapFocus` from @angular/cdk/a11y (CDK is already a dependency).

findings.what: The patch board's row entrance animation (14 px slide + fade, 0.42 s, staggered per row) runs under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`; only the skeleton shimmer is switched off, although the comment above the rule promises 'reduced motion drops it entirely'.
findings.evidence: src/app/news/patch-board.component.ts:241 `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .skeleton .card { animation: none; } }` vs :357-361 `/* … reduced motion drops it entirely. */ .row { animation: pb-in 0.42s cubic-bezier(…) both; … }` — no `.row` rule inside any reduced-motion query (grep prefers-reduced-motion in the file → one hit, line 241).
findings.fix: Extend the media query in patch-board.component.ts to `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .skeleton .card, .row { animation: none; } }`.

findings.what: On /news every stream tile's first image layer is requested eager with `fetchpriority="high"` — 12 thumbnails (more after 'show more') compete at top priority with the stage hero that is the page's LCP, and below-the-fold tiles are never lazy.
findings.evidence: src/app/news/news-thumb.component.ts:410-411 `[attr.loading]="i === 0 ? 'eager' : 'lazy'" [attr.fetchpriority]="i === 0 ? 'high' : null"` — not gated on `featured()`; news-list.component.ts:247-252 renders `<sc-news-thumb … [featured]="false">` per stream tile (STREAM_PAGE = 12, :34).
findings.fix: Gate on the featured input: `[attr.loading]="featured() && i === 0 ? 'eager' : 'lazy'"` and `[attr.fetchpriority]="featured() && i === 0 ? 'high' : null"` in news-thumb.component.ts (the ImgReadyDirective already tolerates lazy layers, see its comment lines 11-16).

findings.what: The Data-Uploader/download panels expose the raw i18n key 'desktop.appTitle' as a native browser tooltip: `title="desktop.appTitle"` is written as a static attribute on the <sc-app-download-panel> host, so hovering the panel shows the key text (and a native title, REQ-8).
findings.evidence: src/app/desktop/desktop-download.component.ts:52 `title="desktop.appTitle"`, src/app/desktop/download.component.ts:37, src/app/desktop/uploader-access.component.ts:54 — panel input is `readonly title = input.required<string>()` (src/app/desktop/app-download-panel.component.ts:210); compiled dist chunk consts carry `["icon","⬆","title","desktop.appTitle",…]` as static DOM attributes.
findings.fix: Bind the key instead of writing a static attribute in the three call sites: `[title]="'desktop.appTitle'"` (or rename the panel input to `titleKey`), so no DOM `title` attribute is emitted.

findings.what: Drawing-board tiles are links carrying `role="listitem"`, which overrides the link role: a screen reader announces them as list items, not links, and `listitem` is not a permitted role on `<a href>`.
findings.evidence: src/app/hangar/hangar-dashboard.component.ts:157-163 `<div class="db-scroll" role="list">` … `<a class="db-tile" role="listitem" [routerLink]="['/codex/upcoming', a.id]">` and `<a class="db-tile" role="listitem" [href]="c.rsiUrl" target="_blank" …>`.
findings.fix: Keep `role="list"` on `.db-scroll`, wrap each tile in `<div role="listitem">` (or switch to `<ul>/<li>`) and remove `role="listitem"` from the two `<a>` elements and the static `<div>`.

findings.what: `/codex/keybinds` renders the whole action profile (~1 000 rows, hard cap 10 000) as one expanded DOM list with a tooltip directive instance and four method calls per row, re-evaluated on every change detection — each search keystroke re-filters and re-renders all of it.
findings.evidence: src/app/codex/keybinds.component.ts:295-315 `@for (g of groups(); track g.actionmap) { … @for (r of g.rows; track r.key) { <li class="row" [class.picked]="isSelected(r)" … [scTooltip]="rowTitle(r)">` and :341 `@for (c of chips(r); …)` with `tx(c.key)`; no `shown`/page signal in the file (`grep -n 'PAGE\|showMore' keybinds.component.ts` → none); data size: src/app/codex/codex.service.ts:288-289 `KEYBIND_PAGE_SIZE = 1000; KEYBIND_MAX_PAGES = 10;`, src/app/codex/keybind-category.service.ts:146 "re-reading ~1k rows per save"; search input is set synchronously (:847 `this.searchInput.set(v)`) with no debounce. Compare fps-list, which pages at 60 (src/app/codex/fps-list.component.ts:51,749).
findings.fix: Render category sections collapsed by default (native `<details>` per `.cat`, first one open) or page rows like fps-list (`shown` signal + load-more), and move `chips(r)`/`rowTitle(r)` into the row objects built in the `groups` computed so the template only reads fields.

findings.what: The plain-viewer feedback panel paints "the team asked you a question" and the unread dot in `--sc-accent-hot`, which CLAUDE.md reserves for elevated-access surfaces.
findings.evidence: src/app/feedback/user-feedback-panel.component.ts:308-313 `.tab-dot { background: var(--sc-accent-hot); }`, :341 `.topic.needs-answer { border-color: var(--sc-accent-hot); }`, :380 `.status-pill.question { border-color: var(--sc-accent-hot); color: var(--sc-accent-hot); }`, :458-463 `.reply-badge { border: 1px solid var(--sc-accent-hot); color: var(--sc-accent-hot); }`. The panel is mounted only for non-admins (src/app/shell/user-feedback-fab.component.ts:312 `!this.roles.isAdmin()`). Contrast the same file's own area picker comment (feedback-area-picker.component.ts:1193-1196) and CHANGELOG entry "Red now means what the rest of the app means by it" (CHANGELOG.md:2015, admin panel).
findings.fix: Switch the four rules to `--sc-accent` (or `--sc-warning` for the needs-answer state so it still stands out) in user-feedback-panel.component.ts; the meaning is already carried by the pill text.

findings.what: The all-time stability chart's columns navigate to the dossier route but are rendered as `<button (click)>`, so middle-click / Ctrl-click / 'open in new tab' cannot open a patch from the chart (RULE-B); the component comment claiming the click 'expands that line on this page' is stale.
findings.evidence: src/app/news/stability-history.component.ts:664-666 comment 'A column is a BUTTON because clicking it expands that line on this page (an action), not a navigation', :682-684 `<button type="button" class="col" … (click)="showLine.emit(v.line)">`; src/app/news/patch-board.component.ts:95 `(showLine)="openLine($event)"`, :578-580 `void this.router.navigate(['/news/patches', line], …)`.
findings.fix: Render each column as `<a class="col" [routerLink]="['/news/patches', v.line]" [queryParams]="queryParams()">` (add a `queryParams` input to sc-stability-history fed from the board's query), drop the `showLine` output and `openLine`, and update the stale comment.

findings.what: The stability-history chart columns navigate (open /news/patches/:line) but are <button>s, so middle click / Ctrl+click / 'open in new tab' do not work on them.
findings.evidence: src/app/news/stability-history.component.ts:34-36 `<button type="button" class="col" … (click)="showLine.emit(v.line)">`; parent src/app/news/patch-board.component.ts:95 `(showLine)="openLine($event)"` → :579 `void this.router.navigate(['/news/patches', line], …)`.
findings.fix: Render each column as `<a class="col" [routerLink]="['/news/patches', v.line]" [queryParams]="query ? { q: query } : null" (click)="onCol($event, v.line)">` with `onCol` gated by isPlainLeftClick (emit + preventDefault only on a plain left click); pass the current `q` into the component as an input; update the spec selector `button.col` → `a.col`.

findings.what: Undo after a clear re-equips the piece without any expectation, so it overwrites whatever another tab or device put into that slot during the 5 s undo window (and re-adds a piece another tab deliberately removed).
findings.evidence: src/app/codex/set/codex-set-gear.component.ts:367 `await this.hangar.setRoleLoadoutSlot(this.setId(), last.slot, { className: last.className, kind: last.kind })` — no 4th `expect` argument; src/app/hangar/hangar.service.ts:792 only guards when `expect !== undefined`; codex-set-gear.component.ts:351-352 offers Undo whenever the server slot comes back empty, including when another tab emptied it (`undefined !== shown`).
findings.fix: Let `expect: null` in `setRoleLoadoutSlot` mean "the slot must still be empty" (compare `find(...)?.className ?? null`), pass it from `undo()`, and show the conflict note when the set comes back holding a different piece.

findings.what: Hovering the whole app-download panel shows an OS tooltip with the raw i18n key "desktop.appTitle": the static attribute title="desktop.appTitle" on the <sc-app-download-panel> host is written to the DOM as a native title (Angular renders static attributes on component hosts even when they also feed an input), so a native tooltip with the untranslated key appears on /download, /uploader and the uploader-access box.
findings.evidence: src/app/desktop/download.component.ts:37 `title="desktop.appTitle"`; src/app/desktop/desktop-download.component.ts:52 same; src/app/desktop/uploader-access.component.ts:54 same; the input is `readonly title = input.required<string>()` (src/app/desktop/app-download-panel.component.ts:210) — a static attribute, not a property binding, so the DOM attribute stays.
findings.fix: Bind it as a property so no DOM attribute is rendered: `[title]="'desktop.appTitle'"` in the three call sites — or rename the input to `titleKey` to make the accident impossible.

findings.what: Seven native <select> elements remain outside the sc-select implementation; their OPEN state renders in the OS look (light popup inside the dark UI, no app tokens) — four of them on plain-viewer pages (settings language/region, friends report category, loadout share friend picker).
findings.evidence: src/app/settings/settings.component.ts:257 and :276 `<select class="sc-select"`; src/app/social/friends.component.ts:252 `<select class="sc-select"`; src/app/social/loadout-share-panel.component.ts:78 `<select id="share-friend-select" class="sc-select"`; src/app/admin/admin.component.ts:350 `<select class="sc-select" [value]="modDaysValue()"`; src/app/desktop/desktop-download.component.ts:81 `<select class="psel"`; src/app/desktop/channel-picker.component.ts:28 `<select [value]="channel()"`. The project's own component explains why native is wrong: src/app/shared/sc-select.component.ts:40. `.sc-select` is not a global class (no hit in src/styles.scss) — it is only component-local trigger styling.
findings.fix: Swap each for `<sc-select [options] [value] (valueChange)>` (same pattern as the hangar role/pin pickers from #669), starting with the four viewer-facing ones; keep the channel-picker/promote selects for a second step.

findings.what: Raw PostgREST / HTTP error messages and the untranslated literal 'Unknown error' reach the user-facing error cards of every codex core page (carry-over 'raw PostgREST messages in error cards' is still open).
findings.evidence: codex-detail.component.ts:2325 `this.error.set((err as Error).message ?? 'Unknown error')` rendered at :332 `{{ err }}`; :2388 `error: (e as Error).message ?? 'error'` rendered at :962 `{{ c.error }}`; codex-list.component.ts:1526; fps-list.component.ts:1292; blueprint-detail.component.ts:388 (rendered :47); keybinds.component.ts:857 and keybind-category.service.ts:91/147 (`err.message ?? 'Unknown error'` rendered at keybinds :291 `{{ cerr }}`); codex.service.ts:509 `buildError.set((err as Error).message ?? 'Unknown error')` → thrown by buildOrThrow :479 into every list; upcoming-ships.service.ts:459 → upcoming-grid.component.ts:54; upcoming-detail.component.ts:112 `{{ err }}` from hangar.error().
findings.fix: Add two keys (`codex.error.loadFailed`, `codex.error.unknown`) to public/i18n/{de,en}.json; in each catch set the signal to `t.instant('codex.error.loadFailed')` and `console.error('[codex] <op> failed', err)` instead of the raw message; keep the retry buttons as they are.

findings.what: Several controls on the feedback surfaces are far below the 44 px touch floor and get no coarse-pointer lift — including the only way to remove a queued attachment on a phone (a 15 px badge).
findings.evidence: src/app/admin/feedback/feedback-attachments.component.ts:349 `.att-row.dense .att-remove { width: 15px; height: 15px; }`, :426-427 `.att-remove { width: 18px; height: 18px }`, :490 `.lb-close … width: 32px; height: 32px`; src/app/admin/feedback/admin-feedback.component.ts:1058 `.search-clear { … min-width: 32px; min-height: 32px }`, :1247 `.read-more { … min-height: 32px }`. The same attachments file lifts `.lb-tool` to 48px (508) with a comment about the touch floor, so the rule is known.
findings.fix: Add `@media (pointer: coarse)` rules: give `.att-remove` a 44px hit area via `::before { content:''; position:absolute; inset:-13px }` (keep the 15/18px visual), and raise `.lb-close`, `.search-clear`, `.read-more` to `min-width/min-height: var(--sc-tap-min)`.

findings.what: The news error cards print the raw HttpErrorResponse text ("Http failure response for https://…supabase.co/functions/v1/fetch-verse-news: 0 Unknown Error") and offer no retry action — the carry-over item 'raw PostgREST messages in error cards' is still open for /news and /news/patches.
findings.evidence: src/app/news/news.service.ts:195 `this.error.set((err as Error).message ?? 'Unknown error');` src/app/news/news-list.component.ts:176-178 `{{ 'news.errorTitle' | translate }}: {{ err }}`; src/app/news/patch-board.component.ts:73 same. No `
findings.fix: Store a translated key instead of the transport message (e.g. `news.errorBody` = 'Bitte später erneut versuchen') plus a `news.retry` button on both cards that calls `svc.refresh()`; log the raw message via console.warn('[news] feed failed', err) instead of rendering it.

findings.what: Channel colours reuse reserved semantic tokens on a plain-viewer surface: the Spectrum pill on every news card/stage/detail is drawn in `--sc-accent-hot` (red = elevated access, RULE-C) and video tiles/badge/play disc use `--sc-danger` (reserved for errors/destructive actions).
findings.evidence: src/app/news/news-thumb.component.ts:483 `.ch-pill.ch-spectrum { color: var(--sc-accent-hot); border-color: var(--sc-accent-hot); }`, :484 `.ch-pill.ch-youtube { color: var(--sc-danger); … }`; src/app/news/news-list.component.ts:608-609 `.card.video { border-color: color-mix(in srgb, var(--sc-danger) 45%, …) }`, :617 play disc border, :642-643 `.vid-tag { color: var(--sc-danger) }`. src/styles.scss:31 documents `--sc-accent-hot, which means elevated access`; feedback 0a5268e7 asked videos to stay *distinct*, not for the danger token.

findings.what: The current build is read once per document and never re-validated: after a nightly ingest flips `is_current`, a long-open tab (desktop PWA) keeps treating the old build as live — the REQ-10 equip lock never engages because `viewingPastPatch()` compares two stale signals — and once `prune_codex_builds(2)` removes that build id, every Arsenal list, facet dropdown and rating silently shows nothing (no error, no retry).
findings.evidence: src/app/codex/codex.service.ts:456 `if (this.build()) return this.build();` (no refresh path, no visibilitychange/focus hook — grep found none); :502-503 `liveBuild` set only in fetchCurrentBuild; :604 listByKind returns `{ rows: [], count: 0 }` for a vanished build without touching buildError; live probe: `codex_facet_values` with an unknown uuid answers HTTP 200 `{"sizes": [], "grades": [], "manufacturers": [], "componentKinds": []}`; src/app/codex/fps-list.component.ts:349 `[disabled]="… || svc.viewingPastPatch()"`.
findings.fix: Re-read the `is_current` LIVE build id on `document.visibilitychange` (visible) and on the 30-min SwUpdate poll cadence; when it changed, update `liveBuild`, and when the active build id no longer exists, `selectBuild(null)` and raise the patch-headline notice so the lists reload on the live build.

findings.what: Ship hulls and livery icons have one host: when the R2 Worker 5xx's or hits its Free-plan 100k requests/day hard stop (error 1027), every Holotable hull and skin picker breaks until midnight UTC — the client never falls back to the Supabase bucket URL, and for ships committed in R2 mode the Supabase copy has already been deleted, so no second copy exists at all.
findings.evidence: src/app/codex/ship-skins.service.ts:31 `const BUCKET_PUBLIC = shipSkinsBase(environment.assets?.r2BaseUrl);` (build-time constant, one URL per asset); src/app/codex/holo/codex-holo-stage.component.ts:981 `img.onerror = () => {` → fallback ring only; src/app/codex/ship-skin-viewer.component.ts:155 `(error)="onModelError()"` → retry of the same URL; cloudflare/assets-worker/src/index.js:8-9 "HARD-STOPS at 100k requests/day (error 1027…)"; supabase/functions/ingest-skins/index.ts:302-303 `// Everything this ship still needs is in R2 now; the Supabase copy goes. keepPaths.clear();`.
findings.fix: Decide the second source: either `assetUrl` returns ordered candidates [R2, Supabase] and the viewer/stage fall through on error (covers not-yet-migrated ships only), or ingest-skins keeps the `standard` hull/icon in the Supabase bucket so an outage degrades to the default skin instead of a broken stage.

findings.what: Most modal dialogs neither trap Tab inside the dialog nor return focus to the opener on close; several also never move focus into the dialog, so a keyboard user Tabs into the page behind an `aria-modal="true"` overlay and lands nowhere after closing.
findings.evidence: grep -cE "keydown\.tab|key === 'Tab'|cdkTrapFocus|inert" per dialog file = 0 and grep -cE "returnFocus|activeElement|\.focus\(" = 0 for: src/app/desktop/desktop-download.component.ts:103 (`<div class="hx-dialog" role="dialog" aria-modal="true"`), src/app/desktop/uploader-access.component.ts:76, src/app/admin/api-tokens/api-tokens.component.ts:140 + :195, src/app/starscape/starscape.component.ts:335 (`<div class="lightbox" role="dialog" aria-modal="true"`), src/app/news/news-list.component.ts:320 (`nd-panel` — closeDetail() at ~1150 only disposes the overlay), src/app/news/patch-dossier.component.ts:113 (only `this.focus()` signal, no element focus), src/app/shell/quick-search.component.ts:74 (focuses `.qs-input` on open at :402, `close()` :407-415 restores nothing). Only codex-component-modal (:299 Tab loop), codex-weapon-detail (:182), codex-swap-picker (:695 returnFocus, :1266 Tab loop) and admin-feedback/feedback-attachments (`inert`) do it right.
findings.fix: Extract the Tab-loop + returnFocus logic already in src/app/codex/codex-component-modal.component.ts (:299-310) into a small `sc-focus-trap` directive (or use CDK `cdkTrapFocus` + `cdkTrapFocusAutoCapture`) and apply it to the eight `role="dialog" aria-modal="true"` panels listed; on close, `.focus()` the element saved from `document.activeElement` at open.

findings.what: Users see raw transport/PostgREST/GoTrue text in error cards: with the network down the codex list shows 'Could not load the codex: Failed to fetch', a statement timeout shows 'canceling statement due to statement timeout', the hangar banner and the sign-in form show the backend's English sentence verbatim. Carry-over item 'raw PostgREST messages in error cards' from the 2026-09-25 audit is still open.
findings.evidence: `this.error.set((err as Error).message ?? 'Unknown error')` at src/app/codex/codex-list.component.ts:1524, fps-list.component.ts:1275, keybinds.component.ts:832, codex-bridge.component.ts:615, codex-landing.component.ts:813, codex-detail.component.ts:2341, blueprint-detail.component.ts:387, news/news.service.ts:195, hangar/hangar.service.ts:243 (+20 write sites 339–1017 `this.error.set(error.message)`); rendered raw at codex-list.component.ts:311 `{{ err }}`, hangar-dashboard.component.ts:107 `{{ err | translate }}` (comment: 'raw backend messages pass through'), upcoming-detail.component.ts:111, news-list.component.ts:177, patch-board.component.ts:73, user-feedback-panel.component.ts:90 `@default { {{ err }} }`, login.component.ts:121/645/711, password-form.component.ts:113, set-password.component.ts:148, p4k.service.ts:57/73/87. The one correct pattern is starscape.component.ts:165-168 (translated `starscape.errors.timeout|load` + technical line).

findings.what: No timeout on any Supabase, Edge-Function or HttpClient call except the Starscape gallery: on a hung connection the hangar, every codex reader, the news feed and the admin invite/delete flows spin indefinitely with no error card and no retry offered.

findings.evidence: fetch-verse-news/index.ts:117 `await fetch(COMM_LINK_API, { headers: … })`; :356 `await fetch(YT_FEED_URL, …)`; :442-451 `fetch(SPECTRUM_API, { method: 'POST', …})` (no signal); :626-628 `fetch(STATUS_PAGE_URL, { headers: … })`; all joined at :1650 `await Promise.all([fetchCommLinks(), fetchYouTube(), fetchSpectrum(), fetchPatchNotes(), fetchStatus()])`. findings.fix: Add a `fetchWithTimeout(url, init, ms)` helper (AbortController, ~10 s) in fetch-verse-news/index.ts and use it at lines 117, 356, 442 and 626; the existing per-source try/catch then degrades that source to [] instead of hanging the feed.

findings.what: The silhouette build step shows raw i18n keys ("silhouettes.building", "silhouettes.buildFailed: …") in the run view because the four `silhouettes.*` keys exist in no dictionary and the `t(key) || fallback` pattern never falls back (t() returns the key itself when missing).
findings.evidence: data-uploader/src/renderer/main.ts:2481 `const label = t('silhouettes.building', {}) || 'Silhouetten werden gebaut';`, :2083 `t('silhouettes.buildFailed', {}) || 'Silhouetten übersprungen'`, :2495 `t('silhouettes.toolsFailed', {}) || …`, :2507 `t('silhouettes.hint', {}) ||`; src/lib/i18n.ts:53-56 `return interpolate(lookup(dict, key) ?? lookup(FALLBACK, key) ?? key, params)` (returns the key, which is truthy); key diff of src/i18n/en.json against renderer usage lists 'silhouettes.buildFailed', 'silhouettes.building', 'silhouettes.toolsFailed', 'silhouettes.hint' as missing; main.ts:2553 uses `tOr(...)` with a German-only fallback for every locale.

findings.what: The cgf-converter.exe build tool is downloaded from a third-party GitHub release and executed on the operator's machine with only a size floor as integrity check — no hash pin, no signature, no timeout — so a replaced release asset would run as the operator.
findings.evidence: data-uploader/src/main/skin-bridge.ts:23-25 `CGF_CONVERTER_URL = 'https://github.com/Markemp/Cryengine-Converter/releases/download/v2.0.0/cgf-converter.exe'` / `CGF_CONVERTER_MIN_BYTES = 100_000_000`; :86 `if (existsSync(dest) && statSync(dest).size >= CGF_CONVERTER_MIN_BYTES) return dest;`; :107-110 `if (statSync(tmp).size < CGF_CONVERTER_MIN_BYTES) throw …; renameSync(tmp, dest);` — grep for sha256/createHash/integrity in the file: 0 hits. The binary is then spawned by the Python sidecar (hull3d.py:210 `subprocess.run(cmd, …)`).
findings.fix: Pin the expected SHA-256 of the v2.0.0 asset as a constant in skin-bridge.ts, hash the stream while writing `.part` (node:crypto createHash) and refuse the rename on mismatch; verify the cached file once on first use per app version; add an AbortController timeout to the download.

findings.what: On Linux the mobile gate does not find Playwright's Chromium: `findBrowser()` ignores PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH / /opt/pw-browsers / ~/.cache/ms-playwright, so in this container `--skip-if-unavailable` prints 'no Chrome/Edge binary in this environment' and exits 0 although a Chromium is installed, and a plain run exits 2.
findings.evidence: scripts/mobile-gate.mjs:168-184 — `const explicit = process.env.MOBILE_GATE_CHROME || process.env.CHROME_BIN || process.env.CHROME_PATH;` then a fixed list ending `'/usr/bin/google-chrome', '/usr/bin/chromium', '/usr/bin/chromium-browser'`. Measured on this box: `PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH=/opt/pw-browsers`, `/opt/pw-browsers/chromium-1194/chrome-linux/chrome` exists, CHROME_BIN unset; `node scripts/mobile-gate.mjs --selftest --skip-if-unavailable` → `[mobile-gate] SKIPPED — no Chrome/Edge binary in this environment` exit=0. docs/mobile-gate.md:69-70 says 'auto-discovered; override with CHROME_BIN or MOBILE_GATE_CHROME' (CHROME_PATH, which the code reads, is undocumented).
findings.fix: In findBrowser() add candidates from `process.env.PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH` and `~/.cache/ms-playwright` (glob `chromium-*/chrome-linux/chrome`, `chromium_headless_shell-*/chrome-linux/headless_shell`), plus `/usr/bin/google-chrome-stable`; mention Playwright browsers and CHROME_PATH in docs/mobile-gate.md 'Requirements'.

findings.what: Even with CHROME_BIN set, the mobile gate cannot launch Chromium as root on Linux: it never passes `--no-sandbox`, Chrome aborts immediately, and the gate waits 30 s then exits 2 'Browser did not expose a DevTools port'.
findings.evidence: scripts/mobile-gate.mjs:195-209 — flags list `'--remote-debugging-port=0', `--user-data-dir=…`, '--no-first-run', … 'about:blank'` with `if (headless) flags.unshift('--headless=new', '--disable-gpu')`; no sandbox flag. Measured: `CHROME_BIN=/opt/pw-browsers/chromium-1194/chrome-linux/chrome node scripts/mobile-gate.mjs --selftest` → `[mobile-gate] Browser did not expose a DevTools port within 30s.` exit=2; the binary's own stderr with the gate's flags: `ERROR:…zygote_host_impl_linux.cc:101] Running as root without --no-sandbox is not supported`; the same command plus `--no-sandbox` wrote DevToolsActivePort within 6 s.
findings.fix: In launchBrowser() add `--no-sandbox` when `process.platform === 'linux' && process.getuid?.() === 0` (or when MOBILE_GATE_NO_SANDBOX=1), and surface Chrome's stderr in the 'did not expose a DevTools port' failure (spawn with stdio ['ignore','ignore','pipe'] and print the last lines) so the next launch failure is diagnosable.

findings.what: 56 of 145 app tooltips sit on non-focusable hosts (span/div/li/td/i), so their content is reachable only by hover or long-press — never by keyboard — and the `aria-describedby` the directive sets on a plain span is not announced by screen readers.
findings.evidence: grep -rnoE '<(span|div|li|svg|td|dd|…)\b[^>]*\[?scTooltip\]?=' src/app → span 46, div 7, li 1, td 1, i 1; none has tabindex (`grep -rnE '<span\b[^>]*scTooltip[^>]*tabindex' → 0`). Samples carrying information not otherwise visible: src/app/admin/feedback/admin-feedback.component.ts:298 `<span class="dot hot" [scTooltip]="'adminFeedback.sourceFilter.untriagedHint' | translate"`, :567 `<span class="ch-time" [scTooltip]="waitingSinceIso(m) | scDate: 'datetime'"`, :603 `<span class="av" role="img" … [scTooltip]="roleTitle(a)"`, src/app/admin/admin.component.ts:306 `<span class="tip-wrap" [scTooltip]="moderationLockReason(f.user)"`, src/app/desktop/app-download-panel.component.ts:58 `<span class="ap-ver" [scTooltip]=…`. Directive: src/app/shared/tooltip/sc-tooltip.directive.ts:174 opens on `focusin` only.
findings.fix: Triage the 56 hosts: where the tooltip is the only place the information lives, add `tabindex="0"` plus a role (`img`/`note`) and an `aria-label` with the same text (as codex-set-stage.component.ts:117-119 already does), or render it as visible/`sr-only` text; where it merely repeats visible text, drop the tooltip (REQ-8).

findings.what: The ingest-side `is_variant` heuristic flags class names ending in `_Renegade` as non-buyable, which hides the Aegis Avenger Titan Renegade (a real pledge-store ship) from every Arsenal list, the ship facets and the search counts in the live build.

findings.what: When the Supabase fallback fails, the Worker either crashes to a CORS-less 500 (fetch throws) or reports a 5xx/429 outage as a plain 404; Range requests on a Supabase-backed key get a full 200 body; a Supabase 304 is relayed without its ETag.
findings.evidence: cloudflare/assets-worker/src/index.js:63-80 — `const res = await fetch(upstream, { method: request.method, headers: request.headers.get('if-none-match') ? {...} : {} });` (no try/catch, Range not forwarded) … `if (res.status === 304) return new Response(null, { status: 304, headers: baseHeaders(key) });` (no etag) … `if (!res.ok) return plain(404, 'not found');` (any upstream status). test/index.test.mjs:101-105 only covers upstream 400 → 404.
findings.fix: Wrap the upstream fetch in try/catch and answer 502 with the CORS headers on a throw or on an upstream 5xx/429 (keep 404 only for upstream 404/400); forward the `range` header and relay 206 + content-range/content-length; set `etag` on the relayed 304. Add node tests for the throw and the 5xx path.

findings.what: 13 edge-function test files (113 tests) have no runner: no npm script, no CI step and no documented `deno test` invocation reference them, so they can rot unnoticed.

findings.what: Destructive and fork confirmations use the browser's window.confirm()/window.prompt() (OS-look dialog, untranslated buttons, blocks the tab); a plain viewer meets it when editing a followed loadout on the Holotable and when deleting the account. findings.evidence: Viewer-facing: src/app/codex/holo/codex-holo-fork-guard.ts:45 `if (!window.confirm(question)) return 'cancelled';`, src/app/settings/settings.component.ts:1340 `if (!window.confirm(msg)) return;`. Admin/collaborator: src/app/admin/api-tokens/api-tokens.component.ts:618, src/app/admin/feedback/admin-feedback.component.ts:2660, src/app/admin/admin.component.ts:1523,1661,1678, src/app/p4k/p4k-history.component.ts:458 (`window.prompt`),465,471. The app already avoids it where it matters: src/app/social/friends.component.ts:244 comment "a one-line native confirm() cannot carry" a reason and builds an in-app form.

findings.what: The api function's `last_used_at` touch and the `api_request_log` insert the rate limiter counts on are fire-and-forget without `EdgeRuntime.waitUntil`; if the runtime drops pending work once the Response is returned, the limiter silently under-counts and fails open, and token usage never updates. fetch-verse-news already uses waitUntil for exactly this reason.
findings.evidence: api/_auth.ts:176-180 `ctx.supabase.from('api_tokens').update({ last_used_at: … }).eq('id', ctx.token.id).then(() => null);` (comment: "We deliberately don't await"); api/_rate-limit.ts:302-310 `ctx.supabase.from('api_request_log').insert({…}).then(() => null); return response;` while :272-276 counts that table. Precedent: fetch-verse-news/index.ts:1641-1644 `EdgeRuntime?.waitUntil?.(p)` "keeps the isolate alive until the promise settles".
findings.fix: Wrap both promises in `(globalThis as any).EdgeRuntime?.waitUntil?.(p)` (falling back to a plain await when the global is absent), or simply `await` the request-log insert before returning the response.

findings.what: codex-list and fps-list are ~150 literal lines and 50 members apart from being one list shell; the card markup is written twice.

findings.what: Full-height layouts use `100vh`; on phones the mobile browser toolbar overlaps that height, so the patch dossier's phone sheet (`height: 100vh`) hides its last rows behind Safari's bar and the feedback panels size against the wrong viewport. Three files already use `100dvh` as the precedent.
findings.evidence: src/app/news/patch-dossier.component.ts:564 `.panel { max-height: 100vh; height: 100vh; border-radius: 0; }` (phone breakpoint); src/app/shell/user-feedback-fab.component.ts:200 `height: min(600px, calc(100vh - 120px))` and :205; src/app/shell/feedback-fab.component.ts:216, :222; src/app/shell/shell.component.ts:326 `:host { … min-height: 100vh; }`; src/app/shell/public-layout.component.ts:51; src/app/app.component.ts:51; src/app/codex/holo/codex-holo-stage.component.ts:663 sticky top calc. dvh precedent: src/app/admin/concepts/concept-page.component.ts:71 `min-height: calc(100dvh - 4rem)`.
findings.fix: Replace `100vh` with `100dvh` in the nine declarations (R6 fix policy: mechanical); keep `100vh` only where a fallback line precedes it.

findings.what: Bottom-anchored fixed bars ignore the iOS home-indicator inset: on phones the Holotable strip (the page's main control bar at ≤640px), its expanded panel, the undo toast and the shell's nav-scan label sit in the safe-area zone. The FABs and the energy dock already add env(safe-area-inset-bottom).
findings.evidence: src/app/codex/holo/codex-holo-strip.component.ts:475 `.holo-strip { position: fixed; inset-inline: 0; inset-block-end: 0; … }` and :486 `.hs-panel { position: fixed; inset-inline: 0; inset-block-end: 0; …}`; src/app/codex/holo/codex-holo-stage.component.ts:682 `.undo-toast { position: fixed; bottom: calc(var(--holo-strip-h, 64px) + 16px); …}`; src/app/shell/shell.component.ts:440 `.nav-scan__label { position: fixed; bottom: 24px; …}`. Precedent: src/app/codex/codex-energy-dock.component.ts:887 `padding-block-end: env(safe-area-inset-bottom)`, src/app/shell/feedback-fab.component.ts:303. Viewport is `viewport-fit=cover` (src/index.html:7), so the inset is real.
