findings.what: Text below the 12 px readability floor is rendered on touch devices in the set/stage/holo pages because these rules bypass the `max(…, var(--sc-fs-floor))` guard; radar and gauge captions render at ~5–7 px on a phone.
findings.evidence: src/app/codex/set/codex-set-rank-card.component.ts:184 `.radar text { font-size: 6px }` (viewBox 200 at max-width 210px ≈ 6.3px); src/app/codex/codex-rank-card.component.ts:277 `font-size: 6px`, :350 `7px`; src/app/codex/holo/codex-holo-perspectives.component.ts:169 `.gauge text.l { font-size: 6px }`, :152/156 `11px`, :175 `10.5px`; src/app/codex/holo/codex-holo-strip.component.ts:441 `.hp-cooling text.l { font-size: 5.5px }`, :374/447 `10px`, :411 `9px`; src/app/codex/ship-hardpoint-map.component.ts:135 `.nose { font-size: 5px }`; src/app/codex/stage/codex-stage.component.ts:194 `font-size: 10px` (eyebrow), :277 `9px` (archive line); src/app/codex/stage/hangar-picker.component.ts:135 `font: 600 9px/1 …`, :142 `8px`, :167 `9px/28px`; src/app/codex/codex-landing.component.ts:510,520 `font-size: 9px`; src/app/codex/holo/codex-holo-stage.component.ts:525 `kbd … 10px`, :550 `11px`; src/app/codex/holo/codex-holo-table.component.ts:264 `10px`, :306 `9px`; src/app/codex/holo/codex-holo-inspector.component.ts:186 `10px`, :228 `9.5px`; src/app/codex/codex-kpi-band.component.ts:106 `10px`; src/app/codex/codex-swap-picker.component.ts:523,525,593,599,602,605 `11px`. styles.scss:334 sets `--sc-fs-floor: 12px` under `(pointer: coarse)`, docs/mobile-gate.md:110 `text-too-small | font-size < 12px`.
findings.fix: Wrap each literal in `max(<px>, var(--sc-fs-floor))`; for the SVG captions (radar axes, gauge labels, map nose) either enlarge the viewBox text or replace them with HTML labels outside the SVG on coarse pointers, since a 12 px caption in a 200-unit radar collides with its neighbours.

findings.what: A transport error while loading note outlines marks every slug of that batch as permanently `missing` for the lifetime of the SPA (the service is root-scoped, not per visit as the comment says); the 'load the rest' button then disappears and the notes can never be searched or expanded without a full reload.
findings.evidence: src/app/news/roadmap.service.ts:206-213 `catch { // … mark them missing for THIS visit … this.missing.update(…add every slug)` inside `@Injectable({ providedIn: 'root' })` (:64); src/app/news/patch-board.component.ts:522 `!this.roadmap.hasOutline(slug) && !this.roadmap.isMissing(slug)` hides the button; patch-note-detail.component.ts:673 renders 'unavailable' with no retry.
findings.fix: Keep a separate `failed` set with an attempt counter (max 2) instead of writing transport failures into `missing`; let `requestOutlines` re-enqueue a failed slug on the next explicit call (the 'load rest' button / row expand) and only file it as missing after the second failure.

findings.what: The Verse-News feed (a plain-viewer surface) paints YouTube videos in --sc-danger and the Spectrum channel pill in --sc-accent-hot as brand/channel colours — red that means neither error/destructive nor elevated access.
findings.evidence: src/app/news/news-list.component.ts:608 `.card.video { border-color: color-mix(in srgb, var(--sc-danger) 45%, …) }`, :609, :617 `.play … var(--sc-danger)`, :642-643 `.vid-tag … color: var(--sc-danger)`, :798 `.play-link:hover … background: var(--sc-danger)`; src/app/news/news-thumb.component.ts:483 `.ch-pill.ch-spectrum { color: var(--sc-accent-hot) …}`, :484 `.ch-pill.ch-youtube { color: var(--sc-danger) …}`.
findings.fix: Add channel tokens in src/styles.scss next to --sc-offense (e.g. `--sc-ch-video` and `--sc-ch-spectrum`, distinct hues that are not the danger/hot aliases) and reference them in news-list.component.ts and news-thumb.component.ts instead of --sc-danger / --sc-accent-hot.

findings.what: Runtime errors in production reach nobody: there is no custom ErrorHandler, no `unhandledrejection`/`window.onerror` sink and PostHog exception capture is off, so a thrown error in a signed-in flow is only visible in the user's own devtools console.
findings.evidence: src/app/app.config.ts providers list has no `{ provide: ErrorHandler … }` (`grep -rn 'ErrorHandler' src/app` → only set-arsenal-transition.ts:1/35 injecting the default); `grep -rn 'unhandledrejection\|window.onerror' src/` → 0; src/main.ts:12 `bootstrapApplication(...).catch((err) => console.error(err))` is the only global catch; src/app/core/analytics.service.ts:130-139 `posthog.init` has no `capture_exceptions` (`grep -rn 'capture_exceptions\|captureException\|\$exception' src/app` → 0).
findings.fix: Add `src/app/core/app-error-handler.ts` (extends Angular ErrorHandler: logs `[app] unhandled` with route + error, and — only when `consent.statisticsAllowed()` — forwards a redacted `$exception` event through AnalyticsService, which already runs with `person_profiles: 'never'`); register it in app.config.ts. Zone.js already routes unhandled promise rejections into ErrorHandler, so one class covers both.

findings.what: With R2 secrets present, any failure to read Cloudflare usage (missing token, Analytics API error or its rate limit — each edge isolate caches for only 5 min) answers 503 for every `sign`, and the uploader has no Supabase fallback: a whole skins run ends with one "sign failed" line per ship and zero ships published, with no single operator-facing signal.
findings.evidence: supabase/functions/ingest-skins/index.ts:184-190 `catch (e) { return json({ error: 'r2_usage_unknown', … }, 503); }`; supabase/functions/ingest-skins/_r2.ts:134-135 `USAGE_TTL_MS = 5 * 60 * 1000; let usageCache` (module-level, per isolate) and :144 `throw new Error('CF_ANALYTICS_TOKEN is not set')`; data-uploader/src/main/skin-ingest.ts:198-199 `onLog(`${shipId}: sign failed — ${signed.error}`, 'error'); out.push({ ok: false, … })` — continues to the next ship.
findings.fix: Uploader: abort the run on the first 503 `r2_usage_unknown` / 507 with one clear message naming the gate; function: accept a cached reading up to 24 h old when the Analytics call errors (still fail closed with no reading at all).

findings.what: Settings offers "Delete account" to every signed-in user, but the delete-user edge function refuses everyone who is not an admin — a viewer confirms the native dialog and gets a raw "forbidden" line; self-deletion never works for the users the privacy page promises it to.
findings.evidence: src/app/settings/settings.component.ts:404-416 renders the danger-zone button with no role condition (`grep isAdmin` → only the role pill at :143); :1343 `functions.invoke('delete-user', { body: { userId: user.id } })`; supabase/functions/delete-user/index.ts:72-74 `if (callerProfile?.role !== 'admin') { return json({ error: 'forbidden' }, 403); }`; settings.component.ts:1353-1358 then shows `payload.error` ("forbidden") verbatim; src/app/legal/privacy.component.ts:1228 comment: "deletion → supabase/functions/delete-user (admin-gated today)".
findings.fix: Either let delete-user accept `userId === user.id` for non-admins (keeping last-admin/protected checks) or hide the danger-zone card for non-admins and replace it with a localized "contact us to delete" line; in both cases map `forbidden`/`invalid_body` to i18n keys instead of printing the code.

findings.what: No CI runs the web app's unit tests, typecheck or mobile gate — the 226 spec files and the RULE-H gate are enforced only by hand on the developer machine; a red suite can merge to main and deploy.
findings.evidence: .github/workflows/*.yml: all five workflows are path-filtered to satellites (browser-extension/**, data-uploader/**, supabase/functions/**, docs/readme-io/**, wallpaper-app/**); `grep -rn "npm test\|typecheck\|ng test" .github/workflows` hits only data-uploader-build.yml:31-32 (`npm run typecheck` / `npm test` inside data-uploader). scripts/vercel-build.sh:26-30 runs only `npm run prebuild`, the exit guard and `npm run postbuild`. docs/feedback-routine.md:189 prescribes `npm run typecheck && npm run build && npm test` as a manual step. `find src -name '*.spec.ts' | wc -l` = 226.
findings.fix: Add `.github/workflows/web-ci.yml` (on push to main + pull_request, paths src/**, public/**, package*.json, angular.json, tsconfig*.json, ngsw-config.json, scripts/**) with actions/setup-node 24, `npm ci`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm test`, `npm run test:gate`, `npm run test:assets-worker`; `permissions: contents: read`.

findings.what: database.types.ts is five days stale and not load-bearing: it lacks 81 of 96 migration functions (incl. all three spot-checked RPCs) and the Supabase client is created untyped.
findings.evidence: src/app/core/database.types.ts header: 'AUTO-GENERATED by `supabase gen types typescript` (via Supabase MCP) … regenerate after migrations'; last regenerated in 8696869 (#640, 2026-09-21); holds 26 tables / 15 functions vs 57 tables / 96 functions created in supabase/migrations; codex_facet_values, codex_armor_rating, prune_codex_builds: 0 hits (migrations 20260926120000, 20260926140000/150000, 20260925010000); 36 of 49 RPC names used via .rpc('…') in src/app and 19 of 33 table names used via .from('…') are absent (e.g. admin_feedback, hangar_share_links, codex_silhouettes, get_telemetry_stats, adopt_shared_loadout); src/app/core/supabase.client.ts:38 and :67 call `createClient(` without `<Database>`; hangar.service.ts:502 comments 'profiles.flagship_ship_class postdates the generated database.types'; only codex.types.ts:15 and hangar.types.ts:8 consume `Tables<>`; no npm script regenerates it (grep package.json: none).
findings.fix: Add `"db:types": "supabase gen types typescript --project-id hcnqhvzlavdycidqyaai --schema public > src/app/core/database.types.ts"` to package.json and run it after every migration (document in .claude/deep-knowledge/supabase.md); then type the client `createClient<Database>(…)` so missing tables/RPCs fail typecheck. Regeneration needs Supabase access (MCP auth was rejected in this run).

findings.what: The service worker never caches the translation tables (188 kB de.json / 177 kB en.json), the meshopt decoder or release-notes.json: every cold start fetches i18n over the network and an offline PWA start renders raw keys.
findings.evidence: ngsw-config.json assetGroups cover only `/favicon.ico, /index.html, /manifest.webmanifest, /*.css, /*.js` (app) and `/icons/**, /assets/**, /*.(svg|…)` (assets) — no `/i18n/**`, `/meshopt/**` or `/release-notes.json`; there is no `public/assets/` folder at all (ls public → .well-known, favicon.ico, humans.txt, i18n, icons, img, manifest.webmanifest, meshopt, release-notes.json, robots.txt, sitemap.xml). Loader: src/app/app.config.ts `provideTranslateHttpLoader({ prefix: 'i18n/', suffix: '.json' })`. Sizes: public/i18n/de.json 188 666 B, en.json 177 054 B, release-notes.json 418 836 B.
findings.fix: In ngsw-config.json replace the dead `/assets/**` entry with `/i18n/**`, `/meshopt/**` and `/release-notes.json` in the `assets` group (installMode lazy, updateMode prefetch) so they are hash-versioned and served from cache after first use; keep dataGroups unchanged.

findings.what: ingest-skins has no `[functions.ingest-skins]` block in config.toml, so its platform JWT gate is whatever the last deploy left; live it is ON (unauthenticated POST → gateway `UNAUTHORIZED_NO_AUTH_HEADER`), while its siblings ingest-bundle/ingest-catalog are documented as REQUIRING the gate OFF because it rejected the uploader's session token (CHANGELOG 0.17.1). Either skin uploads fail at the gateway for the data-uploader (REQ-36 broken) or the config.toml rationale for ingest-bundle/ingest-catalog is stale — the file that is supposed to be the source of truth says nothing for this function.
findings.evidence: supabase/config.toml: blocks exist for 16 functions, none for ingest-skins (grep `functions.ingest-skins` → 0). Live: `curl -X POST …/functions/v1/ingest-skins` → 401 {"code":"UNAUTHORIZED_NO_AUTH_HEADER"} vs ingest-bundle → 401 {"error":"unauthorized"} (function body). config.toml:64-73 (ingest-catalog): "`supabase functions deploy` … defaults verify_jwt to TRUE when a function has no block, silently re-enabling the gate". ingest-skins/index.ts:3-4 "Same auth shape as ingest-bundle (user JWT + release-token + admin/collaborator role)"; data-uploader/src/main/skin-ingest.ts:96-101 sends `authorization: Bearer <session access token>`.
findings.fix: Add a `[functions.ingest-skins]` block to supabase/config.toml with `verify_jwt = false` and the same rationale as ingest-bundle (the body already does getUser + role + release-token), then redeploy; or, if the gateway now accepts asymmetric session tokens, add the block with `verify_jwt = true` and rewrite the ingest-bundle/ingest-catalog comments so the file stops claiming the gate breaks uploads.

findings.what: The public OpenAPI spec and the /docs embed snippet point every generated client at `https://sc-companion.vercel.app`, which serves the Angular index.html for /openapi.json and /v1/* (verified live); the readme.io docs correctly use the Supabase functions URL, so integrators get two contradicting base URLs and the spec-driven one returns HTML 200.
findings.evidence: api/openapi.ts:22-24 `servers: [{ url: 'https://sc-companion.vercel.app', description: 'Production' }]`; api/docs.ts:89 `data-url="https://sc-companion.vercel.app/openapi.json"`. Live: `curl https://sc-companion.vercel.app/openapi.json` → 200 text/html `<!doctype html>…`; `/v1/patch` → 200 text/html. vercel.json rewrites: only /ingest/* and `/(.*) → /index.html`. readme-sync/content.ts:148 uses `https://hcnqhvzlavdycidqyaai.supabase.co/functions/v1/api`.
findings.fix: In api/openapi.ts set `servers[0].url` to `https://hcnqhvzlavdycidqyaai.supabase.co/functions/v1/api` and in api/docs.ts point the embed snippet's `data-url` at `…/functions/v1/api/openapi.json` (or add Vercel rewrites for /openapi.json and /v1/* to the function).

findings.what: starscape-summary caches a FAILED resvg wasm download forever: `wasmReady` keeps the rejected promise, so after one CDN hiccup every render on that isolate fails until restart, and the terminal fallback answers HTTP 200 with a plain-text body and no Content-Type, so the wallpaper app receives a 'successful' non-PNG. The wasm fetch also has no timeout.
findings.evidence: starscape-summary/index.ts:94-105 `let wasmReady … if (!wasmReady) { wasmReady = fetch(RESVG_WASM_URL).then(…).then((buf) => initWasm(buf)); } return wasmReady;` (never reset on rejection); :364-367 `catch (fallbackErr) { … return new Response('starscape-summary unavailable', { status: 200, headers: CORS_HEADERS }); }`.
findings.fix: In ensureWasm() attach `.catch((e) => { wasmReady = null; throw e; })` and pass `AbortSignal.timeout(10_000)` to the fetch; in the final catch return status 503 with `Retry-After: 60` and `Content-Type: text/plain` so the client retries instead of using the text as an image.

findings.what: No edge-function test ever runs in CI: the 13 Deno `*.test.ts` files (concept-page, fetch-verse-news ×7, patch-stability-sample, rsi-roadmap ×2, ship-link) have no `deno test` step in any workflow, and `npm run test:assets-worker` — the only runner of `_r2-usage.test.mjs`, which REQ-29 names as its acceptance signal — is not invoked by any workflow, hook or gate script. The R2 cost guard can regress without a red build.
findings.evidence: `grep -rn "deno test\|test:assets-worker\|_r2-usage.test\|node --test" .github/ scripts/ .husky/ .claude/hooks/ package.json` → only package.json:24 defines the script; workflows call `npm run check:edge-functions` (edge-functions-deploy.yml:69), `npm test` only in data-uploader-build.yml:34 (uploader). `node --test supabase/functions/ingest-skins/_r2-usage.test.mjs` → 8/8 pass locally, so the tests are green but unenforced.
findings.fix: Add to the `plan` job of .github/workflows/edge-functions-deploy.yml (and to the PR path) two steps: `npm run test:assets-worker` and a `deno test --allow-none supabase/functions` step via denoland/setup-deno, so a failing guard test blocks the deploy.

findings.what: Deleting a collaborator account who ever re-uploaded a build fails with a foreign-key violation: p4k_bundles.disabled_by references auth.users with no ON DELETE clause, and every supersede writes disabled_by = uploader.
findings.evidence: supabase/migrations/00005_phase2_diff_disable_build.sql:11 `add column if not exists disabled_by uuid references auth.users(id),` (only FK to auth.users without an on-delete action in the whole schema — grep); 20260707120000_bundle_superseded_at.sql:431-432 `disabled_by = p_uploader, disabled_at = now(), superseded_at = now()` inside ingest_bundle_atomic; delete-user surfaces it as 500: supabase/functions/delete-user/index.ts:142-144 `deleteUser(userId) … return json({ error: 'delete_failed' …}, 500)`.
findings.fix: New migration: drop the auto-named FK on p4k_bundles.disabled_by and re-add it as `references auth.users(id) on delete set null` (column is already nullable).

findings.what: codex.service.ts is a 2 301-line single @Injectable that bundles seven unrelated data domains and hosts the types that create a 6-file import cycle.
findings.evidence: src/app/codex/codex.service.ts: 1 @Injectable, 186 members; domains: builds/lists (fetchCurrentBuild 484, listByKind 597, countSearchMatches 660), FPS catalog (weaponFacets 848, listFpsCatalog 895, 86 lines), silhouettes (silhouette 1115, silhouettes 1151), rank cohort (getRankCohort 1477, cohortOccupantsFor 1569), keybinds (listKeybinds 1686), blueprints (1808–2096: fetchBlueprintCategories, listBlueprints, getBlueprint, getCraftingRecipe, blueprintsUsingIngredient 1961 = 135 lines), locale (resolveLocaleKeys 1650); config constants 249–353 (PAGE_SIZE, SEARCH_LIMIT, FPS_CATALOG_HARD_CAP, CATEGORY_PAGE_SIZE, KEYBIND_PAGE_SIZE, WEAPON_FACET_HARD_CAP). Types CodexKind :49, CodexListRow :70, LocalizedText declared here and imported back by stock-loadout.ts:15, codex-edition-group.ts:1, codex-skin-group.ts:1, codex-build-diff.ts:14, codex-poly-search.ts:12 (SCC of 6 files).
findings.fix: Split by domain into codex-blueprint.service.ts (1808–2096), codex-fps-catalog.service.ts (848–980), codex-silhouette.service.ts (1115–1220), codex-rank-cohort.service.ts (1477–1616) and keep CodexService for builds/lists/search; move CodexKind, CodexListRow, LocalizedText, CodexListFilters to codex.types.ts.

findings.what: A detail page whose hardpoint or strings query fails renders as if the entity had no ports (empty loadout/hardpoint sections, no error, no retry) — partial failure is indistinguishable from complete data.
findings.evidence: src/app/codex/codex.service.ts:1017-1053 `fetchDetailForBuild`: `Promise.all([rowRes, portsRes, stringsRes])`, then only `if (rowRes.error) throw rowRes.error;` — `portsRes.error` and `stringsRes.error` are never read; :1048 `ports: ((portsRes.data ?? []) as unknown[])…`. codex-detail's error card + retry (:330-336) therefore never appears for this failure mode.
findings.fix: In fetchDetailForBuild add `if (portsRes.error) throw portsRes.error; if (stringsRes.error) throw stringsRes.error;` after the row check so the existing error card and retry cover the ports/strings reads too (extend the getDetail spec with a failing ports response).

findings.what: Pin and config activation are two unguarded sequential updates with no server-side uniqueness for pins: two devices pinning different ships to rank 1 (each with a stale cache) leave two ships on rank 1 permanently; for configs the partial unique index turns the second device's activation into a raw 23505 in the hangar banner.
findings.evidence: src/app/hangar/hangar.service.ts:411-431 `const occupant = this.ships().find((s) => s.pinnedRank === rank …)` then two `.update()` calls; :671-689 activateConfig clears then sets; supabase/migrations/20260613000000_hangar.sql:39 `pinned_rank int check (pinned_rank between 1 and 3),` — no unique index on (user_id, pinned_rank).
findings.fix: Migration: `create unique index hangar_ships_one_per_rank on public.hangar_ships (user_id, pinned_rank) where pinned_rank is not null;` and in `pinShip`/`activateConfig` treat 23505 as "reload ships/configs and retry once" instead of surfacing the PostgREST text.

findings.what: No CI job tests the web app: none of the five workflows runs `npm test`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run build` or the mobile gate for `src/`, so the Karma suite and the responsive gate run only when someone runs `/ship` locally; auth-gated routes are gated only on a machine that has the test-account credential.
findings.evidence: `ls .github/workflows` → browser-extension-build.yml, data-uploader-build.yml, edge-functions-deploy.yml, readme-docs-sync.yml, wallpaper-app-build.yml; `grep -l "npm test\|ng test\|gate:mobile" .github/workflows/*.yml` → only data-uploader-build.yml (:190 `npm run typecheck` for the uploader); vercel.json:3 builds via `scripts/vercel-build.sh` which runs prebuild/build/postbuild only.
findings.fix: Add `.github/workflows/web-ci.yml` on pull_request/push to main: `npm ci`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm test`, `npm run build`, `npm run gate:mobile -- --skip-if-unavailable`, and `gate:mobile:auth` when the `SC_TEST_*` secrets are present.

findings.what: The nightly retention job ranks builds purely by `created_at`, so an ingest that is still running at 03:30 UTC — or one that was abandoned before `finalize` — counts as one of the two kept builds and the previous LIVE build (the inline diff's "previous", the Holotable picker's older patch) is deleted while the new one is incomplete; an abandoned build then stays listed as a patch "with data".
findings.evidence: supabase/migrations/20260925010000_codex_build_retention.sql:47-56 `row_number() over (partition by b.channel order by b.created_at desc) … where … r.rn > p_keep and not r.is_current` — no age or `entity_counts is not null` condition; src/app/codex/codex-patch-timeline.ts:79-81 every build row gets `hasData: true`.
findings.fix: In `prune_codex_builds`, rank only rows with `entity_counts is not null` (set by finalize) or `created_at < now() - interval '24 hours'`, and delete non-current rows older than 7 days that never got `entity_counts` as abandoned.

findings.what: ingest-telemetry falls back to a hard-coded dev HMAC key (and dev hash salt) when the secrets are unset — the same literal is compiled into the data-uploader's dev/test builds — so a missing `TELEMETRY_HMAC_KEY` in the project turns the only authentication of this verify_jwt=false endpoint into a public string and lets anyone insert telemetry rows with the service role, with no log line saying the fallback is active.
findings.evidence: ingest-telemetry/index.ts:46 `const HMAC_KEY = Deno.env.get('TELEMETRY_HMAC_KEY') ?? 'scc-telemetry-dev-key-v1';` :47 `const HASH_SALT = Deno.env.get('TELEMETRY_HASH_SALT') ?? 'scc-telemetry-salt-v1';` data-uploader/vitest.config.ts:19 `__SC_TELEMETRY_HMAC_KEY__: JSON.stringify('scc-telemetry-dev-key-v1')`.
findings.fix: Fail closed: if `TELEMETRY_HMAC_KEY` (or the salt) is missing, return 503 `server_misconfigured` (log once) unless an explicit `TELEMETRY_DEV=1` env opts into the dev key; operator verifies the secret exists on the project (`supabase secrets list`).

findings.what: Feedback screenshots (a viewport capture that can include the settings page with e-mail and user id) are stored in the PUBLIC `feedback-images` bucket and referenced by permanent unauthenticated public URLs; only the UUID in the path protects them.
findings.evidence: src/app/feedback/feedback-images.util.ts:986-990 `const path = \`${uid}/${crypto.randomUUID()}.${ext}\`` … `urls.push(bucket.getPublicUrl(path).data.publicUrl)`; supabase/migrations/20260713000000_feedback_images_bucket.sql:27 "Public read of feedback-images objects (anon + authenticated)"; src/app/feedback/page-screenshot.service.ts:751 captures `doc.body` minus only the feedback UI (:814-817).
findings.fix: Make the bucket private and hand out `createSignedUrl` (e.g. 1 h) at render time in `sc-feedback-attachments` / the admin board, storing the object path in the body instead of the public URL; add an RLS read policy limited to the author and admins.

findings.what: codex-detail.component.ts is a 4,560-line god component whose template repeats ~280 lines verbatim between the classic branch and the Holotable branch (carry-over 'component size codex-detail 4.7k lines' not applied).
findings.evidence: Sizes: template 299–1467 (1,168 lines), styles 1468–1848 (380 lines, ~18.0 kB minified), class 1849–4560 with 86 methods; `load()` 2254–2345 (92 lines) resets 31 signals by hand; `resolveShipTech` 2419–2478 (60), `openInspect` 4205–4259 (55), `saveLoadoutDraft` 3047–3098 (52). Verbatim duplicates (grep of class/heading markers): skin picker 410–428, 534–552, 1188–1206 (×3, 19 lines each); edition picker 434–452, 513–531, 1167–1185 (×3); ship-link form 588–636 and 1232–1280 (×2, 49 lines); tail loadout card 793–815 and 1283–1305; description 819–823 and 1307–1311; recipe 1001–1028 and 1312–1339; hardpoints 931–998 and 1341–1405 (~66 lines); spec/raw block 1053–1085 and 1407–1439.
findings.fix: Move each repeated block into an `<ng-template #skinPicker>` / `#editionPicker` / `#shipLinkForm` / `#tailLoadout` / `#description` / `#recipe` / `#hardpoints` / `#specRaw` rendered via `ngTemplateOutlet` from both branches (DOM and bindings unchanged, existing specs stay green); as a second step extract the ship-link form and the hardpoint/compat list into their own components.

findings.what: `CodexService.armorRating` (RPC call, per-build cache, null on error) has no service-level spec; only the page spec covers the null path through a mocked service.
findings.evidence: grep `armorRating|codex_armor_rating` in src/app/codex/codex.service.spec.ts → 0 hits, while `facetValues` has its own describe ('CodexService.facetValues', codex.service.spec.ts:704-805). codex-set.component.spec.ts:162 'loads the rating of the equipped armour…' and :180 'keeps an honest gap…' stub `armorRating` directly.
findings.fix: Add a `describe('CodexService.armorRating')` mirroring the facetValues block: asserts rpc name/params, sorted-classname cache key reuse, cache reset on build switch, and null (not throw) on an rpc error.

findings.what: The set stage's 'part names follow the UI language' fix has no spec; the language-switch path is tested for the gear rows only.
findings.evidence: codex-set-stage.component.ts:363 `lang = signal(toLang(this.t.getCurrentLang()))` and :428 `onLangChange…subscribe` have no counterpart in codex-set-stage.component.spec.ts (grep `lang|LangChange` → 0 hits); codex-set-gear.component.spec.ts:295 'follows a language switch to German and back' covers the gear component only.
findings.fix: Add a stage spec that emits `onLangChange` with 'de' and expects the tile `.name` to switch to the German `name.de` of the resolved entity, then back to EN.

findings.what: Gap-reason and readiness tooltips sit on non-focusable spans, so keyboard users can never open them (the directive opens on focusin only).
findings.evidence: src/app/codex/set/codex-set-rank-card.component.ts:113-117 `<span class="bar-gap-hatch" [scTooltip]=…>` and :124-129 `<span class="gap-dash" [scTooltip]=… [attr.aria-label]=…>` (aria-label on a role-less span); src/app/codex/set/codex-set-stage.component.ts:118-120 `<span class="rdy-ic" role="listitem" [scTooltip]=…>`; sc-tooltip.directive.ts:174-180 opens on `focusin` + keyboard modality, no pointer-less path otherwise.
findings.fix: Give `.gap-dash` (and `.rdy-ic`) `tabindex="0"` + `role="img"`/`role="note"` so Tab reaches them, or print the gap reason as visible text in the bar row instead of a tooltip.

findings.what: The build exit guard's own test never runs: scripts/build-with-exit-guard.test.mjs is referenced by no npm script and no workflow, so the script that decides what counts as a successful production build is effectively untested.
findings.evidence: `grep -rn "build-with-exit-guard.test" --include=*.json --include=*.yml --include=*.md .` → no hits; package.json:23 `test:gate` lists only routine-gate.liveness, routine-janitor-scan, pre.ask.unattended and lib/test-account tests; package.json:24 `test:assets-worker` likewise runs in no workflow.
findings.fix: Append `scripts/build-with-exit-guard.test.mjs` to the `test:gate` file list in package.json:23 (the file already exports `runGuarded`/`COMPLETION_MARKER` for that purpose).

findings.what: Dead code: five members of codex-detail and one public CodexService method are defined but referenced nowhere (template, other files or specs).
findings.evidence: grep counts (in-file / other files): `loadoutGroups` codex-detail.component.ts:4394-4411 (1/0), `emptyLoadoutCount` :4381 (1/0), `moduleSlotCount` :3722-3724 (1/0), `fmtSummary` :4266-4268 (1/0), `patchLabel` :4276-4279 (1/0); `CodexService.resolveKind` codex.service.ts:1181-1195 (5 sequential head-count probes) has no caller in src/app (files=1, itself).
findings.fix: Delete the six members (and `summarizePorts` import in codex-detail if it becomes unused; it is still used by codex-format's compare collector).

findings.what: The Worker turns every non-OK upstream answer from Supabase (429, 5xx, timeout) into a 404, so a transient Supabase outage reads as "asset does not exist" and the card component flips to its placeholder for the rest of the session.
findings.evidence: cloudflare/assets-worker/src/index.js:69 `if (!res.ok) return plain(404, 'not found');` src/app/codex/fallback-image.component.ts:10 "`(error)` flips the card to a placeholder glyph forever".
findings.fix: Return 404 only for upstream 404; map other upstream failures to 502 with `cache-control: no-store` (and add a test case next to `falls back to the Supabase bucket`).

findings.what: /docs loads the Scalar reference UI from jsDelivr with no version pin and no SRI, so an upstream breaking release or a compromised package renders on the project's API docs page without any change on our side (the same page also ships this unpinned tag in its copy-paste embed snippet).
findings.evidence: api/docs.ts:101 `<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@scalar/api-reference"></script>`; :90 embed snippet `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@scalar/api-reference` (no @version, no integrity).
findings.fix: Pin `@scalar/api-reference@<version>` in both places (and add `integrity`/`crossorigin` for the page's own tag).

findings.what: feedback.types.ts is a 1 944-line 'types' file that is mostly logic (search ranking, statistics, workflow queue, answer parsing).
findings.evidence: src/app/admin/feedback/feedback.types.ts: 222 exported members, 0 decorators; function bodies searchTokens :882 (112 lines), rankFeedbackSearch :1141, computeStats :803, weeklyPulse :1360 (65), flightPosition :1688, parseAnswerOptions :1897; a whole workflow-queue section 489–768 (buildWorkflowQueue :547, filterWorkflowScope :612, filterWorkflowKind :659, workflowKindCounts :668, workflowScopeCounts :679, workflowFocusIndex :718, foldThread :753) has no caller in any component or service (grep over src/app/admin/feedback/*.component.ts, *.service.ts = 0 hits).
findings.fix: Keep the interfaces/enums in feedback.types.ts; move search into feedback-search.ts (882–1180), statistics into feedback-stats.ts (769–880, 1284–1470), answer parsing into feedback-answers.ts; delete or wire the workflow section (see the spec-only finding).

findings.what: The display-level variant fold hides distinct armour records that share name and facets: in the live build 29 helmet records in 18 groups vanish behind one card (colourways and `_hair_extension` variants), and the folded records can neither be opened nor equipped from the Arsenal — only recognised as already equipped.
findings.evidence: Live probe, build 4.10.0, attach_type=Char_Armor_Helmet, is_variant=false: 683 rows → 18 fold keys with >1 class name, 29 hidden, e.g. `argus helmet|VGL|1|A|Light => vgl_armor_light_helmet_01_01_starlifter, vgl_armor_light_helmet_01_01_01`, `deadhead helmet||1|A|Medium => srvl_helmet_01_01_12_hair_extension, …_13_…, …_14_…, srvl_helmet_01_01_01, srvl_helmet_01_01_01_hair_extension`; src/app/codex/codex-variant-fold.ts:60-76 fold key = name + facets; src/app/codex/fps-list.component.ts:1068 `(card.foldedClassNames ?? []).includes(item.className)` (equipped check only).
findings.fix: Keep the fold, but let the folded card open a picker of its absorbed class names in equip mode (same pattern as the skin picker) so a specific colourway can be equipped; document the measured number in the fold header.

findings.what: A failed Starscape vote silently flips the thumbs-up back: the optimistic icon and count revert with no message and no log, so the tap reads as 'did that register?' — the exact ambiguity the optimistic update was meant to remove.
findings.evidence: src/app/starscape/starscape-votes.service.ts:139-141 `} catch { this.applyLocal(imageId, had); } finally { this.markBusy(imageId, false); }`; starscape.component.ts template has no failure hint (`grep -n 'vote.*fail\|votes\.(error|failed)' src/app/starscape/starscape.component.ts` → 0); the rollback itself is tested (starscape-votes.service.spec.ts:88).
findings.fix: Add a `voteFailed = signal<string|null>(null)` set in that catch (cleared after ~3 s) plus `console.warn('[starscape] vote write failed', err)`, and render a one-line `starscape.votes.failed` hint next to the tile's vote button (new DE/EN key).

findings.what: Five route guards each spin their own 30 ms `setInterval` poll waiting for `auth.ready()` (four with no timeout) instead of awaiting one promise — every navigation during boot runs a timer per guard in the chain.
findings.evidence: src/app/auth/auth.guard.ts:19 `const interval = setInterval(() => { if (auth.ready()) { clearInterval(interval); resolve(); } }, 30);` — duplicated verbatim in src/app/auth/approved.guard.ts:78, src/app/auth/public-only.guard.ts:39, src/app/auth/public-or-approved.guard.ts:52, src/app/auth/role.guard.ts:36; only src/app/auth/role.service.ts:246-250 pairs its poll with `setTimeout(finish, RoleService.WAIT_READY_TIMEOUT_MS)`.
findings.fix: Add `AuthService.whenReady(): Promise<void>` (a promise resolved where `ready` is set true) and replace the five `waitForReady`/`waitForAuth` helpers with `await auth.whenReady()`; keep the guards' return values unchanged.

findings.what: News thumbnails still animate `filter: blur(8px → 0)` over 0.6 s on every image reveal — the exact property CHANGELOG 0.71.0 removed from the Starscape and shared reveals as "the most expensive property" — on a list that renders many cards at once.
findings.evidence: src/app/news/news-thumb.component.ts:459-464 `.layer { … opacity: 0; filter: blur(8px); … transition: opacity 0.6s ease, filter 0.6s ease, transform 0.4s ease; }` :466 `.layer.show { opacity: 1; filter: blur(0); }`. CHANGELOG.md 0.71.0 Fixed: "Dropped the most expensive property from both reveals. `filter: blur()` animated on the Starscape image reveal … and on the shared content reveal. Opacity and a small translate carry it now." Reduced motion is handled (:501-502 `filter: none`), duration 600 ms is above the 500 ms guidance and undocumented.
findings.fix: In news-thumb.component.ts drop `filter` from `.layer`/`.layer.show` and the transition list; carry the reveal with opacity + the existing `transform: scale(var(--sc-thumb-zoom))` (as starscape `.tile-img` does, 0.42 s).

findings.what: Column-menu popover text is a literal 11px, below the mobile gate's 12px floor on touch devices (RULE-H: thresholds are never relaxed) because the rules bypass `--sc-fs-floor`.
findings.evidence: column-menu.component.ts:161 `.cm-title { … font-size: 11px …}`, :164 `.cm-sortbtn … font-size: 11px`, :168 `.cm-range input … font-size: 11px`, :176 `.cm-clear … font-size: 11px` — while `.unit`/`.cm-secondary` in the same file already use `max(11px, var(--sc-fs-floor))`.
findings.fix: Change the four literals to `font-size: max(11px, var(--sc-fs-floor))` (desktop unchanged, 12px on a coarse pointer).

findings.what: The same 'in hangar' ✓ badge opens its tooltip at the Info tier on the bridge and at the Label tier on the Arsenal cards (tier inconsistency for one control).
findings.evidence: src/app/codex/codex-bridge.component.ts:295 `✓` (no tier → Info 1500 ms) vs src/app/codex/codex-list.component.ts:427-428 same badge with `scTooltipTier="label"`. Otherwise the 94 Label-tier call sites sampled (admin lock reasons, truncated badges, date cells, icon-only pins/favourites/view switch, disabled reasons) all meet criterion a/b/c; no call site passes a raw delay (grep scTooltipDelay → none); tiers live in the directive (src/app/shared/tooltip/sc-tooltip.directive.ts:19-25).
findings.fix: Add `scTooltipTier="label"` to the bridge's `.in-hangar` span (icon-only badge, criterion a).

findings.what: Three runtime files are referenced by nothing but their own spec: an orphaned holo hangar tab component, a swipe directive and a retired guard (662 lines).
findings.evidence: src/app/codex/holo/codex-holo-hangar.component.ts (377 lines, selector 'sc-codex-holo-hangar' at :39): no template uses the selector and no non-spec file imports CodexHoloHangarComponent; superseded by stage/hangar-picker.component.ts in 7423427 ('in-picture hangar picker'); src/app/core/swipe-action.directive.ts (225 lines, selector '[scSwipeAction]' at :52): 'scSwipeAction' appears in no template since it was added in #610; src/app/auth/public-or-approved.guard.ts (60 lines): app.routes.ts:262 comment 'former signed-out teaser (`publicOrApprovedGuard`) is gone'.
findings.fix: Delete the three files and their specs (codex-holo-hangar.component.spec.ts, swipe-action.directive.spec.ts, public-or-approved.guard.spec.ts); remove the stale comment at app.routes.ts:262.

findings.what: `sc-codex-holo-hangar` (376 lines + 150-line spec) is compiled and tested but rendered nowhere — the Holotable uses `sc-hangar-picker` instead; the dead component also carries an N+1 (`listConfigs` per hangar ship) and a snapshot `location.pathname` redirect the rest of the app moved away from (REQ-27).
findings.evidence: `grep -rl 'sc-codex-holo-hangar\|CodexHoloHangarComponent' src/app` → only src/app/codex/holo/codex-holo-hangar.component.ts and its spec; src/app/codex/holo/codex-holo-stage.component.ts:292-301 `<sc-hangar-picker kind="ship" [docked]="true" …>`; codex-holo-hangar.component.ts:347-363 `await Promise.all(ships.map(async (ship) => { const configs = await this.hangar.listConfigs(ship.id); …`; :245 `currentPath = typeof location !== 'undefined' ? location.pathname : '/'`.
findings.fix: Delete src/app/codex/holo/codex-holo-hangar.component.ts and codex-holo-hangar.component.spec.ts (nothing imports them).

findings.what: The skin viewer's ranged GLB-head fetch has no AbortController and no timeout: switching ships or leaving the page lets the ~1 MB request run to completion, and a stalled server keeps the promise pending forever (only the result is sequence-guarded).
findings.evidence: src/app/codex/ship-skin-viewer.component.ts:734 `void fetch(url, { headers: { Range: \`bytes=0-${GLB_HEAD_BYTES - 1}\` } })` with :86 `GLB_HEAD_BYTES = 1_048_576`; :731,737 seq guard only drops the late result; no `signal:` option, no `AbortSignal.timeout`.
findings.fix: Keep an `AbortController` per read, abort it in `readLocators` before starting the next one and on destroy, and pass `signal: AbortSignal.any([ctrl.signal, AbortSignal.timeout(10_000)])`.

findings.what: A large GIF bypasses the 5 MB client check (it exists only for non-images) and is passed through un-re-encoded, so it fails at the bucket with the generic 'attachment not cached' / 'upload error' sentences instead of the specific too-large message.
findings.evidence: src/app/admin/feedback/feedback-composer.component.ts:1190-1198 `if (!isImage && file.size > MAX_FILE_BYTES)`; :1256-1259 `if (file.type === 'image/gif') { const dataUrl = await this.readAsDataUrl(file); … }` (no size check, no re-encode); bucket ceiling supabase/migrations/20260713000000_feedback_images_bucket.sql:22 `5242880`.
findings.fix: In addFiles change the guard to `if ((!isImage || file.type === 'image/gif') && file.size > MAX_FILE_BYTES)` so GIFs get the `fileTooLarge` sentence.

findings.what: The throughput chart's per-week numbers are reachable only through a native title tooltip on a non-focusable span (hover-only: no keyboard, no touch, not in the accessible name).
findings.evidence: src/app/admin/feedback/feedback-dashboard.component.ts:188 `<span class="wk" [class.now]="w.current" [attr.title]="weekTitle(w)">` inside `role="img"` (186); `throughputLabel()` (988-999) names only totals/peak/current, not the weeks.
findings.fix: Drop the `[attr.title]` and append the per-week text (`weeks().map(weekTitle).join('; ')`) to `throughputLabel()`, or render it as a visually hidden `<ul>` after the chart.

findings.what: Dead members: two template aliases and one constant field are never referenced.
findings.evidence: src/app/admin/feedback/admin-feedback.component.ts:1424 `readonly turnLabelKey = turnLabelKey;` (`grep -c "turnLabelKey("` in the file = 0), :1422 `readonly isPlainLeftClick = isPlainLeftClick;` (template never calls it; only onViewInApp uses the import); src/app/admin/telemetry-stats.component.ts:538 `readonly windows = WINDOWS;` (no `windows` reference in the template).
findings.fix: Delete the three fields (and the now-unused `turnLabelKey` import at 74).

findings.what: Defence-in-depth gap: the concept iframe src is trusted verbatim from the ticket response with bypassSecurityTrustResourceUrl and an allow-scripts+allow-same-origin sandbox, without checking it points at the function origin.
findings.evidence: src/app/admin/concepts/concept-page.component.ts:131-134 `this.sanitizer.bypassSecurityTrustResourceUrl(url)`, :61 `sandbox="allow-scripts allow-same-origin allow-forms allow-popups allow-downloads"`; src/app/admin/concepts/concept-page.service.ts:91-93 only `typeof body.url !== 'string'`. The function is first-party (supabase/functions/concept-page), so this is hygiene, not an exposure.
findings.fix: In mintTicket reject a url that does not start with `${environment.supabase.url}/functions/v1/concept-page/` (throw ConceptTicketFailure('error')).

findings.what: Layout properties are animated on the dashboard bars and meters (height/width transitions) instead of compositor properties; the row-fold service also animates height/padding/margin, though as a one-off 320 ms effect.
findings.evidence: src/app/admin/feedback/feedback-dashboard.component.ts:403 `transition: height 0.45s cubic-bezier(…)` on `.wk-raised, .wk-shipped`, :571 `transition: width 0.45s` on `.meter-fill`; src/app/admin/feedback/feedback-motion.service.ts:207-221 keyframes on `height`, `paddingTop/Bottom`, `borderTop/BottomWidth`, `marginBottom`. Reduced motion is honoured (dashboard 618-621, service 203-206).
findings.fix: Dashboard: set `[style.transform]="'scaleY(' + pct/100 + ')'"` with `transform-origin: bottom` / `left` and `transition: transform 0.45s` instead of height/width. Keep the fold as is (a layout collapse needs the height) and note it as deliberate.

findings.what: The dossier panel is sized with `100vh` on phones (and `calc(100vh - 48px)` on desktop), so on mobile browsers the panel's bottom — last TOC pill row and the tail — sits under the browser chrome (ui-defaults R6: use dvh/svh for full-height layouts).
findings.evidence: src/app/news/patch-dossier.component.ts:564 `.panel { max-height: 100vh; height: 100vh; border-radius: 0; border: 0; }`, :395 `max-height: calc(100vh - 48px)`.
findings.fix: Replace with `100dvh` / `calc(100dvh - 48px)` (keep the `100vh` declaration on the line before as the fallback).

findings.what: The header status chip's focus ring is a literal colour instead of a token (R0), and differs from the `outline: 2px solid var(--sc-accent)` idiom every other news control uses.
findings.evidence: src/app/news/verse-status-chip.component.ts:133 `.vs-chip:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px rgba(0, 212, 255, 0.35); }` (the only non-black literal colour in the module; grep rgba/hex in src/app/news).
findings.fix: `box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px color-mix(in srgb, var(--sc-accent) 35%, transparent);` — or `outline: 2px solid var(--sc-accent); outline-offset: 2px;` like :188.

findings.what: 47 `:hover` rules in the news module (none in the whole app) sit outside `@media (hover: hover)`; the two that move things — card lift and thumbnail zoom — stick after a tap on touch devices (R6 static).
findings.evidence: grep `:hover` src/app/news/*.ts → 47 hits, grep `hover: hover` src/app/news src/styles.scss → 0. Transform hovers: src/app/news/news-list.component.ts:600-605 `.card:hover { transform: translateY(-3px) scale(1.005); … }`, src/app/news/news-thumb.component.ts:467-468 `:host-context(.card:hover) .layer.show { transform: scale(calc(var(--sc-thumb-zoom, 1) * 1.04)); }`.
findings.fix: Wrap those two transform hover rules in `@media (hover: hover)` (colour/border hovers can stay); the app-wide guard is a polish topic for the shared styles lens.

findings.what: Layout properties are animated on small hot-path elements: the cadence dot fill transitions `width` every 250 ms while the carousel rotates, chart bars transition `height`, and a toggle uses `transition: all`.
findings.evidence: src/app/news/patch-cadence.component.ts:271 `.dot-fill { … transition: width 250ms linear; }` (ticks via setInterval TICK_MS 250, :498-503), :299 `.win-opt { … transition: all 0.16s; }`, :350 `.col-bar { transition: height 0.3s ease; }`; src/app/news/stability-panel.component.ts:564 and src/app/news/stability-history.component.ts:708 same `transition: height 0.3s`.
findings.fix: Draw the fill with `transform: scaleX(pct)` + `transform-origin: left` (bind `[style.transform]`), animate `transform: scaleY()` for bars or drop the height transition, and list the properties explicitly instead of `all`.

findings.what: The header status popover's trigger announces `aria-expanded` but has no `aria-haspopup`/`aria-controls`, and the opened `role="dialog"` panel receives no focus, so a keyboard user must Tab past the trigger to find it.
findings.evidence: src/app/news/verse-status-chip.component.ts:57-63 `<button … [attr.aria-expanded]="open()" … (click)="toggle($event)">`, :69 `<div class="vs-panel" role="dialog" …>` — no focus() call (grep), unlike src/app/desktop/app-download-menu.component.ts:465-486 which focuses the popover and restores focus.
findings.fix: Add `aria-haspopup="dialog"` and `[attr.aria-controls]="'vs-panel'"` on the trigger, give the panel `id="vs-panel" tabindex="-1"`, focus it after open and return focus to the trigger on Escape/close (mirror app-download-menu).

findings.what: Five string `redirectTo` routes drop the incoming query string (Angular 22 keeps only params named in the redirect string); the root redirect therefore turns the documented deep link `/?item=<id>` into `/news` without the item.
findings.evidence: src/app/app.routes.ts:52 `redirectTo: 'news'`, :294 `p4k → uploader`, :337 `desktop → uploader`, :353 `admin/integrations → admin/api-tokens`, :427 `'**' → news`; node_modules/@angular/router/fesm2022/_router-chunk.mjs:2713 `new UrlTree(newRoot, this.createQueryParams(urlTree.queryParams, this.urlTree.queryParams), …)` where createQueryParams (2715-2727) copies only the redirect's own params; src/app/news/news-list.component.ts:1022 `// Deep link: /news?item=<id>`; the file already documents the behaviour at :38-40 for blueprintListRedirect.
findings.fix: Turn the root redirect (and, if bookmarks matter, the three legacy aliases) into a functional redirect like blueprintListRedirect that forwards `queryParams`, e.g. `redirectTo: ({ queryParams }) => inject(Router).createUrlTree(['/news'], { queryParams })`, with a case in app.routes.spec.ts.

findings.what: The header's phase badge is hard-coded template text ('alpha') instead of an i18n key or the `environment.appPhase` value it mirrors.
findings.evidence: src/app/shell/shell.component.ts:74 `alpha`; src/environments/environment.ts `appPhase: 'alpha' as const`.
findings.fix: Render `{{ environment.appPhase }}` (or add `nav.phaseBadge` to public/i18n/de.json + en.json and use `{{ 'nav.phaseBadge' | translate }}`) so the badge flips with the phase.

findings.what: The chunk-load recovery is one-shot per URL, not per session: with a service worker stuck on a stale index, every rarely visited nav entry earns its own full page load, and the SwUpdate startup auto-reload can add one more — bounded (no infinite loop), but a user can see three or four reloads in a row before the notice appears.
findings.evidence: src/app/core/route-load-recovery.service.ts:151 `if (this.recoveredUrl() === url) {` (marker holds a single URL, :167 `this.rememberRecovered(url)` overwrites it); src/app/core/sw-update.service.ts:95-99 `if (withinStartup && !this.autoReloadedThisSession()) { … void this.applyUpdate();`.
findings.fix: Keep a small session counter next to the URL marker (e.g. `sc.nav.recoveries`), and once it reaches 2 within the session surface `loadFailed` instead of reloading again.

findings.what: The patch board's loading skeleton is a local background-position shimmer loop (1.5 s) — the kind of second skeleton tempo CHANGELOG 0.71.0 removed in favour of the single `.sc-skel` inference system; it repaints continuously while the board loads.
findings.evidence: src/app/news/patch-board.component.ts:234-240 `.skeleton .card { … background-size: 240% 100%; animation: pb-shimmer 1.5s linear infinite; } … @keyframes pb-shimmer { from { background-position: 140% 0; } to { background-position: -40% 0; } }`. CHANGELOG.md 0.71.0: "There is now a single system … Structure and chrome … get an inference layer" (`.sc-skel`, styles.scss:820-846).
findings.fix: Give the skeleton cards the `sc-skel` class (optionally `--sc-skel-i` per row) and delete the local `.skeleton .card` background/animation, `pb-shimmer` keyframes and their reduced-motion override.

findings.what: The patch-cadence countdown pill is a continuous layout animation: a 250 ms `setInterval` steps `elapsed`, the fill's `width` follows, and `transition: width 250ms linear` smooths it — four width transitions per second for as long as the carousel rotates.
findings.evidence: src/app/news/patch-cadence.component.ts:268-273 `.dot-fill { position: absolute; … transition: width 250ms linear; }`; :497-504 `const id = setInterval(() => { const next = this.elapsed() + TICK_MS; … else this.elapsed.set(next); }, TICK_MS);` with `TICK_MS = 250` (:37); :486-490 `fillPct` feeds the width. Reduced motion is handled (:487 `if (!this.hasSlides() || this.reducedMotion()) return 100;`, :398 `.dot-fill { transition: none; }`).
findings.fix: Bind the fill to `transform: scaleX(pct/100)` with `transform-origin: left` (e.g. `[style.--fill]="fillPct()/100"` and `transform: scaleX(var(--fill))`) and transition `transform` instead of `width`; the spec (patch-cadence.spec.ts:284-297) asserts `fillPct()` and element presence, not `style.width`.

findings.what: The patch dossier smooth-scrolls unconditionally (TOC click and card jump) while the rest of the app switches to `'auto'` under reduced motion; its reduced-motion CSS block covers only its keyframes.
findings.evidence: src/app/news/patch-dossier.component.ts:794 `el.scrollIntoView({ behavior: 'smooth', block: 'center' });` and :862 `target.scrollIntoView({ behavior: 'smooth', block: 'start' });` — grep 'reduced|matchMedia' in the file hits only the CSS media query at :447. Compare src/app/settings/settings.component.ts:1125-1128 `return reduced ? 'auto' : 'smooth';` and src/app/admin/feedback/feedback-motion.service.ts:85 `behavior: this.reducedMotion ? 'auto' : 'smooth'`.
findings.fix: Add a `prefersReducedMotion()` check (matchMedia) in patch-dossier.component.ts and pass `behavior: reduced ? 'auto' : 'smooth'` at both call sites.

findings.what: The hangar item picker popover has no Escape handler and no dialog role, so it can only be dismissed with the pointer (backdrop click or the × button).
findings.evidence: src/app/hangar/hangar-item-picker.component.ts:41 `<div class="picker sc-card" (click)="$event.stopPropagation()">`; `grep -nE 'HostListener|keydown' src/app/hangar/hangar-item-picker.component.ts src/app/hangar/hangar-ship-detail.component.ts` → 0 hits; parent closes only via `(closed)="pickerPort.set(null)"` (:312).
findings.fix: Add `@HostListener('document:keydown.escape') onEscape() { this.closed.emit(); }` to HangarItemPickerComponent and `role="dialog" [attr.aria-label]="'hangar.picker.searchPlaceholder' | translate"` on the `.picker` root.

findings.what: Two symbol-only buttons have no accessible name and no app tooltip: the holo hangar group "←" back button and the KPI "ⓘ" info button (which only has aria-describedby, so it is announced as an unnamed button followed by the description).
findings.evidence: node scan of 603 `<button>/<a>` for symbol-only text without aria-label/scTooltip → 2 hits: src/app/codex/holo/codex-holo-hangar.component.ts:100 `<button type="button" class="hh-back" (click)="activeGroup.set(null)">←</button>`; src/app/codex/codex-kpi-band.component.ts:30 `<button type="button" class="kpi-info tip" tabindex="0" [attr.aria-describedby]="'kpi-tip-' + c.key">ⓘ</button>`.
findings.fix: Give both an `[attr.aria-label]` from an i18n key (a "back to groups" key and "more about {label}") and, per R1 (a), a `[scTooltip]` on the Label tier for the back arrow.

findings.what: Four interactive elements still carry a native `title` tooltip, which never opens on keyboard focus and renders in the OS look; in every case an aria twin already exists, so the attribute is redundant (REQ-8 wording: no native title on interactive elements).
findings.evidence: grep -rnE '<(button|a|input)[^>]*\btitle=|\[title\]|\[attr\.title\]' src/app → src/app/codex/holo/codex-holo-inspector.component.ts:38 `[title]="('codex.swap.close' | translate) + ' (Esc)'"` (button already has aria-label); src/app/codex/codex-mission-bar.component.ts:41 `[attr.title]="disabledReason(m.id) ? … : (m.labelKey | translate)"` on `role="radio"` buttons (aria-describedby present); src/app/codex/codex-loadout-save-bar.component.ts:57 `[attr.title]="partial() ? …"` (aria-describedby=reasonId present); src/app/codex/holo/codex-holo-table.component.ts:108 `[attr.title]="pin.resolved ? pin.label : …"` on pin buttons.
findings.fix: Delete the four `title` bindings; where the text is not yet on screen (holo-table unresolved pin) replace it with `[scTooltip]` on the Label tier.

findings.what: Three text fields have only a placeholder as their name — the hangar notes textarea, the settings username input and the quick-search combobox input — so once text is entered a screen reader has no label for them.
findings.evidence: node scan of 77 form controls: src/app/hangar/hangar-ship-detail.component.ts:329 `<textarea rows="3" [ngModel]="notesDraft()" … [attr.placeholder]=…>` (heading `<h2>` at :328 not linked); src/app/settings/settings.component.ts:193-199 `<input type="text" class="text-input" … [placeholder]="'settings.username.placeholder' | translate"` (h3 at :190 not linked); src/app/shell/quick-search.component.ts:75-87 `<input class="qs-input" type="search" role="combobox" … [attr.placeholder]=…>` with no aria-label (the surrounding dialog has one at :74). The other 7 scan hits are false positives (doc comments, hidden file inputs, label-wrapped controls at admin.component.ts:344 and feedback-composer.component.ts:313).
findings.fix: Add `id` + `aria-labelledby` pointing at the existing heading (hangar notes, settings username) and `[attr.aria-label]="'quickSearch.placeholder' | translate"` on the quick-search input.

findings.what: The shell has no skip link: every page starts with the brand link, ~10 nav links, the quick search, the status chip and the user menu before `<main>`, and a keyboard user must Tab through all of them on every route.
findings.evidence: `grep -rn 'skip-link\|skip to' src/app src/styles.scss` → 0 hits; landmarks exist: src/app/shell/shell.component.ts:58 `<header class="topbar">`, :78 `<nav class="nav">`, :313 `<main class="content" [@routeReveal]=…>`; public layout src/app/shell/public-layout.component.ts:43 `<main class="content">`.
findings.fix:
Add `{{ 'nav.skipToContent' | translate }}` as the first child of the shell (and public layout) template, `id="sc-main" tabindex="-1"` on `
`, a visually-hidden-until-focus rule in styles.scss, and the DE/EN keys.

findings.what: The admin feedback board loads every feedback row, every thread message and every author message with no range/limit and holds them all in memory; PostgREST silently caps each select at 1 000 rows, so the board both grows unbounded and truncates silently past that.
findings.evidence: src/app/admin/feedback/admin-feedback.component.ts:2138-2142 `.from('admin_feedback').select('id, seq, author_id, body, … author:profiles(display_name, username, role)').order('created_at', { ascending: true });` — no `.range()`/`.limit()` (grep for `\.range\(|\.limit\(` in src/app/admin/feedback → 0 hits); same at :2163-2165 and :2209-2211. Cap: supabase/config.toml:8 `max_rows = 1000`. Only the delivered band is paged client-side (:1536 `visibleDeliveredDays = computed(() => this.deliveredDays().slice(0, this.deliveredDaysShown()))`).
findings.fix: Load the delivered/shipped buckets server-side in pages (`.range()` ordered by created_at desc, driven by `deliveredDaysShown`) and request `{ count: 'exact' }` on the open buckets so a truncated result shows a notice instead of vanishing rows.

findings.what: The Starscape lightbox is `role="dialog" aria-modal="true"` but never receives focus and has no focus trap or focus return: a keyboard user who opens a tile keeps tabbing through the page behind the overlay.
findings.evidence: src/app/starscape/starscape.component.ts:335 `<div class="lightbox" role="dialog" aria-modal="true" (click)="close()">`, :1061-1063 `open(w) { this.active.set(w); }` (no focus), :1082-1085 `close()` (no focus return). Contrast app-download-menu.component.ts:463-466 which focuses its popover and :486 returns focus.
findings.fix: Add `tabindex="-1"` on the `<figure>`, a `viewChild` + `effect` that focuses it when `active()` is set, remember `document.activeElement` in `open()` and restore it in `close()`.

findings.what: The bundle-history patch row is a `<div role="button" tabindex="0">` with hand-written Enter/Space handlers instead of a real `<button>` (CLAUDE.md: actions stay `<button>`).
findings.evidence: src/app/p4k/p4k-history.component.ts:66-70 `<div class="patch-main" role="button" tabindex="0" (click)="toggleGroup(…)" (keydown.enter)="…" (keydown.space)="…; $event.preventDefault()" [attr.aria-expanded]=…>`.
findings.fix: Make it `<button type="button" class="patch-main">` (reset `font: inherit; text-align: left; width: 100%`) and drop the keydown handlers.

findings.what: The shell's route-reveal Angular animation (320 ms rise + scale on every navigation) ignores prefers-reduced-motion: the global CSS clamp only reaches CSS animations, not Web-Animations-driven `@trigger`s.
findings.evidence: shell.component.ts:49-56 `trigger('routeReveal', [transition(':increment', [style({ opacity: 0, transform: 'translateY(10px) scale(0.994)' }), animate('320ms …')])])`; the component's only reduced-motion rule is for `.nav-scan__bar` (:450); styles.scss:538-546 clamps `animation-duration`/`transition-duration` which does not affect the Web Animations API.
findings.fix: Read `matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches` once in ShellComponent and bind `[@.disabled]="reducedMotion"` on `<main class="content">` (or gate `[@routeReveal]` to a constant).

findings.what: Login form errors are not announced to screen readers and the 'not invited' notice has no role — unlike the sibling auth pages which use role="alert".
findings.evidence:
login.component.ts:65 `
`, :121 `
{{ errorMsg() }}
`, :167, :211 (no role); set-password.component.ts:75 and password-form.component.ts:212 use `role="alert"`.
findings.fix: Add `role="alert"` to the three `.err` divs and to `.notice.denied` in login.component.ts.

findings.what: The segmented control hides its scrollbar entirely, so when segments overflow on a narrow screen nothing indicates that more choices exist off-screen (R5: a local scrollbar style diverging from the global one).
findings.evidence: segmented-control.component.ts:124 `overflow-x: auto; overflow-y: hidden; scrollbar-width: none;` and :126 `.seg::-webkit-scrollbar { display: none; }`; the global thin bar is styles.scss:556-580.
findings.fix: Either keep the global thin scrollbar, or add edge fades (`mask-image: linear-gradient(90deg, transparent, #000 12px, #000 calc(100% - 12px), transparent)`) when the pill overflows.

findings.what: Stale API doc: the segmented control's `titleKey` is documented as a native `title` tooltip although it renders through the app tooltip directive (REQ-8 wording).
findings.evidence: segmented-control.component.ts:39 `/** Optional i18n key for the \`title\` tooltip — use for abbreviated labels. */` vs :86/:99 `[scTooltip]="o.titleKey ? (o.titleKey | translate) : null" scTooltipTier="label"`.
findings.fix: Reword the comment to "Optional i18n key for the app tooltip (`[scTooltip]`, label tier)".

findings.what: Outbound fetches without a timeout outside the news path: the three R2 calls behind the REQ-29 gate (a hung Cloudflare analytics API stalls every `sign` until the platform limit instead of failing closed quickly), the ReadMe probe and the resvg wasm download.
findings.evidence: ingest-skins/_r2.ts:112 `const res = await cfg.client.fetch(url.toString());` :122 `cfg.client.fetch(objectUrl(cfg, key), { method: 'DELETE' })` :145-152 `await fetch('https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/graphql', { method: 'POST', … })` (no signal); readme-sync/readme-api.ts:76 `await fetch(`${this.base}${path}`, { method: 'GET', headers: this.headers() })`; starscape-summary/index.ts:97 `fetch(RESVG_WASM_URL)`.
findings.fix: Pass `signal: AbortSignal.timeout(10_000)` in each init (aws4fetch's `client.fetch` forwards RequestInit); the existing catch blocks already map a throw to 503 `r2_usage_unknown` / 500 `sign_failed`.

findings.what: Every `sign` call lists the ENTIRE R2 bucket to compute the quota (`bucketBytes` → ListObjectsV2 over all prefixes, 1000 keys/page, Class A ops), once per ship signed (~150 per catalog run) and growing with the bucket, while the usage read next to it is cached for 5 min.
findings.evidence: ingest-skins/index.ts:193-194 `used = await bucketBytes(r2);` per sign request; _r2.ts:128-131 `const objects = await listObjects(cfg, ''); return objects.reduce((sum, o) => sum + o.size, 0);` :104-118 follows continuation tokens with no cap; _r2.ts:134-135 `USAGE_TTL_MS = 5 * 60 * 1000` caches only fetchUsage.
findings.fix: Cache the bucketBytes result in module scope with the same `USAGE_TTL_MS` (add the bytes just signed to the cached total), or derive the quota check from `usage.storageBytes` already returned by fetchUsage.

findings.what: Shell renders the untranslated status badge text `alpha` outside ngx-translate.
findings.evidence: src/app/shell/shell.component.ts:74 `alpha` (the sibling `nav.brandAria` at :69 is translated). Brand name "Star Citizen Companion" at shell.component.ts:73 and footer.component.ts:28 is a proper noun and not counted.
findings.fix: Add `nav.alphaBadge` ("Alpha") to de.json/en.json and render `{{ 'nav.alphaBadge' | translate }}` in shell.component.ts:74.

findings.what: `.env.example` and `src/env.d.ts` document NG_APP_POSTHOG_* environment variables that nothing reads — the PostHog key is hard-coded in environment.ts, so the documented 'set it in your hosting provider' route is a no-op.
findings.evidence: .env.example:1-5 `NG_APP_POSTHOG_PROJECT_TOKEN=` + 'set the same values in your hosting provider's environment variables for production builds'; src/env.d.ts:3-4 declares them and :8-10 admits 'no env-substituting builder is wired … import.meta.env is undefined'; `grep -rn "import.meta.env\|process.env" src --include=*.ts` → only env.d.ts; src/environments/environment.ts:23-26 `posthog: { key: 'phc_…', host: 'https://eu.i.posthog.com' }` (same in environment.prod.ts:23-25); analytics.service.ts:48/130 reads `environment.posthog.key`.
findings.fix: Delete `.env.example` and the `Env`/`ImportMeta` declarations in src/env.d.ts, and point the README/analytics comment at `src/environments/environment*.ts` as the only configuration place.

findings.what: browser-extension/README.md says host permissions cover 'the two Companion origins' while the manifest and COMPANION_ORIGINS hold exactly one (the second was removed 2026-08-02 as a hijack target).
findings.evidence: browser-extension/README.md:19-20 — 'host permissions scoped to `robertsspaceindustries.com/…/account/pledges*` and the two Companion origins.'; browser-extension/manifest.json:15-19 lists one companion origin `https://sc-companion.vercel.app/*`; src/lib/hangar-core.js:17-24 — '`star-citizen-companion-web` was listed here until 2026-08-02 … `COMPANION_ORIGINS = Object.freeze(['https://sc-companion.vercel.app'])`'.
findings.fix: Change README.md line 20 to 'and the Companion origin `sc-companion.vercel.app`'.

findings.what: The stashed ship list (`pendingImport`) outlives the documented 30-minute expiry: the TTL is only enforced when the Companion tab asks for it, so a user who clicks Import and never reaches /hangar/import keeps the full list in chrome.storage.local until 'Forget stored data' or the next handover.
findings.evidence: browser-extension/src/content/companion-bridge.js:45-57 — the expiry check `Date.now() - candidate.capturedAt < PENDING_TTL_MS` runs only inside `sendPending()` (on `hangar-import:request`); rsi-hangar.js:197-203 writes `PENDING_KEY` on Import and nothing on the RSI side ever prunes it; popup.js:60 removes it only on 'forget'. browser-extension/PRIVACY.md:45 — '`pendingImport` | The ship list awaiting confirmation | Deleted after confirm/cancel, expires after 30 min'.
findings.fix: In rsi-hangar.js `evaluate()` (runs on every hangar visit) and in popup.js `render()` read `pendingImport` and `chrome.storage.local.remove` it when `capturedAt` is older than 30 min (export PENDING_TTL_MS from hangar-core.js so all three sites share it); or, cheaper, reword PRIVACY.md to 'discarded the next time the extension runs after 30 min'.

findings.what: The two HttpClient calls to edge-function proxies have no timeout, so a hung proxy leaves the 'Where to buy' section on its loading text and the upcoming feed in its loading state indefinitely.
findings.evidence: src/app/codex/uex-shop.service.ts:303 `const res = await firstValueFrom(this.http.get<UexEnvelope<T>>(url));` (no `timeout()`); src/app/codex/upcoming-ships.service.ts:452 `await firstValueFrom(this.http.get<UpcomingShipsFeed>(this.endpoint))`; grep for `timeout(|AbortSignal|signal:` over uex-shop, upcoming-ships, codex.service, supabase.client returns nothing. codex-detail.component.ts:2578-2602 only clears `buyLoading` in `finally`, i.e. after the promise settles.
findings.fix: Pipe both gets through rxjs `timeout(15_000)` (import from 'rxjs') before `firstValueFrom`; the existing catch branches already turn a rejection into the empty/error state.

findings.what: The pre-redesign picker table API (columns, sort chain, facet filters, stat rows) and three other exported helpers survive only because their specs still call them; no production code does.
findings.evidence: src/app/codex/swap-table.ts:339 `swapColumns`, :380 `swapColumnBars`, :418 `toggleSwapSort`, :434 `defaultSwapSort`, :446 `sortSwapCandidates`, :480 `EMPTY_SWAP_FILTERS`, :496 `filterSwapCandidates`, :527 `swapFacets`, :539 `pruneSwapFilters`, :560 `swapStatRows` — each referenced once in swap-table.ts (its definition) and otherwise only in *.spec.ts (`grep -rlw` over src/app excluding specs); same for src/app/codex/codex-build-compare.ts:120 `compareShipBuilds`, src/app/codex/codex-kpi-sets.ts:15 `kpiSetFor`, src/app/codex/ship-summary-panels.ts:239 `buildShipSummaryPanels`. swap-table.ts:568-572 comment: "Everything below is ADDITIVE — the helpers above keep their behaviour and their specs."
findings.fix: Remove swap-table.ts:292-566 (the retired columns/sort/filter block) plus `compareShipBuilds`, `kpiSetFor` and `buildShipSummaryPanels` together with their spec cases; keep `swapTypeLabel`/`swapArchetype`/`buildSwapCandidate`, which the picker still uses.

findings.what: The uploader hand-off auto-submits the access token plus a freshly minted long-lived refresh token to any `http://127.0.0.1:<port>` named in `?cb=` with no consent click, so a crafted link opened by a signed-in collaborator posts both tokens to whatever local process listens on that port (a dev server logging request bodies is enough).
findings.evidence: src/app/desktop/desktop-auth.component.ts:216-234 `form.action = this.cb; … addField('token', handoff.access_token); … addField('refresh_token', handoff.refresh_token); … form.submit();` (runs from `ngOnInit`, no user gesture); src/app/desktop/loopback.util.ts:23-31 accepts any port 1–65535; supabase/functions/desktop-session/index.ts:24-29 mints an independent session with its own rotation chain.
findings.fix: Show a one-click confirmation ("Connect the Data Uploader on port 4682X?") before the form submit; keep the loopback policy as documented.

findings.what: Six bare native `<select>` dropdowns remain although the app has `sc-select` (R2a): language and region pickers on Settings, the report category on Friends, the friend picker in the share panel, the release-channel picker and the admin promote picker.
findings.evidence: src/app/settings/settings.component.ts:257 and :276 `<select class="sc-select"`; src/app/social/friends.component.ts:252; src/app/social/loadout-share-panel.component.ts:980; src/app/desktop/channel-picker.component.ts:28 `<select [value]="channel()"`; src/app/desktop/desktop-download.component.ts:81 `<select class="psel"`; src/app/shared/sc-select.component.ts exists (REQ-9 already migrated the hangar pages: `grep '<select' src/app/hangar` → 0).
findings.fix: Replace each with `<sc-select [options] [value] (valueChange)>` (labelKey per option as in hangar-dashboard.component.ts:338-340); delete the local `.sc-select`/`.psel` styles.

findings.what: Chart columns in the stability history are <button>s that navigate to a patch-line dossier via router.navigate — a navigation on a non-anchor (no middle-click / open-in-new-tab).
findings.evidence: src/app/news/stability-history.component.ts:34-36 `<button type="button" class="col" … (click)="showLine.emit(v.line)">` → src/app/news/patch-board.component.ts:578-579 `openLine(line) { void this.router.navigate(['/news/patches', line], …) }`. All other 25 `router.navigate`/`navigateByUrl` call sites are keyboard (Enter/Escape), form submit, post-action redirects or reached through anchors gated by isPlainLeftClick (scan of every <a (click)>: all 15 in-app handlers call isPlainLeftClick; external ones never preventDefault).
findings.fix: Render each column as `<a class="col" [routerLink]="['/news/patches', v.line]" [queryParams]="query ? {q: query} : {}">` and drop the `showLine` output (or keep it for the gated plain-click path with isPlainLeftClick).

findings.what: `--sc-danger` colours negative comparison deltas and an over-limit gauge (data-viz), the same class of use REQ-14 removed from the rank card's weakest axis; the reserved meaning (error / destructive) is diluted.
findings.evidence: src/app/codex/codex-kpi-band.component.ts:104 `.kpi-delta.bad { color: var(--sc-danger); background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--sc-danger) 12%, transparent); }`; src/app/codex/holo/codex-holo-strip.component.ts:360 `.d.down { color: var(--sc-danger); }` and :439 `.hp-cooling .va.over { stroke: var(--sc-danger); }`; src/app/codex/codex-swap-picker.component.ts:591 `.cell.d.down { color: var(--sc-danger); }`; src/app/codex/holo/codex-holo-patch-delta.component.ts:98 `tr.bad .pct { color: var(--sc-danger, #ff5252); }`; src/app/codex/codex-hardpoint-layout.component.ts:881 `.fig .dl.down { color: var(--sc-danger, #ff5252);`. Precedent: src/app/codex/codex-rank-card.component.ts:281 comment "--sc-warning, not --sc-danger: a weak axis is…".

findings.what: Session loss is never acted on: `onAuthStateChange` only updates signals, so after a revoked refresh token (password change, global sign-out from another device — the desktop hand-off documents sign-out as global) the shell stays rendered and every write fails with the raw PostgREST message until the next navigation bounces to /login.
findings.evidence: src/app/auth/auth.service.ts:58-60 `this.sb.realClient.auth.onAuthStateChange((event, session) => { this._session.set(session); this._ready.set(true);` — no SIGNED_OUT branch (grep `SIGNED_OUT` in auth.service.ts: none); src/app/hangar/hangar.service.ts:353 `this.error.set(error.message)`; measured PostgREST wording for a denied read: "permission denied for table hangar_role_loadouts".
findings.fix: In `onAuthStateChange`, when `event === 'SIGNED_OUT'` and the current route is under the gated shell, `router.navigate(['/login'], { queryParams: { redirect: router.url } })`.

findings.what: All three route guards poll `auth.ready()` every 30 ms with no upper bound; if `getSession()` never settles (storage throwing on the first read, a PKCE exchange that hangs), the first navigation never resolves and the visitor sees an empty document with no message.
findings.evidence: src/app/auth/auth.guard.ts:16-25 `const interval = setInterval(() => { if (auth.ready()) { … } }, 30);` (identical copies in approved.guard.ts:97-107 and public-only.guard.ts:37-47); src/app/auth/auth.service.ts:50-53 `getSession().then(…)` with no `.catch`/timeout.
findings.fix: Extract one `waitForReady(auth, timeoutMs = 10000)` helper that resolves on timeout and lets the guards treat the visitor as signed out (`/login`), and add a `.catch(() => this._ready.set(true))` to the `getSession()` call.

findings.what: Three `role="tablist"` groups and five `role="radiogroup"` groups declare composite-widget roles but provide no arrow-key navigation, no `aria-controls`/tabpanel, so screen-reader users are told to use arrows that do nothing (each item is still Tab-reachable).
findings.evidence: tablists without keydown: src/app/codex/holo/codex-holo-stage.component.ts:209-211, src/app/feedback/user-feedback-panel.component.ts:56-70, src/app/shell/quick-search.component.ts:89-91 (`grep -nE 'ArrowLeft|ArrowRight'` → 0 in all three). radiogroups without arrow handling (grep -cE 'ArrowLeft|ArrowRight|keydown\.arrow' = 0): src/app/codex/holo/codex-holo-stage.component.ts:270 rolebar, src/app/codex/codex-mission-bar.component.ts:31, src/app/codex/set/codex-set-rank-card.component.ts:36, src/app/codex/set/codex-set-mission-bar.component.ts:23, src/app/codex/codex-rank-card.component.ts:128. sc-segmented, holo-strip and energy-dock do handle arrows (2 hits each).
findings.fix: Route the five radiogroups through `sc-segmented` (which already has arrow roving) or copy its keydown handler; for the three tablists either add ArrowLeft/ArrowRight roving + `aria-controls` on each tab and `role="tabpanel"` on the content, or downgrade to `role="group"` with `aria-pressed` buttons.

findings.what: Feedback submit/reply leaves orphaned objects in the public `feedback-images` bucket on partial failure: images are uploaded one by one, then the row is inserted; if upload k fails or the insert fails, uploads 1..k-1 (or all of them) stay in storage with nothing referencing them. The user-facing state is consistent (error shown, no row), the storage is not.
findings.evidence: src/app/feedback/user-feedback.service.ts:231-236 `const urls = await uploadFeedbackImages(...)` / `catch { this._error.set('upload'); return false; }` and :249-256 insert error → `this._error.set(... error.message); return false;` with no cleanup; same shape in `reply()` :285-296. feedback-images.util.ts:116-124 loops `bucket.upload` and `throw new Error(error.message)` at the first failure after earlier successes. A cleanup helper already exists but is only used on discard: feedback-draft.service.ts:383-390 `removeUploads()` → `storage.from(FEEDBACK_IMAGES_BUCKET).remove(paths)`.
findings.fix: Make `uploadFeedbackImages` return the paths uploaded so far on failure (or catch inside and remove them), and in `submit()`/`reply()` call a best-effort `bucket.remove(paths)` when the insert returns an error; add a spec case in user-feedback.service.spec.ts for 'insert fails → uploaded objects removed'.

findings.what: Profile locale preferences are applied only once per document: after sign-out and sign-in as another account in the same tab, the second account's preferred_lang/region are never applied, and the first account's profile values stay in memory.
findings.evidence: app.component.ts:119 `private appliedProfileLocale = false;` set true at :128 and never reset; the effect at :125-127 returns early on `!user` without clearing; locale.service.ts:130 `clearProfile()` exists but has no caller (grep across src/app).
