findings.what: The reduced-motion "Ruhepuls" for skeletons is dead code: the block re-declares `sc-breathe 2.4s infinite` for `.sc-skel/.sc-skel-line/.sc-skel-field`, but the earlier global clamp sets `animation-duration: 0.01ms !important; animation-iteration-count: 1 !important` on `*`, so the shorthand (no `!important`) is overridden and reduced-motion skeletons are static — while the comment promises they breathe.
findings.evidence: src/styles.scss:538-545 `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { *, *::before, *::after { animation-duration: 0.01ms !important; animation-iteration-count: 1 !important; …` vs :922-930 `/* Ruhepuls als gemeinsame Rueckfallebene: die Flaeche atmet … */ … .sc-skel, .sc-skel-line, .sc-skel-field { animation: sc-breathe 2.4s ease-in-out infinite; }` — cascade: `!important` longhands beat a later non-important shorthand. Same pattern at :887-889 `.sc-skel-field:not([data-neuro-ready])::after { animation: sc-breathe … }`.
findings.fix: Decide once: either delete the three `sc-breathe` re-declarations in the reduced block and reword the comment to "static" (matches the app-wide "Reduced Motion = Schnitt" policy), or mark them `!important` if the breathing is wanted.

findings.what: A draft-swapped component whose stat hydration fails stays in the pending (spinner) state for the rest of the page's life — no retry, no message, no log; the user can only reload the page to see numbers for that row.
findings.evidence: src/app/codex/codex-detail.component.ts:3021-3024 `} catch { // A failed hydration just leaves the row pending forever rather than rendering wrong numbers — Falle 2 }` and the `finally` at :3025-3031 only clears `pendingClasses` when the epoch still accepts the class, so a rejected `getEntityPayloads`/`getAmmoPayloads` (e.g. `console.error('[codex] getEntityPayloads chunk failed')` at codex.service.ts:1292 returns an empty map, a thrown transport error rejects) leaves `isDraftClassPending()` true indefinitely.
findings.fix: In the catch, `console.warn('[codex] hydrateDraftClass failed', className, err)`, remove the class from `pendingClasses` and add it to a `hydrationFailed` set; the swap row renders dashes with a small 'retry' action that calls `hydrateDraftClass` again (keeps the 'no wrong number' rule, drops the infinite spinner).

findings.what: Saving a loadout from the codex detail page ignores whether activating the freshly created config succeeded: `activateConfig` first deactivates every config of the ship and then activates the new one; if step 2 fails the ship has no active config on the server, and the page still writes the loadout into it and reports success.
findings.evidence: src/app/hangar/hangar.service.ts:671-690 `activateConfig`: `update({ is_active: false })…` then `update({ is_active: true }).eq('id', id)`; `if (error) { this.error.set(error.message); return false; }` — no rollback. src/app/codex/codex-detail.component.ts:3072 `await this.hangar.activateConfig(target.id, ship.id);` (return value unchecked, flow continues to `updateConfig` at :3083). The other caller, hangar-ship-detail.component.ts:622, does check the boolean.
findings.fix: At codex-detail.component.ts:3072 treat `false` like the createConfig failure (`saveError.set(saveErrorHangar); return;`); optionally, in `activateConfig`, re-activate the previous config when step 2 fails.

findings.what: The item picker declares `role="listbox"` on the `<ul>` but the `role="option"` elements are buttons nested inside role-less `<li>`s, so the listbox owns no options for assistive tech.
findings.evidence: src/app/hangar/hangar-item-picker.component.ts:593 `<ul class="results" role="listbox">` → :595 `<li>` → :596 `<button type="button" class="result" role="option" (click)="pick(r)">`.
findings.fix: Drop `role="listbox"`/`role="option"` (a list of real buttons is already accessible) or move `role="option"` onto the `<li>` with `role="presentation"` removed from the button.

findings.what: Hover "lift" transforms on the hangar cards and hero tiles are not scoped to `@media (hover: hover)`, so a tap on touch devices leaves the card stuck in its lifted state (R6).
findings.evidence: src/app/hangar/hangar-dashboard.component.ts:514 `.hero:hover { transform: translateY(-2px); box-shadow: … }`, :628 `.card:hover { transform: translateY(-2px); …}`; no `@media (hover: hover)` or `(pointer: coarse)` reset in the file (only :681 `.shared-toggle` sizing). Contrast starscape.component.ts:467 and :674 which scope/reset the lift.
findings.fix: Wrap the two lift rules in `@media (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine) { … }`.

findings.what: A failed quick-search request is presented as 'no results' rather than as an error, so an offline user believes the catalogue has no match.
findings.evidence: quick-search.component.ts:521-525 `catch { if (seq === this.searchSeq) { this.results.set([]); … } }` and template :103 `@else if (query() && displayResults().length === 0) { … 'quickSearch.noResults' }`.
findings.fix: Add an `error` signal set in the catch, show a `quickSearch.error` line (new de/en key) instead of noResults, cleared on the next query.

findings.what: The app never declares `color-scheme`, so whatever the platform still draws (number spinners in the column menu, the search field's clear button, autofill, form popups) renders in the light scheme on a dark UI.
findings.evidence: grep `color-scheme|prefers-color-scheme` over src/styles.scss, src/index.html and src/app → 0 hits; index.html:164 `<body class="sc-theme-dark">` (dark-only app); column-menu.component.ts:113-116 `<input type="number">`, quick-search.component.ts:77 `type="search"`.
findings.fix: Add `:root { color-scheme: dark; }` next to the scrollbar block in styles.scss and `<meta name="color-scheme" content="dark">` in index.html.

findings.what: The quick-search shortcut hint is hard-coded to one OS: it reads 'Ctrl K' on macOS although the handler binds ⌘K there.
findings.evidence: quick-search.component.ts:65 `<kbd>Ctrl K</kbd>`; :371 `if ((ev.ctrlKey || ev.metaKey) && ev.key.toLowerCase() === 'k')`.
findings.fix: Derive the modifier label once from `navigator.userAgentData?.platform ?? navigator.platform` (mac → '⌘ K', else 'Ctrl K') in a computed and bind it into the <kbd>.

findings.what: 15 of 21 functions have no test at all, including every auth gate and the public API router/limiter: api (router, auth, cors, rate-limit, 6 handlers), check-bundle, delete-user, desktop-latest, desktop-session, ingest-bundle, ingest-catalog, ingest-telemetry, invite-user, process-p4k, readme-sync, rsi-upcoming-ships, starscape-summary, uex-proxy, verify-release-token.

findings.fix: Add Deno tests for the pure parts first: api/_auth.ts hasScope/sha256Hex + router matching, api/_cors.ts origin rules, ingest-skins toolVersionAtLeast (already exported), uex-proxy safeParam, rsi-upcoming-ships normalizeName/nameCandidates/rsiThumbnails, ingest-telemetry HMAC verify.

findings.what: Two migration headers name a different file than the one they live in, so `grep` by the header name finds nothing and the ledger name in the comment is wrong.

findings.what: Five extra locale files (es/fr/pt/ru/zh) are shipped in the bundle but cover 7.4 % of the keys, carry 27 stale keys and are not offered anywhere in the UI.
findings.evidence: node flatten: each of es/fr/pt/ru/zh.json = 267 keys, 240 present in en (7.4 % of 3 252), 27 not in en any more (nav.profile, news.refresh, admin.invite.*, blueprint.category.*, hangar.roleLoadouts.slotsTitle …), 62–79 values identical to English (e.g. es `p4k.kpi.total="Total bundles"`); src/app/core/locale/locale.types.ts:13 `export type AppLanguage = 'de' | 'en'`; settings.component.ts:949 `readonly languages: readonly LangId[] = ['de', 'en']`; app.config.ts:46 `fallbackLang: 'en'`; angular.json:28-32 copies `public/**/*` so ~65 KB of dead JSON is deployed; last touch git 66bae19 (#610).

findings.what: 105 i18n keys exist in de.json/en.json that no template or service references (another 107 are only reachable through single-segment prefix helpers and were not confirmed either way).
findings.evidence: Script /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Star-Citizen-Companion-Web/5f9024c5-2d78-50f3-acdc-7f203e29ec48/scratchpad/i18n-usage.js (dotted literals + `x.${` + `'x.' +` prefixes over every non-spec src/app/**/*.ts): 212 keys unreferenced, 105 confirmed (last segment never appears quoted anywhere in src). findings.what: en.json mixes British and American spelling in visible labels, most visibly Armour vs Armor for the same concept.
findings.evidence: grep -oi 'armou?r' en.json: `armour` 14 / `armor` 12 — en.json:171 `"armor": "Armour"`, :937 `"ARMOUR"`, :1585 `"Armour"` vs :998 `"Armor stats"`, :1913 `"FPS Armor"`, :1963 `"Armor"`, :1967 `"Armor slot"`, :1985 `"No armor in this build."`; British: :1888/1890/1894 `specialisation`, :1076 `bottom centre`, :4053 `Pick a colour`, :3427 `analyse`, :3360/3418 `Cancelled`, :2346 `labelled`; American: `favorite` ×11, `catalog` ×13, `customiz`, `organiz`.

findings.what: Four German legal/privacy strings open with a typographic „ and close with a straight " (mixed quotation marks).
findings.evidence: public/i18n/de.json:3035 `„Mit Google fortfahren\"`, :3049 `„Präferenzen\"`, :3050 `„Statistik\"`, :3061 `„Anmeldung mit Google\"`; elsewhere de.json uses „…“ (28 lines) and \"…\" (12 lines) consistently per string.

findings.what: The same object is called "Set" on the codex pages, "Rollen-Loadout"/"Role loadouts" in the hangar and "kit" in the public docs.

findings.what: Docs still present `/codex/blueprint` as its own list page; since 0.103.0 it redirects to the Index kind tab.
findings.evidence: docs/readme-io/pages/docs/features/codex.md:185 `\`/codex/blueprint\` lists the game's **crafting blueprints**` vs CHANGELOG 0.103.0 `Die Blueprint-Liste steckt jetzt im Index. \`/codex/blueprint\` führt zum Index mit Blueprint-Filter` (REQ-11).

findings.what: README stack badge still says Angular 21 while the project (and the README's own subtitle) is on Angular 22; the release version itself is consistent everywhere.
findings.evidence: README.md:9 `stack-Angular%2021%20…` vs README.md:6 'Built with Angular 22 PWA' and package.json:61 `@angular/core ^22.2.0`. Version 0.103.1 matches in package.json:3, README.md:3, CHANGELOG.md:8 `## [0.103.1] - 2026-09-26`, public/release-notes.json:3 `"current": "0.103.1"` (regenerated in scratchpad: byte-identical).
findings.fix: Change the badge text in README.md:9 to `Angular%2022`.

findings.what: The BrowserWindow has no `will-navigate` guard, so a file or URL dropped onto the window navigates the app away from its renderer (Chromium default drag-and-drop navigation) until restart; only `window.open` is intercepted.
findings.evidence: data-uploader/src/main/index.ts:189-205 `mainWindow.webContents.setWindowOpenHandler(({ url }) => { … return { action: 'deny' }; })` is the only navigation hook — grep for `will-navigate|will-redirect|will-attach-webview|setPermissionRequestHandler` across src/: 0 hits. Sandbox + contextIsolation are on (index.ts:156-159), so the impact is loss of the UI, not Node access.
findings.fix: In createWindow() add `mainWindow.webContents.on('will-navigate', (e, url) => { if (!url.startsWith('file:') && url !== process.env['ELECTRON_RENDERER_URL']) e.preventDefault(); })` and (optionally) a `setPermissionRequestHandler` that denies everything.

findings.what: The OAuth loopback page reflects the POSTed `error` field into HTML without escaping — HTML injection into the "connect failed" page (mitigated by the CSRF `state` check, so only a party holding the state can trigger it).
findings.evidence:
data-uploader/src/lib/oauth.ts:184 `res.end(renderPage('SC Data Uploader · Fehler', body.error ?? 'Kein Token erhalten.', false));` and :270-272 `

${title}

${body}

` (no escaping); state is validated first at :176.
findings.fix: Escape `&<>"'` in renderPage() (a five-line replace map) before interpolating `body`, or clamp `body.error` to a fixed set of known codes.

findings.what: Two Phase-1 demo stubs (a synthetic extraction that sleeps and emits fake ship names, and a placeholder validator) still ship in src/lib with no consumer.
findings.evidence: data-uploader/src/lib/extractor.ts (239 lines) header "Extractor — Phase 2 stub … no real parsing is happening yet", :224 `note: 'phase-1 demo — real extraction in phase 2'`; src/lib/validator.ts:49 `warnings: … ['phase-1 heuristic only — replace with real schema in phase 2']`; grep `lib/extractor|lib/validator|from './extractor|from './validator` over src/ and test/: only validator.ts:13 importing extractor.ts and a doc comment in python-bridge.ts:57 — no runtime consumer, no spec.
findings.fix: Delete src/lib/extractor.ts and src/lib/validator.ts and reword the python-bridge.ts:57 comment to point at `PythonExtractEvent` alone.

findings.what: The main process is essentially untested: of 14 src/main modules only catalog-bridge and skin-ingest are imported by any spec; the 40+ IPC handlers, the updater (beyond semver), python/skin/silhouette bridges, session, logging, tray and throttle have no coverage.
findings.evidence: grep `from '../src/main/` in data-uploader/test/: only test/skin-ingest.spec.ts (skin-ingest), test/upload-resume.spec.ts and test/upload-token-refresh.spec.ts (catalog-bridge); src/main/index.ts is 1286 lines with `ipcMain.handle/on` at 216-1170; 30 vitest specs cover src/lib and two main modules; python/tests has 34 files run by CI (workflow :66).
findings.fix: Extract the pure parts of updater.ts (event mapping, downgrade gate), python-bridge.ts (argv building like silhouette-bridge-args.ts, stdout line parsing) and the settings-patch whitelist of index.ts into src/lib modules with specs; keep Electron-bound glue thin.

findings.what: de.json and en.json drift by one key pair (`common.tempo` only in en, `run.tempo` only in de) and neither key is referenced by the renderer.
findings.evidence: Key diff: en 283 / de 283, de missing `common.tempo`, de extra `run.tempo` (data-uploader/src/i18n/en.json:6 `"tempo": "Tempo"` under common, de.json:95 under run); grep `common.tempo|run.tempo|.tempo'` in src/renderer/: 0 hits (only comments mention tempo).
findings.fix: Remove the unused key from both files, or move de's `run.tempo` to `common.tempo` so the two dictionaries have identical key sets.

findings.what: Colour literals instead of tokens: an amber `#f0b35c` badge duplicated in two files, GitHub-palette hex tags on the release notes, and `rgba(0,212,255,…)`/`rgba(248,113,113,…)` accent/danger tints hard-coded in eleven components.
findings.evidence: src/app/hangar/hangar-dashboard.component.ts:604-608 `.badge.preliminary { … color: #f0b35c; border: 1px solid color-mix(in srgb, #f0b35c 45%, transparent) }` and hangar-import.component.ts:160 `.badge.fuzzy { color: #f0b35c; …}`; src/app/release-notes/release-notes.component.ts:877-882 `.tag-added { color: #3fb950 } .tag-fixed { color: #d29922 } .tag-removed { color: #f85149 } .tag-deprecated { color: #db6d28 } .tag-security { color: #a371f7 }`; accent tint `rgba(0, 212, 255, 0.25)` in settings.component.ts:705,746, friends.component.ts:332, feedback-area-picker.component.ts:1247,1252, release-notes.component.ts:831,840,857, p4k-history.component.ts:274,334,339; danger tint `rgba(248, 113, 113, 0.1)` in settings:493,770,777, friends:312, loadout-share-panel:1070, desktop-download:965, download:1328, p4k-history:254,301, user-feedback-panel:322. Tokens exist: `--sc-warning`, `--sc-accent`, `--sc-danger`, `--sc-success` (src/styles.scss:23-36).
findings.fix: Replace with `color-mix(in srgb, var(--sc-warning|--sc-accent|--sc-danger) N%, transparent)`; map the release-note tags onto `--sc-success/--sc-accent/--sc-warning/--sc-danger/--sc-fg-2`.

findings.what: Several failure paths are swallowed with neither a log line nor a signal: a refused slot write, a failed vote write (rolled back silently), failed single-row hangar reads and the desktop-connection RPC — nothing greppable is left for support.
findings.evidence: src/app/hangar/hangar.service.ts:789 `if (read.error || !read.data) return null;`, :804 `if (write.error) return null;`, :372 and :733 `if (error || !data) return null;`; src/app/starscape/starscape-votes.service.ts:139-143 `catch { this.applyLocal(imageId, had); }`; src/app/desktop/desktop-connection.service.ts:302 `if (error) return; // silent`, :316-318 `catch { /* offline */ }`, :337-339; src/app/social/account-status.service.ts:274-277 `catch { … }`. Only 7 `console.warn` calls exist in the whole area (settings:1299,1312; starscape.service:317; votes:235; desktop-session.util:43,52,61).
findings.fix: Add a `console.warn('[hangar] slot write refused', { id, slot })`-style line (or the app's logger, if one is introduced) at each swallow point, keeping the UX silent.

findings.what: The Holotable's radar sweep and the selected pin's ping loop forever, and keep running while the table is scrolled out of view (the ports list and perspectives sit below it); the SVG-fallback figure's holo sweep does the same when WebGL is unavailable.
findings.evidence: src/app/codex/holo/codex-holo-table.component.ts:181-184 `.sweep { … animation: holo-sweep 12s linear infinite; will-change: rotate; }`, :277-279 `.pin.sel i::before { … animation: pin-ping 1.6s var(--e-out) infinite; }`; src/app/codex/codex-board-figure.component.ts:319-325 `.pd-scan { display: block; animation: pd-sweep 9s linear infinite; }`; no IntersectionObserver / `animation-play-state` toggle in either file.
findings.fix: Pause the loops with an `IntersectionObserver` on the table host that toggles a `.parked` class setting `animation-play-state: paused` (the reduced-motion cut already stops them).

findings.what: Text inputs are 15px on touch devices, so iOS Safari zooms the page on every focus (R6: inputs below 16px).
findings.evidence: styles.scss:485 `font-size: 15px` on html/body; styles.scss:650-660 `.sc-input { … font: inherit; }` (15px); quick-search.component.ts:195 `.qs-input … font-size: 1rem` (15px); column-menu.component.ts:168 inputs at 11px; no `16px` rule for inputs anywhere (grep). index.html:7 viewport has no maximum-scale (correctly), so the zoom happens.
findings.fix: In styles.scss add `@media (pointer: coarse) { input:not([type='checkbox']):not([type='radio']), textarea, select { font-size: max(16px, 1em); } }`.

findings.what: Admin telemetry numbers use Angular's DecimalPipe with the default en-US locale (no LOCALE_ID provided), so a German UI shows `1,234` while every other page formats through the locale service.
findings.evidence: src/app/admin/telemetry-stats.component.ts:7 `import { DecimalPipe } from '@angular/common'` and 30 `| number` usages (:142, :150-152, :181-184, :288 `| number:'1.0-0'`); `grep -rn LOCALE_ID src/` → no provider; the rest of the app uses `new Intl.NumberFormat(this.locale.intlLocale(), …)` (news/patch-monitor.component.ts:373, patch-cadence.component.ts:570, patch-cycle.component.ts:419) or `formatNumber(v, locale)` (codex/codex-format.ts:256).
findings.fix: Either provide `{ provide: LOCALE_ID, useFactory: () => inject(LocaleService).intlLocale() }` in app.config.ts (with registerLocaleData for de) or replace the `| number` pipes in telemetry-stats with a small `fmt()` helper using `Intl.NumberFormat(this.locale.intlLocale())`.

findings.what: CSP script-src and frame-src allow https://accounts.google.com although the client never loads a Google script or frames Google (sign-in is a full-page redirect via supabase signInWithOAuth); accounts.google.com hosts JSONP endpoints and is a documented CSP-bypass source.
findings.evidence: vercel.json:23 `script-src 'self' 'wasm-unsafe-eval' https://accounts.google.com https://eu-assets.i.posthog.com` and `frame-src https://accounts.google.com https://*.supabase.co`; grep 'gsi/client|accounts.google.com|google.accounts|signInWithIdToken|skipBrowserRedirect' over src/app + src/index.html (non-spec) → 0 hits; src/app/auth/auth.service.ts:114 `signInWithOAuth({ provider: 'google', options: { redirectTo: ... } })` (redirect flow, no embedded script)
findings.fix: Remove `https://accounts.google.com` from script-src and frame-src in vercel.json (keep it in connect-src only if a live check shows supabase-js contacting it, otherwise drop it there too); verify Google sign-in on a preview deployment.

findings.what: connect-src grants two origins nothing in the client fetches: http://127.0.0.1:* (the loopback hand-off is a top-level form POST covered by form-action; the fetch() path was retired with Desktop-Tool 0.4.6) and https://api.star-citizen.wiki (only called from the fetch-verse-news edge function).
findings.evidence: vercel.json:23 `connect-src 'self' blob: ... http://127.0.0.1:* ... https://api.star-citizen.wiki ...`; grep '127.0.0.1' in non-spec src/app → only src/app/desktop/loopback.util.ts:27 (validation, no fetch); src/app/desktop/desktop-auth.component.ts:202-206 'NOT a background fetch() ... The earlier fetch() approach (Desktop-Tool ≤ 0.4.5) died silently'; grep -rl 'star-citizen.wiki' src → 0 files, hits only in supabase/functions/fetch-verse-news/{index,comm-link-url}.ts
findings.fix: Drop `http://127.0.0.1:*` and `https://api.star-citizen.wiki` from connect-src in vercel.json (leave `form-action 'self' http://127.0.0.1:*` untouched — the hand-off needs it); re-run scripts/check-csp-connect-src.mjs.

findings.what: CSP connect-src/img-src/frame-src use the wildcard https://*.supabase.co (and wss://*.supabase.co) although the app talks to exactly one project; the wildcard lets an injected script exfiltrate to any attacker-owned Supabase project or frame one.
findings.evidence: vercel.json:23 `img-src ... https://*.supabase.co`, `connect-src ... https://*.supabase.co wss://*.supabase.co`, `frame-src ... https://*.supabase.co`; src/environments/environment.prod.ts:5 `url: 'https://hcnqhvzlavdycidqyaai.supabase.co'` (single fixed host, no preview/branch project in fileReplacements angular.json:65-69)
findings.fix: Pin the three directives to `https://hcnqhvzlavdycidqyaai.supabase.co` / `wss://hcnqhvzlavdycidqyaai.supabase.co` in vercel.json; extend scripts/check-csp-connect-src.mjs to fail on `*.supabase.co`.

findings.what: `npm audit` reports 2 moderate advisories, both dev-only and both with a non-breaking fix available: qs 6.15.3 reached through karma → body-parser 1.20.6.
findings.evidence: baseline/npm-audit.json: `qs` (node_modules/qs, range 2.2.5–6.15.3) — GHSA-x5fp-wj9c-mxmx 'array-limit bypass via bracket-key comma parsing' (CVSS 3.7) and GHSA-4mjr-xmp4-gh2g 'Denial of Service via Attacker Controlled isBuffer' (CVSS 5.3); effect chain `karma/node_modules/body-parser` 1.20.5–1.20.6; `fixAvailable: true` on both; metadata high=0 critical=0. karma is a devDependency (package.json:90), nothing reaches the browser bundle.
findings.fix: Run `npm audit fix` (moves qs to ≥6.16.0 in package-lock.json only) or add `"qs": "^6.16.0"` to `overrides` in package.json.

findings.what: `sc-news-thumb` takes its channel glyph as a plain string input and passes it straight through `bypassSecurityTrustHtml`, so the trust decision lives in the child while the constant lives in the parent — a latent XSS sink for any future caller that binds feed data.
findings.evidence: src/app/news/news-thumb.component.ts:509 `readonly channelIcon = input('');`, :520-522 `readonly safeChannelIcon = computed<SafeHtml>(() => this.sanitizer.bypassSecurityTrustHtml(this.channelIcon()))`; the only caller passes compile-time constants (src/app/news/news-list.component.ts:1196-1204 `iconFor`).
findings.fix: Change the input to `input<SafeHtml | null>(null)` and pass `safeIcon(item.channel)` (already exists in news-list), or accept only the `channel` key and resolve the constant SVG inside the thumb.

findings.what: User-facing strings produced in the main process bypass i18n: the folder-picker title is German only, the Windows shutdown notice is English only, and the OAuth loopback pages are German only with `lang="de"`, regardless of the operator's language.
findings.evidence: data-uploader/src/main/index.ts:450 `title: 'Star-Citizen-Channel-Ordner wählen',`; index.ts:376 `shutdown /s /t ${secs} /c "Star Citizen Companion: upload complete."`; src/lib/oauth.ts:143 `renderPage('SC Data Uploader · Fehler', 'Anfrage zu groß.', false)`, :178 `'CSRF-Mismatch — versuch es erneut.'`, :191 `'Du kannst dieses Fenster schließen.'`, :219 `'Bitte den Login im Data Uploader Fenster starten.'`, :263 `<html lang="de">`. The tray already has a label-push channel for this (index.ts:396 `sc:tray:labels`).
findings.fix: Extend the existing `sc:tray:labels` push (preload TrayLabelPush) with `pickFolderTitle`, `shutdownNotice` and the four loopback-page strings resolved by the renderer's dictionary, and read them in index.ts / pass them into runOAuthFlow(); set the page `lang` from the active locale.

findings.what: Native `window.confirm()` / `window.prompt()` dialogs (OS look, R0) are used for account deletion and for the bundle disable/re-enable/delete actions.
findings.evidence: src/app/settings/settings.component.ts:1340 `if (!window.confirm(msg)) return;`; src/app/p4k/p4k-history.component.ts:458 `window.prompt(this.translate.instant('p4k.prompts.disable', …))`, :465 and :471 `window.confirm(...)`. Friends already argues against it (friends.component.ts:243-245).
findings.fix: Inline two-step confirm as in hangar-dashboard (`confirmDeleteId`) for the three p4k actions and the account delete; for the disable reason use a small inline text field next to the confirm button.

findings.what: After an in-place language switch the set-page eyebrow ("Rüstung 3/6", role name), the landing stage captions, the Holotable Einsatz sub-lines and readings, and the bridge freshness line stay in the old language because their `computed()` strings call `t.instant` without reading a language signal.
findings.evidence: src/app/codex/set/codex-set-stage.component.ts:372-375 `readonly roleLabel = computed(() => this.t.instant('hangar.roles.' + this.set().role))` / `equipSuffix = computed(() => '· ' + this.t.instant('codex.stage.armorEquipped', …))` (the component has a `lang` signal at :363 but neither reads it); src/app/codex/codex-landing.component.ts:644,713,717-727 (`stageShipTitle`, `stagePersonTitle`, `stagePersonRoleLabel`, `stagePersonEquipSuffix`); src/app/codex/holo/codex-holo-stage.component.ts:1320-1323 `sub = this.t.instant('codex.holo.stage.portsCount', …)` and :1678-1690 `sayFor` inside `perspectiveTiles`; src/app/codex/codex-bridge.component.ts:749; the app switches with `translate.use(lang)` in place (src/app/app.component.ts:151,159 — no reload). Correct pattern exists in codex-swap-picker.component.ts:840 `this.lang();`.
findings.fix: Read a language signal inside each affected computed (set-stage already has `lang`; give landing/holo-stage/bridge a `signal(toLang(t.getCurrentLang()))` fed by `onLangChange`) or move the strings into the template behind `| translate`.

findings.what: REQ-9 has no test: nothing asserts the hangar role/pin pickers and the rank card's scope picker are `sc-select` with per-option disabled — the two hangar pages that host them have no spec.
findings.evidence: `grep -rln 'sc-select\|ScSelect' src/app/hangar --include=*.spec.ts` → 0 (sc-select is used in hangar-dashboard.component.ts, hangar-ship-detail.component.ts, codex-rank-card.component.ts); codex-rank-card.component.spec.ts has no `sc-select`/scope assertion (it titles at :20-146).
findings.fix: Add a spec like codex-list.component.spec.ts:207 ("offers its facets as themed selects — a native one opens as an unthemed OS menu") for hangar-dashboard (role + pin picker) and extend codex-rank-card.component.spec.ts with a scope-picker `sc-select` + disabled-option assertion.

findings.what: Quick-search 'add to hangar' shows neither a busy nor a failure state: a failed insert leaves the button unchanged with no message, and a double click fires two inserts.
findings.evidence: quick-search.component.ts:501-504 `async addToHangar(ev, row) { ev.stopPropagation(); await this.hangar.addShip(row.classNameSlug, 'owned'); }` — hangar.service.ts:240-243 returns `null` and sets `this.error` on failure, which nothing in the quick-search template reads (:145-154).
findings.fix: Track an `adding` signal (Set of slugs) to disable the row's button while in flight and render `hangar.error()` under the results list when addShip returns null.

findings.what: ingest-catalog's `preview` op writes to the public `codex-previews` bucket at a key built from two unvalidated client strings (`build_number`, `name`), unlike ingest-skins' SAFE_ID discipline; a seed-token or collaborator caller can place objects at arbitrary keys (`../`, nested folders, non-webp names served as image/webp).
findings.evidence: ingest-catalog/index.ts:279-284 `const build = String(body.build_number ?? '').trim(); const name = String(body.name ?? '').trim(); … const path = `${build}/${name}`;` then :285-287 `.upload(path, bytes, { contentType: 'image/webp', upsert: true })`. Contrast ingest-skins/index.ts:57 `const SAFE_ID = /^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$/;` and :170-172.
findings.fix: In the `preview` op reject `build` and `name` that do not match `/^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$/` (400 `unsafe_id`), and require `name` to end in `.webp`.

findings.what: patch-stability-sample's operator gate compares the service-role key with a plain `!==` (not constant-time) and only accepts the legacy JWT-form key as `Bearer <key>`, so an `sb_secret_*`-keyed project cannot use `?force=1`/`?backfill=1` at all, while readme-sync already accepts both forms.
findings.evidence: patch-stability-sample/index.ts:375-378 `const authHeader = req.headers.get('authorization'); if (authHeader !== `Bearer ${SERVICE_KEY}`) { return json({ ok: false, error: 'operator paths require the service role' }, 401); }`. readme-sync/index.ts:109-111 `bearer === serviceKey || jwtRole(bearer) === 'service_role'`.
findings.fix: Reuse readme-sync's check (exact secret OR `role: service_role` claim, since the gate is off here compare the secret with a timing-safe byte comparison as concept-page/index.ts:127 does).

findings.what: ingest-catalog's `finalize` ignores the result of the `entity_counts` update, so a failed write is neither logged nor reported while the build is still promoted to current.
findings.evidence: ingest-catalog/index.ts:360-362 `if (body.entity_counts) { await admin.from('codex_builds').update({ entity_counts: body.entity_counts }).eq('id', buildId); }` — no `error` destructured; the following rpc at :363-364 does `if (error) throw error`.
findings.fix: Destructure `{ error: countsErr }` and `throw countsErr` (the catch at :369 maps it to 500 `ingest_failed`) or at least `console.error('finalize: entity_counts update failed', buildId, countsErr.message)`.

findings.what: The ship rank card and the set rank card are structural twins (same radar SVG API and 34 shared style rules) implemented separately.
findings.evidence: src/app/codex/codex-rank-card.component.ts (537 lines, selector sc-codex-rank-card) and src/app/codex/set/codex-set-rank-card.component.ts (320 lines, sc-codex-set-rank-card): both define ringPoints(), spokePoints(), vertexAt(), axisCaptions, profile/profiles, result, rings, loading with differing bodies; 34 identical CSS selectors; no literal 10-line cluster (renamed copy).
findings.fix: Extract <sc-percentile-radar [axes] [rings]> (SVG polygon/spokes/vertex maths) and a shared .rank-card style block; both cards keep their profile pickers and limiting-piece text.

findings.what: Layer inversions: core imports a feature, shared imports codex, and codex⇄hangar are mutually dependent (49 edges).
findings.evidence: src/app/core/supabase.client.ts:4 `import { ImpersonationService } from '../auth/impersonation.service'` (core → auth, value import used at :35/:95); src/app/shared/column-menu.component.ts:17 `import { ColumnFacet, ColumnKind, SortDir } from '../codex/table-column-menu'` (shared → codex); feature graph: codex → hangar 33 edges (hangar/loadout-stats.ts imported by 8 codex files, hangar/hangar.types.ts by 12, hangar.service.ts by 9) and hangar → codex 16 edges; feedback → admin 7 edges (user-feedback-panel imports admin/feedback/feedback-composer + feedback-attachments) vs admin → feedback 20; auth ⇄ social, auth ⇄ core, codex ⇄ news, codex ⇄ social, hangar ⇄ social also 2-cycles.
findings.fix: Move hangar/loadout-stats.ts and the slot/loadout types of hangar.types.ts into codex (they describe codex payloads) so hangar depends on codex only; move table-column-menu.ts next to shared/column-menu.component.ts; lift the viewAs signal into core (core/view-as.ts) so supabase.client.ts stops importing auth; move feedback-composer/attachments from admin/feedback to feedback/ (they are used by plain users).

findings.what: The initial session read has no error branch and the guards poll `ready()` without any timeout: if `getSession()` rejects and no INITIAL_SESSION event follows, every guarded navigation hangs on the boot splash with no message (RoleService.waitReady, by contrast, times out after 5 s).
findings.evidence: auth.service.ts:50-53 `this.sb.realClient.auth.getSession().then(({ data }) => { …; this._ready.set(true); });` (no .catch); auth.guard.ts:16-26 loop has no upper bound; role.service.ts:302-329 shows the timeout pattern already used elsewhere.
findings.fix: Add `.catch(() => this._ready.set(true))` (treat as signed-out) on the getSession chain and a 10 s upper bound in the shared whenReady() helper that resolves as not-ready.

findings.what: Hover glows use the retired accent colour: 14 rules hard-code rgba(0, 212, 255, …) (#00d4ff) while the StarUI token the app now aliases is #52c1e6 (`--accent-primary-rgb: 82, 193, 230`), plus other literal colours where rgb tokens exist.
findings.evidence: grep `rgba(0, 212, 255` → 14 hits across shell.component.ts (e.g. :401 `.nav a &:hover … rgba(0, 212, 255, 0.08)`, :484-487, :493-497), quick-search.component.ts:197, login.component.ts (preview-locked notice), feedback-fab/user-feedback-fab; node_modules/@starorga/star-ui/lib/design-tokens.css:22-23 `--accent-primary: #52c1e6; --accent-primary-rgb: 82, 193, 230`; styles.scss already uses `rgba(var(--accent-primary-rgb), …)` (:713-716). Also impersonation-banner.component.ts:79,109,110,123 `#10060a` literal ×4; success/danger literals `rgba(74,222,128,…)`/`rgba(248,113,113,…)` in login/set-password/password-form.
findings.fix: Mechanically replace `rgba(0, 212, 255, a)` → `rgba(var(--accent-primary-rgb), a)`, `rgba(255, 87, 34, a)` → `rgba(var(--accent-hot-rgb), a)`, `rgba(74, 222, 128, a)` → `rgba(var(--status-success-rgb), a)`, `#10060a` → `var(--sc-bg-0)`; add a `--accent-danger-rgb` alias in styles.scss for the danger tints.

findings.what: Hover styles are not wrapped in `@media (hover: hover)` anywhere in the shell/auth/shared layer, so a tap on touch devices leaves sticky hover colours (nav entries, avatar, search trigger, footer links, select trigger, segments).
findings.evidence: Only one `@media (hover: hover)` exists in the whole app (starscape.component.ts:467). In scope: shell.component.ts:401 `&:hover { color: var(--sc-accent); … }`, :484 `.avatar-btn:hover`, quick-search.component.ts:173/206/222/240, footer.component.ts:243/265/282, public-layout.component.ts:77, sc-select.component.ts:118, segmented-control.component.ts:492, login.component.ts `.linkish:hover`, `.trust-links a:hover`.
findings.fix: Wrap the `:hover` rules in `@media (hover: hover)` (R6 mechanical fix) file by file; keep `:focus-visible` rules outside.

findings.what: The import preview hard-codes German-style quotation marks around the ship nickname (opening „ with a straight closing "), which renders identically in the English UI.
findings.evidence: src/app/hangar/hangar-import.component.ts:105 `@if (e.customName) { „{{ e.customName }}" }`.
findings.fix: Add `hangar.import.nick` (`„{{name}}“` in de.json, `“{{name}}”` in en.json) and render `{{ 'hangar.import.nick' | translate: { name: e.customName } }}`.

findings.what: About 40 icon-only buttons (close ✕/×, back ←, prev/next ‹ ›, clear, rename ✎, pin, minimize, colour swatches) carry an aria-label but no scTooltip, although the project convention gives close buttons a tooltip (CHANGELOG: "Inspector-Schließen hat einen Tooltip mit Esc").
findings.evidence: Button scan: 418 <button>s, 65 icon-only, 46 without scTooltip (minus 6 with their own aria-describedby tip). Samples per feature — codex: src/app/codex/codex-swap-picker.component.ts:201 `.pick-close` ✕, :393/:400/:407 chip-remove ✕, src/app/codex/codex-compare-tray.component.ts:51 `.chip-x`, src/app/codex/codex-weapon-detail.component.ts:89 `.wd-close`, src/app/codex/holo/codex-holo-inspector.component.ts:36, src/app/codex/holo/codex-holo-hangar.component.ts:100 `.hh-back` ←, src/app/codex/codex-landing.component.ts:235 `.pin`, src/app/codex/codex-bridge.component.ts:94 `.scanner-clear`; hangar: src/app/hangar/hangar-ship-detail.component.ts:88 `.icon-btn` ✎, src/app/hangar/hangar-dashboard.component.ts:324, src/app/hangar/hangar-import.component.ts:61, src/app/hangar/hangar-item-picker.component.ts:50; news: src/app/news/patch-board.component.ts:113, src/app/news/patch-dossier.component.ts:293; shell: src/app/shell/feedback-fab.component.ts:65/:95/:120, src/app/shell/user-feedback-fab.component.ts:59, src/app/shell/footer.component.ts:33/:38; admin: src/app/admin/feedback/admin-feedback.component.ts:285/:468/:728/:731/:936/:990, src/app/admin/feedback/feedback-attachments.component.ts:131/:195/:244/:290/:300; desktop: src/app/desktop/app-download-menu.component.ts:122, src/app/desktop/desktop-download.component.ts:110; starscape: src/app/starscape/starscape.component.ts:373.
findings.fix: Add `[scTooltip]` with the same expression as the aria-label (mechanically derivable); Info tier for universal glyphs (✕ × ‹ › ←), Label tier for ✎ / pin / swatch / minimize (criterion a).

findings.what: The Holotable strip's four "fact" explanations use a hand-rolled hover box instead of scTooltip: no delay tiers, no Escape, no long-press; and the trigger is display:none at ≤640px, so on phones the explanation is unreachable.
findings.evidence: src/app/codex/holo/codex-holo-strip.component.ts:161-177 `<span class="tipw fact"><button type="button" class="tip-trigger">…` ×4; :388-394 `.tipbox { display: block; visibility: hidden; opacity: 0; … } .tipw:hover .tipbox, .tipw:focus-within .tipbox { visibility: visible; opacity: 1; }`; :483 `.tip-trigger { display: none; }` inside `@media (max-width: 640px)`.
findings.fix: Replace `.tipw/.tipbox` with `[scTooltip]="factText" scTooltipTier="label"` on the `.tip-trigger` button (criterion c: it explains a value the user inspects) and keep the trigger visible on phones (long-press opens it).

findings.what: Spacing is written as literals almost everywhere (23 padding/gap declarations use the `--sc-pad-*`/`--sc-gap-*` tokens vs 1 722 literals); per component type the values cluster well, but a handful of outliers break the sibling rule — most visibly the three auth/desktop cards at 32px 36px against a card median of 14px.
findings.evidence: node scan of all inline styles (median / Q1 / Q3 / IQR, outlier = |v−median| > 1.5·IQR): card padding n=25 median 14 (12–20, IQR 8) → outliers src/app/auth/access-unavailable.component.ts:48 `.sc-card { padding: 32px 36px }`, src/app/desktop/desktop-auth.component.ts:73 and src/app/desktop/desktop-read-auth.component.ts:68 (same), src/app/admin/feedback/admin-feedback.component.ts:1174 `.card-head { padding: 0 }`; card gap n=26 median 8 (IQR 2) → src/app/admin/api-tokens/api-tokens.component.ts:252 `.conn-card` 16px, src/app/auth/set-password.component.ts:91 `.card` 14px, src/app/codex/codex-weapon-detail.component.ts:128 `.val-card` 2px; dialog gap n=16 median 8 (IQR 2) → src/app/codex/holo/codex-holo-strip.component.ts:396 `.hs-panel` 22px, src/app/codex/codex-component-modal.component.ts:201 `.cm-panel` 14px; toolbar gap n=95 median 10 (IQR 4) → src/app/shell/shell.component.ts:329 `.topbar` 24px, src/app/starscape/starscape.component.ts:384 `.head` 18px; row gap n=56 median 8 → src/app/p4k/p4k-history.component.ts:336 `.up-row` 16px; toolbar font-size n=45 median 11.5px → four `*-head h2` at 1.05rem (codex-bridge:409, codex-landing:432, codex-weapon-detail:120, upcoming-grid:171) and hangar-import-page:99 h1 1.25rem; border-radius and row padding show no outliers. Whole-repo: padding n=831 median 6, gap n=869 median 8, border-radius n=573 median 6, font-size n=1218 median 11.8px.
findings.fix: Do not auto-snap (> 3 outliers per property). Snap the three 32px-36px `.sc-card` overrides to the global `.sc-card` padding (src/styles.scss:585ff, density level 1) and the two dialog gaps to 8–12px; leave the topbar/starscape head as deliberate. Longer term, route new padding/gap through `--sc-pad-*`/`--sc-gap-*`.

findings.what: One local scrollbar style diverges from the global one (own height and thumb literals, no hover accent), and five horizontal chip strips hide their scrollbar entirely, leaving a mouse user no cue that the strip scrolls.
findings.evidence: Global (tokens, once): src/styles.scss:557-580 `* { scrollbar-width: thin; scrollbar-color: var(--sc-border) transparent; } ::-webkit-scrollbar { width: 10px; height: 10px } …thumb { background: var(--sc-border); border-radius: 999px; border: 2px solid transparent } …thumb:hover { background: var(--sc-accent) }`. Diverging: src/app/codex/codex-bridge.component.ts:426-429 `scrollbar-width: thin; … .lane-track::-webkit-scrollbar { height: 8px; } .lane-track::-webkit-scrollbar-thumb { background: var(--sc-border); border-radius: 999px; }`. Hidden bars: src/app/shared/segmented-control.component.ts:124-126, src/app/codex/holo/codex-holo-stage.component.ts:597-598, src/app/codex/holo/codex-holo-strip.component.ts:329-330, src/app/settings/settings.component.ts:822-826, src/app/news/patch-dossier.component.ts:570-571 (`scrollbar-width: none; ::-webkit-scrollbar { display: none; }`).
findings.fix: Delete the `.lane-track::-webkit-scrollbar*` block in codex-bridge (the global one applies); for the five hidden strips either keep the bar (inherit) or add an edge fade / arrow cue so the overflow is discoverable with a mouse.

findings.what: desktop-auth and desktop-read-auth are the same component copied (80 identical lines, identical member set), without specs.
findings.evidence: src/app/desktop/desktop-auth.component.ts (247 lines) ↔ desktop-read-auth.component.ts (232 lines): clusters 98-134↔92-124 (37 lines), 65-92↔60-87 (28), 219-233↔193-207 (15); identical members route, sb, conn, translate, imp, status, errorMsg, cb, state, returnUrl, ngOnInit; routed at app.routes.ts:315,:333 (auth) and :425 (read-auth); no desktop-auth*.spec.ts exists (ls src/app/desktop/*.spec.ts).
findings.fix: One DesktopAuthComponent with route data { scope: 'write' | 'read' } (app.routes.ts:425 passes scope: 'read'); the read variant's differing copy/handoff lines become a branch on scope. Add one spec covering both scopes.

findings.what: Icon-only close/clear/remove buttons carry an aria-label but no app tooltip (R1: an icon-only control gets a Label-tier `scTooltip`; the sibling controls in codex-list/fps-list do).
findings.evidence: codex-compare-tray.component.ts:46-47 `<button … class="chip-x" … [attr.aria-label]="'codex.compare.remove' | translate">×</button>` (component imports no ScTooltipDirective, :37); extension-promo.component.ts:27-28 `class="close" … [attr.aria-label]="'extension.promo.dismiss' | translate">✕`; codex-weapon-detail.component.ts:84-85 `.wd-close` aria-label only; upcoming-grid.component.ts:38-39 `.search-clear` aria-label only. Contrast: codex-list.component.ts:151-153 `.search-clear` has `[scTooltip]`, codex-component-modal.component.ts:97 `.cm-close` has `[scTooltip]`.
findings.fix: Import ScTooltipDirective in the four components and add `[scTooltip]="<same key> | translate" scTooltipTier="label"` next to each aria-label (text mechanically derived from the existing key).

findings.what: Eight chip rows announce themselves as ARIA radio groups but every radio is its own Tab stop and arrow keys do nothing, and the Holotable's mobile tabs use `role="tab"` without a tablist/tabpanel wiring — screen-reader users are promised a keyboard model the components do not implement.
findings.evidence: src/app/codex/set/codex-set-rank-card.component.ts:36-49 `<div class="profile-row" role="radiogroup"> … <button role="radio" … (click)=…>` (no keydown handling); src/app/codex/set/codex-set-mission-bar.component.ts:343-364; src/app/codex/codex-mission-bar.component.ts:440-455; src/app/codex/holo/codex-holo-stage.component.ts:270-286 rolebar, :209-212 `<div class="mobile-tabs" role="tablist"><button type="button" role="tab" …>` (no `aria-controls`, no `role="tabpanel"`); src/app/codex/codex-energy-dock.component.ts:147-160,331-336; src/app/codex/holo/codex-holo-strip.component.ts:204-210; src/app/codex/codex-rank-card.component.ts:128-152. The shared `sc-segmented` already implements roving tabindex + arrow keys (codex-swap-picker.component.ts:493-494 comment).

findings.what: Several transitions animate layout properties (width, grid-template-columns, translate+width) rather than transform/opacity, so the rank bars, the picker fly-out, the Holotable rail collapse and the Einsatz ink reflow on every frame.
findings.evidence: src/app/codex/set/codex-set-rank-card.component.ts:208 `transition: width 500ms cubic-bezier(…)`; src/app/codex/codex-rank-card.component.ts:321,325 `transition: width 500ms …; animation: bar-grow 700ms` / `@keyframes bar-grow { from { width: 0; } }`; src/app/codex/stage/hangar-picker.component.ts:555 `transition: width .24s ease, opacity .2s ease`; src/app/codex/holo/codex-holo-stage.component.ts:542 `transition: grid-template-columns 360ms var(--e-io)` (three-column reflow of the whole frame), :625 `transition: translate 340ms …, width 340ms …`. Reduced-motion blocks exist in every file.
findings.fix: Animate the bars with `transform: scaleX()` on a left-anchored fill, the picker chain with `clip-path`/`transform`, and the rail collapse with a transform on the rail plus a fixed grid; keep the ink on `translate` + `scale`.

findings.what: The Holotable search field and the swap picker search input render at 12 px on touch devices, so iOS Safari zooms the page when they gain focus.

findings.what: Six public components/services of the area have no spec at all, and the two REQ-5 / REQ-33 reduced-motion cut-throughs are only asserted for the arrival — the set ⇄ arsenal hop's reduced-motion branch is marked `pending` rather than exercised.
findings.evidence: No `*.spec.ts` for src/app/codex/stage/codex-stage.component.ts (402 lines), src/app/codex/holo/codex-holo-table.component.ts (370), src/app/codex/holo/codex-holo-inspector.component.ts (306), src/app/codex/holo/codex-holo-perspectives.component.ts (214), src/app/codex/codex-analysis-panels.component.ts (409), src/app/codex/ship-link.service.ts (217) (`for f in …; [ -f "${f%.ts}.spec.ts" ] || echo`); src/app/codex/set/set-arsenal-transition.spec.ts:62-63 `if (reducedMotion()) { pending('reduced motion navigates without a transition');` — the `prefersReducedMotion()` branch of set-arsenal-transition.ts:455 is never forced true in a test. Covered well: set stage/page/gear/rating, transition happy path, holo stage arrival/pins/hotkeys, board figure, skin viewer.
findings.fix: Add a spec that stubs `matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)')` to `matches: true` and asserts `hop()` calls `navigateByUrl` without `startViewTransition`; add smoke specs for codex-stage (image chain fallback, resize relayout), holo-table (pin rendering per phase, `still`), holo-inspector (target vs pin list vs empty), holo-perspectives (gauge/subs), analysis panels (fold peek) and ship-link.service (error-code mapping).

findings.what: Destructive admin actions confirm through the browser's native window.confirm() (OS look, no app styling, no translation of the buttons); the project has no app-styled confirm component. Raised once for the project.
findings.evidence: src/app/admin/admin.component.ts:1523 (decline request), :1661 (withdraw invite), :1678 (delete user); src/app/admin/api-tokens/api-tokens.component.ts:618 (revoke token); src/app/admin/feedback/admin-feedback.component.ts:2660 (delete topic). findings.what: The two hand-rolled fetch() calls to edge functions have no timeout, so a hung function leaves the token page in 'loading' / the concept page on 'loading' forever.
findings.evidence: src/app/admin/api-tokens/api-tokens.service.ts:153, :163, :174 `fetch(this.apiUrl(…), { method, headers })` — no `signal`; src/app/admin/concepts/concept-page.service.ts:79-83 same; api-tokens.component.ts:564-575 keeps `busy` true until the promise settles; concept-page.component.ts:143 state stays 'loading'.
findings.fix: Pass `signal: AbortSignal.timeout(15_000)` in both services and map the AbortError to the existing error paths (`new Error('timeout')` / `ConceptTicketFailure('error')`).

findings.what: Telemetry and concept page loads are not sequence-guarded: a slower earlier response overwrites the newer one, so quickly switching product/range (or concept id) can show the previous selection's data under the new heading.
findings.evidence: src/app/admin/telemetry-stats.component.ts:635-639 `effect(() => { … void this.load(days, product); })` plus :640 useAutoRefresh, and :704-709 `this.stats.set(data as TelemetryStats)` unconditionally; src/app/admin/concepts/concept-page.component.ts:137-139 `paramMap.subscribe((params) => void this.load(…))` with :151-154 setting state from whichever promise resolves last. REQ-27 fixed the same shape on the set page.
findings.fix: Add a `private loadSeq = 0` counter: `const seq = ++this.loadSeq;` before the await, `if (seq !== this.loadSeq) return;` after it, in both `load()` methods.

findings.what: Overlays outside the holotable animate in but vanish instantly: the download menu, the component modal and the feedback sheets/menus have `-in` keyframes and no exit, whereas the holo family pairs every enter with a shorter exit.

findings.what: Three near-identical "emphasised decelerate" curves coexist for the same kind of motion (reveals/rises), and the holo family redefines its `--e-out` token in four components; there is no global easing token.

findings.what: Data-path failures that degrade the UI leave no log line at all, so a report like 'vote counts are stale' or 'my flagship pin did not sync' has nothing to grep: the failure is swallowed and the page silently shows older data.
findings.evidence: src/app/codex/codex.service.ts:1180 `if (error) continue; // transport error` (silhouette chunk); starscape/starscape-votes.service.ts:106 `catch { /* the tiles simply keep whatever counts they had */ }`, :198, :222; desktop/desktop-connection.service.ts:99 `/* offline / RPC missing */`, :120; hangar/hangar.service.ts:541 `catch { // Offline / stubbed client — localStorage keeps the pin`; codex/codex-detail.component.ts:2475 `// tech chips are a bonus`, :2500, :2549; hangar/hangar-import.component.ts:313 `/* search unavailable → entry stays unmatched */`; codex/codex-landing.component.ts:867; social/account-status.service.ts:147 (deliberate 'say nothing, deny nothing' — keep silent to the user, but still worth a warn).
findings.fix: Add one `console.warn('[scope] <what> failed', err)` (or the shared logger from the no-central-logger finding) inside each listed catch; keep the user-facing behaviour unchanged.

findings.what: No central logger: the 10 shipped `console.*` calls use four different prefix styles and one degraded-but-working case logs at `error`. Every call is legitimate error context (no noise, nothing per frame/request), so this is a consistency gap rather than a leak.
findings.evidence: Inventory (src/app, non-spec): desktop/desktop-session.util.ts:43 warn `[desktop-session] mint failed…`, :52 warn, :61 warn; codex/codex.service.ts:941 error `[codex] listFpsCatalog(…) stopped at the …-row cap` (page still renders → should be warn), :1292 error `[codex] getEntityPayloads chunk failed`, :1325 error `[codex] getAmmoPayloads chunk failed`; settings/settings.component.ts:1299 warn `[settings] set_preferred_lang failed:`, :1312 warn; starscape/starscape.service.ts:317 warn `starscape: variant columns not deployed yet` (no bracket prefix); starscape/starscape-votes.service.ts:235 warn `[starscape] set_starscape_top_only failed:`; src/main.ts:12 error (bootstrap). `grep -rln 'class \w*Logger\|LoggerService' src/app` → none.
findings.fix: Add `src/app/core/log.ts` with `logWarn(scope, msg, ctx?)` / `logError(scope, msg, ctx?)` that formats `[scope] msg` and is the one place a future sink (ErrorHandler/PostHog) hooks in; replace the 10 calls, and downgrade codex.service.ts:941 to warn.

findings.what: No offline awareness anywhere in the client: with the network down the service worker serves the shell, but the codex list, hangar and feedback panels show a generic 'Failed to fetch' card with a Retry button and nothing tells the user they are offline; no `online`/`offline` events or `navigator.onLine` reads exist.
findings.evidence: `grep -rn 'navigator.onLine\|addEventListener(.offline\|addEventListener(.online' src/app src/index.html` → 0; ngsw-config.json has `assetGroups` app/assets but no offline page (`navigationUrls` not set); i18n keys containing offline/network are only admin heartbeat and `starscape.errors.timeout`; codex-list.component.ts:309-313 error card renders `{{ err }}` which for a failed fetch is the TypeError text.
findings.fix: Add `src/app/core/connectivity.service.ts` (signal from `navigator.onLine` + `online`/`offline` events); the shared `describeError` maps a TypeError to `errors.network` and, when `connectivity.online()` is false, to `errors.offline` ('You appear to be offline — the retry will work once the connection is back'); readers keep their Retry button.

findings.what: `desktop-auth.component.ts` and `desktop-read-auth.component.ts` are ~180-line near-copies (template, styles, OAuth stash fallback, `waitFor`, form-POST builder) that differ only in the role gate, the i18n prefix and the fixed callback path.

findings.what: Confirming a fleet import writes ships one by one (insert, then a second update for the nickname) — up to 200 entries × 2 sequential round trips.
