findings.what: Data-path failures are swallowed with empty `catch {}` and no context anywhere in core/auth/shell (the project has no logger; the only console call in scope is main.ts bootstrap), and unhandled promise rejections never reach Angular's ErrorHandler because `provideBrowserGlobalErrorListeners()` is not registered.
findings.evidence: role.service.ts:218 `} catch { return null; }` (profile read failure → identityUnknown, no log); profile.service.ts:45 `const { data } = await …` (error discarded); quick-search.component.ts:521-525 `catch { … results.set([]) }`; analytics.service.ts:144-147; sw-update.service.ts:136-140; presence.service.ts:88; app.config.ts:14-52 has no ErrorHandler/provideBrowserGlobalErrorListeners; fire-and-forget promises without catch: auth.service.ts:50 `getSession().then(…)`, sw-update.service.ts:72/74 `void this.swUpdate.checkForUpdate()`, quick-search.component.ts:400 `void this.hangar.loadAll()`.
findings.fix: Add a tiny `log.warn(scope, msg, ctx)` helper in src/app/core and call it in each catch with the failing id (user id, search term, event); add `provideBrowserGlobalErrorListeners()` to app.config.ts providers.

findings.what: Specs wait on real wall-clock timers (~10 s per run, load-sensitive): the holo stage arrival (1.7 s), the img-ready watchdog (5 × 1.5 s), Angular/CSS animation settles (260 ms) and a 3 s polling budget — all drive `setTimeout`-based code that `fakeAsync`/`tick` could control.
findings.evidence: src/app/codex/holo/codex-holo-stage.component.spec.ts:376 `await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 1700));` (component: REVEAL_MS 1100 via setTimeout, :946); src/app/news/img-ready.directive.spec.ts:18 `PAST_FIRST_RECHECK_MS = 1500` used at :71,86,94,108,120 (news-thumb.component.ts:18 READY_RECHECKS_MS setTimeout); src/app/core/swipe-action.directive.spec.ts:62 `setTimeout(r, 260)` (directive FLY_MS 200 setTimeout :222); admin/feedback/composer-styles.spec.ts:83,91; admin/feedback/feedback-composer.component.spec.ts:633-640 poll until 3000 ms.
findings.fix: Convert codex-holo-stage.spec:371, img-ready.directive.spec and swipe-action.directive.spec to `fakeAsync` + `tick(REVEAL_MS)` / `tick(1200)` / `tick(FLY_MS)`; keep the animation-driven composer-styles spec as is.

findings.what: The ship hero's `bay-drift` animation loops forever (`infinite alternate`) for the whole page lifetime, including while scrolled off-screen; it does respect reduced motion.
findings.evidence: src/app/codex/codex-detail.component.ts:1631-1634 `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference) { .hero.bay .hero-art:not(.icon-only) .art { animation: bay-drift 6s ease-in-out infinite alternate; } @keyframes bay-drift { from { transform: translateY(-3px); } to { transform: translateY(3px); } } }` — compositor-only property, but no pause when off-screen. keybinds.component.ts:464-467 `kb-pulse 1.8s … infinite` is admin-only and also reduced-motion gated.
findings.fix: Either drop the loop (a single 6 s ease-in on load) or add `animation-play-state: paused` when the hero is not intersecting (a 6-line IntersectionObserver in the stage component toggling a host class).

findings.what: Hover styles are declared outside `@media (hover: hover)` throughout the scope, so on touch devices a tapped card keeps its lifted/lit hover state until the next tap elsewhere.
findings.evidence: `grep -rln 'hover: hover' src/app` → 1 file in the whole app; scope counts of `:hover` rules: codex-bridge.component.ts 12 (e.g. :437 `.lane-card:hover { transform: translateY(-2px); …}`), codex-hardpoint-layout.component.ts 11 (:903 `button.slot-btn:hover, button.kid-btn:hover { border-color: var(--sc-accent); …}`), holo/codex-holo-stage.component.ts 9, codex-landing.component.ts 6 (:466), holo/codex-holo-table.component.ts 5 (:291), set/codex-set-gear.component.ts 4 (:200), holo/codex-holo-perspectives.component.ts 2 (:135).
findings.fix: Wrap the transform/background hover rules in `@media (hover: hover)` (mechanical per ui-defaults R6), starting with the lane cards and slot buttons that change layout on hover.

findings.what: Angular toolchain and framework are on different minors: @angular/cli and @angular/build are locked at 22.1.9 while every @angular/* framework package is 22.2.0.
findings.evidence: package.json:80-81 `"@angular/build": "^22.1.9", "@angular/cli": "^22.1.9"` vs :61 `"@angular/core": "^22.2.0"`; package-lock.json:152 resolves build-22.1.9.tgz; npm-outdated.json: `@angular/build` current 22.1.9, wanted 22.2.0 (same for cli).
findings.fix: `npm i -D @angular/build@22.2.0 @angular/cli@22.2.0` (or merge the Dependabot angular group PR) so `ng version` shows one minor for CLI and framework.

findings.what: Error paths that silently hide whole sections of a page log nothing: 11 `catch {}` blocks in codex-detail and 8 swallowed errors in the services, although the project already has a `[codex]`-prefixed console.error convention.
findings.evidence: Convention: codex.service.ts:941, :1292 `console.error('[codex] getEntityPayloads chunk failed', kind, error)`, :1325. Silent: codex-detail.component.ts:2474 (resolveShipTech), :2500 (ammo), :2519 (skin group), :2539 (edition group), :2549 (used-in), :2565 (recipe), :2596 (where-to-buy), :3022 (hydrateDraftClass), :3092 (saveLoadoutDraft), :3537 (rank cohort), :3141 (draft mirror); showroom.service.ts:67 `if (!error) this._entries.set(entries)`; ship-skins.service.ts:63 `if (error) return { skins: [], error: true }`; ship-link.service.ts:70/81 ignore `globalRes.error`/`ownRes.error`; codex.service.ts:706, :753 (RPC `catch { return null }`), :1121 `if (error) return null`; uex-shop.service.ts:308 `catch { return []; }`. Counted with grep: 20 catch blocks in codex-detail, 9 in codex.service.
findings.fix: Add one `console.error('[codex] <operation> failed', { className/kind/buildId }, err)` line inside each listed catch / error branch (or a 4-line `logCodexError(op, ctx, err)` helper in codex-format.ts and call it); no behaviour change.

findings.what: Errors on the data paths of the set page, the figure, the skin viewer and the share popover are caught and dropped without any log line or user feedback, so a failing RPC or a blocked three.js chunk is invisible in the console (the project has no logger service to route them to).
findings.evidence: src/app/codex/set/codex-set.component.ts:325 `.catch(() => land(this.resolvedArmor, new Map()))`, :329, :335, :342-343 `catch { land(this.ratingRows, null); }`; src/app/codex/set/codex-set-gear.component.ts:353,372 `catch { this.failedSlot.set(slot); }`; src/app/codex/codex-board-figure.component.ts:493-496 `catch { // No engine, no problem … this.teardown(); }`; src/app/codex/ship-skin-viewer.component.ts:740-742 `.catch(() => { /* markers are a bonus */ })`; src/app/codex/holo/codex-holo-share.component.ts:201-206 `catch { return; }` (clipboard denied → nothing happens, no toast); src/app/codex/holo/codex-holo-stage.component.ts:1022, codex-landing.component.ts:867,935, codex-bridge.component.ts:658, codex-swap-picker.component.ts:767; `ls src/app/core | grep -i log` → no logger.
findings.fix: Add a `console.warn('[codex] <what failed>', { ids }, err)` (or the project's ErrorHandler for unexpected errors) in each catch that hides a network/RPC failure, and give the share popover's clipboard failure a visible error text.

findings.what: No Node version is pinned anywhere for the web app: a machine on Node 22.22.2 cannot build or test (Angular CLI 22.1.9 requires ^22.22.3 || ^24.15.0 || >=26); the only working pin is a Vercel dashboard setting invisible to the repo.
findings.evidence: package.json has no `engines`/`volta`/`packageManager` (grep empty); no `.nvmrc`/`.node-version` (`cat` → No such file); vercel.json sets no Node version; Vercel project `star-citizen-companion-website` reports `nodeVersion: "24.x"` (MCP get_project). node_modules/@angular/cli/package.json engines `^22.22.3 || ^24.15.0 || >=26.0.0`; this container `node --version` = v22.22.2 → baseline test.log `TEST_EXIT=3` after 0.15 s, build.log empty. README.md Quick start (lines 20-27) names no Node version.
findings.fix: Add `"engines": { "node": "^22.22.3 || ^24.15.0" }` to package.json, a `.nvmrc` with `24`, and one line in README Quick start; keep it aligned with Vercel's 24.x.

findings.what: app.component.spec.ts is the one spec that builds the real Supabase client and real AuthService: `createClient(environment.supabase.url, …)` runs against the cloud project config with `provideHttpClient(withXhr())`, so the smoke test depends on the environment file and would issue requests if a session were present in the Karma profile.
findings.evidence: src/app/app.component.spec.ts:12-19 providers list has no `SupabaseClientProvider`/`AuthService` override; src/app/core/supabase.client.ts:38 `readonly realClient: SupabaseClient = createClient(environment.supabase.url, …, { auth: { persistSession: true, detectSessionInUrl: true, autoRefreshToken: true` ; src/app/auth/auth.service.ts:50 `this.sb.realClient.auth.getSession().then(`; every other spec (29) provides `provide: SupabaseClientProvider`.
findings.fix: Provide `{ provide: SupabaseClientProvider, useValue: fakeSupabase() }` and a stub AuthService (`user: signal(null)`, `ready: () => Promise.resolve()`) in app.component.spec.ts.

findings.what: The skin viewer, the Spot stage and the hangar picker are styled with hex/rgba literals and with fallbacks of custom properties that no token file defines (`--panel`, `--amber`, `--field`), so a future theme swap leaves these surfaces on the hard-coded palette.
findings.evidence: src/app/codex/ship-skin-viewer.component.ts:392 `background: var(--panel, #1c2330)` (`--panel` absent from node_modules/@starorga/star-ui/lib/design-tokens.css and src/styles.scss), :380 `color: #e88`, :393 `color: #cdd`, :504 `#3a4150`, :538-544 `#173a25/#6ad28a/#1c2330/#8fb0e0`, :554 `#7f92ab`, :602-605 `rgba(8,11,16,.94)/#2a3444/#dce6f5`; src/app/codex/stage/codex-stage.component.ts:168 `var(--field, #071520)`, :200 `var(--amber, #f0c27b)`, :201 `rgba(242, 247, 251, .72)`, :280; src/app/codex/stage/hangar-picker.component.ts:535,545,573; src/app/codex/codex-landing.component.ts:383 `box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px rgba(0, 212, 255, 0.22)` (focus ring not the accent), :452 `--meta: #b98bff`, :461 `--soon: #f0b44a`, :513,524,527; src/app/codex/codex-bridge.component.ts:341; src/app/codex/codex-analysis-panels.component.ts:16-23 `DAMAGE_CHANNEL_COLORS` literals.
findings.fix: Define `--sc-amber`, `--sc-stage-field` (and a damage-channel palette) once in styles.scss next to `--sc-idle`, swap the literals for those tokens, and use `color-mix(var(--sc-accent) …)` for the landing/bridge focus rings.

findings.what: Three functions have no caller in the repository: verify-release-token (every ingest-* validates the token inline; it is also deployed with the platform gate ON so its stated no-JWT caller can never reach it), process-p4k (only mention is its config.toml block) and check-bundle (only a comment in the uploader).
findings.evidence: `grep -rn verify-release-token --include=*.ts,*.mjs,*.rs,*.yml .` → only CHANGELOG/release-notes/project-map; live `curl …/verify-release-token` → 401 `UNAUTHORIZED_NO_AUTH_HEADER`; `grep -rn process-p4k` (excl. its own folder) → supabase/config.toml:89 only; `grep -rn check-bundle data-uploader/src` → release-token.ts:21 (comment). verify-release-token/index.ts:288-293 admits it is an unauthenticated 'oracle'; process-p4k/index.ts:374 `const body: RequestBody = await req.json();` unguarded.
findings.fix: Delete supabase/functions/{verify-release-token,process-p4k,check-bundle} and their config.toml blocks (operator runs `supabase functions delete` for each), or wire the intended callers and add a config block + test.

findings.what: `is_admin(uuid)` is executable by anon and authenticated, so any caller can ask `/rpc/is_admin?uid=<uuid>` and enumerate which accounts are admins; nothing in the repo uses the overload.
findings.evidence: supabase/migrations/20260529_public_api_tokens.sql:41 `grant execute on function public.is_admin(uuid) to authenticated, anon, service_role;` — `grep -rn is_admin supabase/functions` finds only a comment (concept-page/index.ts:33); the no-arg is_admin() is what every policy uses.
findings.fix: New migration: `revoke execute on function public.is_admin(uuid) from public, anon, authenticated;` keeping the service_role grant (the api_tokens policy calls it with auth.uid(), which still works because policies run as the table owner's function call — verify with the api_tokens policy before applying).

findings.what: profiles_self_upsert lets an authenticated user INSERT their own profile row with any role/is_approved/suspension values; both guard triggers are BEFORE UPDATE only, so the pin holds only because handle_new_user() always pre-creates the row.
findings.evidence: supabase/migrations/00001_init_schema.sql:20-21 `create policy "profiles_self_upsert" on public.profiles for insert with check (auth.uid() = id);` (no column pin); guards: 20260921220000_profile_last_seen.sql:300-302 `create trigger profiles_role_write_guard before update on public.profiles`, 20260802080000_protected_admins.sql:155-161 `before update or delete`. A profile row missing for a live auth user (manual dashboard delete, failed trigger) would let that user self-insert `role='admin', is_approved=true`.
findings.fix: New migration: replace profiles_self_upsert with `with check (auth.uid() = id and role = 'viewer' and is_approved = false and suspended_at is null)`, or extend profiles_role_write_guard to `before insert or update` treating a NULL old as the neutral defaults.

findings.what: api_request_log grows without bound: the rate limiter inserts one row per API call and reads only the last minute, but the 'autopurge cron' the migration relies on was never created (the only two pg_cron jobs are codex-build-retention and patch-stability-sample).
findings.evidence: supabase/migrations/20260529_public_api_tokens.sql:96-97 `-- For now (alpha, expected <100 req/min) a single table + autopurge cron is fine.`; supabase/functions/api/_rate-limit.ts:37-40 counts `.gte('ts', windowStart)` and :67-71 `.from('api_request_log').insert({…})`; `grep -n "cron.schedule" supabase/migrations/*.sql` → only 20260906130000:32 and 20260925010000:69. No index or partition by ts alone, so the table competes with the 500 MB budget of REQ-35.
findings.fix: New migration: `select cron.schedule('api-request-log-purge', '15 4 * * *', $$delete from public.api_request_log where ts < now() - interval '1 day'$$);` (mirror the unschedule-if-exists guard of 20260925010000).

findings.what: Two of the newest migrations are not re-runnable although the house style (and every neighbouring file) declares 'IDEMPOTENT: safe to re-run', and the project has already been bitten by a partial `db push` rollback.
findings.evidence: supabase/migrations/20260920150000_codex_silhouettes.sql:54 `create table public.codex_silhouettes (` (no if not exists), :89-93 two `create policy` without `drop policy if exists`; 20260920160000_hangar_loadout_sharing.sql:235 `create table public.hangar_share_links (`, :260 `create index hangar_share_links_created_by_idx` (no if not exists), :267-294 six `create policy` without drop. Older offenders (00001, 00008, 00010, 20260613, 20260712, 20260805, 20260816, 20260820) predate the convention. CHANGELOG.md:347-349 records the class of failure: 'Die Migration aus 0.97.0 brach beim Anlegen der schon vorhandenen pg_cron-Erweiterung ab und wurde vollständig zurückgerollt.'
findings.fix: In both files add `if not exists` to the create table/index statements and precede each `create policy` with `drop policy if exists <name> on <table>;` (no semantic change on an already-applied database).

findings.what: Three foreign keys whose ON DELETE actions the app triggers have no usable index, so each parent delete sequentially scans the child table: hangar_share_links.source_config_id, hangar_ship_configs.source_config_id (the partial unique index leads with user_id) and hangar_ship_configs.owner_user_id.
findings.evidence: supabase/migrations/20260920160000_hangar_loadout_sharing.sql:93-95 `source_config_id … on delete set null, … owner_user_id … on delete set null`, :116-118 `create unique index … on public.hangar_ship_configs (user_id, source_config_id) where source_config_id is not null`, :250 hangar_share_links.source_config_id with only `hangar_share_links_created_by_idx` (:260). Every other child FK in the schema is indexed (codex_*_build_idx, feedback_drafts_feedback_idx :79-81, feedback_read_state_feedback_idx). Triggered by hangar.service.ts:693 deleteConfig and :441 removeShip. Tables are per-user small, so cost is latency, not outage.
findings.fix: Add `create index if not exists hangar_share_links_source_idx on hangar_share_links (source_config_id) where source_config_id is not null;` and `hangar_ship_configs_source_idx on hangar_ship_configs (source_config_id) where source_config_id is not null;` (and owner_user_id likewise) in the same migration that fixes the guard/FK conflict.

findings.what: The public access-request form leaks whether an address already has a pending application: the guard raises a distinct 23505 to the anonymous caller although its own comment promises never to confirm that to a stranger.
findings.evidence: supabase/migrations/20260816120000_access_requests.sql:88-98 comment 'never confirming to a stranger whether an application for someone else's address exists' followed by `raise exception 'duplicate access request' using errcode = '23505';` — PostgREST returns the code and message to anon (policy :125-126 `for insert to anon, authenticated with check (true)`).
findings.fix: In access_requests_guard() return NULL (skip the insert silently) on the duplicate branch instead of raising, so success and duplicate are indistinguishable over the API; keep the unique index as the hard guarantee.

findings.what: Browser-extension workflow inlines the manifest version into shell and release inputs after a prefix-only regex, so a crafted `version` string in browser-extension/manifest.json is expanded into `run:` unescaped.
findings.evidence: .github/workflows/browser-extension-build.yml:53 `if (!/^\d+\.\d+\.\d+/.test(m.version ?? ""))` (no `$` anchor); :80 `cp sc-hangar-extension.zip "sc-hangar-extension-${{ steps.manifest.outputs.version }}.zip"`; :136/:147 same output in `files:`/`body:`. Publish step is main-only and the repo is public (fork PRs get a read-only token, no secrets), so impact is limited to PR-run tampering.
findings.fix: Anchor the regex (`/^\d+\.\d+\.\d+(\.\d+)?$/`) and pass the output to the shell via `env: VERSION: ${{ steps.manifest.outputs.version }}` instead of inline expansion.

findings.what: `permissions: contents: write` is granted workflow-wide where jobs do not need it: every publish in wallpaper-app-build.yml uses the PAT on the mirror repo, and data-uploader-build.yml gives write to the typecheck/test jobs that run on every PR.
findings.evidence: .github/workflows/wallpaper-app-build.yml:21-22 `permissions:\n  contents: write` while all `softprops/action-gh-release` steps (:135-160) set `repository: StarOrga/Star-Citizen-Companion-Binaries` + `token: ${{ secrets.BINARIES_RELEASE_TOKEN }}`; data-uploader-build.yml:16-17 same, only the `build-windows` step 'Publish to PRIVATE source-repo release' (:154) uses GITHUB_TOKEN. Compare browser-extension-build.yml:32-33 and edge-functions-deploy.yml:46-47, which correctly use `contents: read`.
findings.fix: Set `permissions: contents: read` at workflow level in both files and add `permissions: contents: write` only on the data-uploader `build-windows` job.

findings.what: Third-party actions are pinned by mutable tag rather than commit SHA, and the Supabase CLI used for production deploys is `version: latest` — a compromised or breaking upstream release reaches CI and the edge-function deploy without a repo change.
findings.evidence: `grep -rhn uses: .github/workflows/*.yml`: softprops/action-gh-release@v3 (5×), ilammy/msvc-dev-cmd@v1, supabase/setup-cli@v3, actions/checkout@v7 (7×), actions/setup-node@v7 (4×), actions/setup-python@v7, actions/upload-artifact@v7 (4×) — no `@<sha>` anywhere; edge-functions-deploy.yml:134-136 `uses: supabase/setup-cli@v3 / with: version: latest` while package.json:97 pins the CLI to ^2.117.0.
findings.fix: Pin `uses:` to full commit SHAs with a `# vX.Y.Z` comment (Dependabot's github-actions group in .github/dependabot.yml already exists and keeps SHA pins current) and set `supabase/setup-cli` `version:` to the devDependency version (2.117.0).

findings.what: data-uploader CI builds on Node 20.10.0 — an exact 2023 patch of a release line that reached end-of-life on 2026-04-30 — so the shipped Electron binary is built with an unsupported toolchain and no security patches.
findings.evidence: .github/workflows/data-uploader-build.yml:29 and :91 `node-version: '20.10.0'`; data-uploader/package.json engines `>=20.10.0`; the other two Node workflows use `node-version: 22` (edge-functions-deploy.yml:64, readme-docs-sync.yml:54).
findings.fix: Bump both `node-version` entries to `22` (and data-uploader engines to `>=22`), verify `npm ci && npm test` in data-uploader on the new version.

findings.what: The service-worker config caches no translation files or the meshopt decoder: an installed PWA that starts from the cached shell offline (or on a flaky network) fetches `i18n/<lang>.json` over the network and renders without any UI text.
findings.evidence: ngsw-config.json:6-27 — `app` group prefetches `/favicon.ico, /index.html, /manifest.webmanifest, /*.css, /*.js`; `assets` group covers `/icons/**`, `/assets/**` and root image/font extensions; no pattern matches `/i18n/*.json` (public/i18n: de,en,es,fr,pt,ru,zh.json) or `/meshopt/**` (ship-skin-viewer.component.ts:51 loads `/meshopt/meshopt_decoder.loader.js`). src/app/app.config.ts:48 `provideTranslateHttpLoader({ prefix: 'i18n/', suffix: '.json' })`.
findings.fix: Add `"/i18n/*.json"` and `"/meshopt/**"` to the `assets` group's `files` in ngsw-config.json (lazy install, prefetch update).

findings.what: Deploy/mirror workflows have no `concurrency` group or `timeout-minutes`: two quick pushes to main can run the edge-function deploy (and the ReadMe mirror push) concurrently and finish out of order, leaving production on the older commit.
findings.evidence: `grep -n "concurrency\|timeout-minutes" .github/workflows/*.yml` → none; edge-functions-deploy.yml:117-121 deploy job triggers on every push to main; readme-docs-sync.yml:76-119 force-replaces the mirror content and pushes.
findings.fix: Add `concurrency: { group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}, cancel-in-progress: false }` and `timeout-minutes: 20` to edge-functions-deploy.yml and readme-docs-sync.yml.

findings.what: The workflow grants `contents: write` to every job (typecheck, vitest, pytest, PR runs) instead of only the tag-gated build-windows job, and the third-party release action that handles `BINARIES_RELEASE_TOKEN` is referenced by floating major tag, not commit SHA.
findings.evidence: .github/workflows/data-uploader-build.yml:16-17 top-level `permissions:\n  contents: write`; :148 and :173 `uses: softprops/action-gh-release@v3` (secret at :176 `token: ${{ secrets.BINARIES_RELEASE_TOKEN }}`); :26/:28/:43 `actions/checkout@v7` etc. also tag-pinned.
findings.fix: Move `permissions: contents: write` under the `build-windows` job and set top-level `permissions: contents: read`; pin `softprops/action-gh-release` (and ideally the actions/* steps) to a full commit SHA with the version in a trailing comment.

findings.what: CI never runs `electron-vite build` on push/PR — only typecheck + vitest — so bundling failures (the `stripRemoteFontImport` plugin throwing, preload CJS format, `define` wiring, renderer JSON imports) surface first on a release tag, where a red build blocks the ship.
findings.evidence: .github/workflows/data-uploader-build.yml:32-34 `- run: npm ci` / `npm run typecheck` / `npm test` in typecheck-and-test; `npm run build` appears only in build-windows (:136) which is `if: startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/data-uploader-v')` (:69); data-uploader/electron.vite.config.ts:16-18 the plugin throws at build time on a surviving Google-Fonts import.
findings.fix: Add `- run: npm run build` (with `SC_API_BASE`/`SC_WEB_BASE` dummy env) after `npm test` in the `typecheck-and-test` job; it needs no Python or Windows.

findings.what: `host_permissions` duplicates the content-script `matches` and grants nothing the extension uses (no extension-page fetch, no `scripting`, no `tabs`); the manifest could drop the block for MV3 minimality without changing the install warning.
findings.evidence: browser-extension/manifest.json:15-19 `"host_permissions": ["https://robertsspaceindustries.com/account/pledges*", "https://robertsspaceindustries.com/*/account/pledges*", "https://sc-companion.vercel.app/*"]` — identical to content_scripts matches at :32-35 and :40; the only network call is `fetch(url, { credentials: 'same-origin' })` from inside the RSI content script (rsi-hangar.js:57), which runs in the page's origin and needs no host permission; the popup makes no requests (popup.js:6 'No network access whatsoever').
findings.fix: Remove `host_permissions` from manifest.json (keep `permissions: ["storage"]`), re-test the handover in developer mode, and drop the 'host permissions' wording from README.md and PRIVACY.md's permission table (keep the site rows as content-script access).

findings.what: The wallpaper-app workflow grants its GITHUB_TOKEN `contents: write` on this repo although every publish targets the separate binaries-mirror repo with a PAT; the extension workflow does the same handoff with `contents: read`.
findings.evidence: .github/workflows/wallpaper-app-build.yml:21-22 `permissions:\n  contents: write`; publishes at :133-142 and :154-165 use `repository: StarOrga/Star-Citizen-Companion-Binaries` + `token: ${{ secrets.BINARIES_RELEASE_TOKEN }}`; .github/workflows/browser-extension-build.yml:31-34 — 'The publish targets a DIFFERENT repo and authenticates with a PAT, so the job's own GITHUB_TOKEN never needs write access. permissions: contents: read'.
findings.fix: Set `permissions: contents: read` in wallpaper-app-build.yml (upload-artifact and softprops/action-gh-release with an explicit token need no repo write), mirroring the extension workflow's comment.

findings.what: Six components query Supabase directly (30 call sites) instead of going through a service, unlike every other feature.
findings.evidence: admin/feedback/admin-feedback.component.ts (16 sites, see the god-file finding); admin/admin.component.ts .rpc() at :1457 (pending_access_requests), :1496/:1526 (decide_access_request), :1545 (list_users_for_admin), :1556 (list_reports_for_admin), :1644 (list_allowed_emails), :1664 (remove_allowed_email), :1701 (set_user_role); admin/telemetry-stats.component.ts:699 rpc('get_telemetry_stats'); settings/settings.component.ts:1297 rpc('set_preferred_lang'), :1310 rpc('set_preferred_region'); desktop/desktop-download.component.ts:268 rpc('promote_desktop_channel'); app.component.ts:130 .from('profiles').select('preferred_lang, preferred_region'). Non-component, non-service files with direct calls: none (grep).
findings.fix: Add admin/admin-users.service.ts (access requests, users, allowed emails, reports, roles), admin/telemetry.service.ts, core/profile-prefs.service.ts (preferred lang/region read+write used by app.component and settings) and DesktopReleaseService.promote(); components call the services.

findings.what: Colour literals instead of design tokens inside scope styles, including one custom property (`--field`) that is defined nowhere so its hex fallback always paints.
findings.evidence: codex-detail.component.ts:1740-1743 `.dmg[data-ch="thermal"] .dmg-fill { background: #ff5252 }`, `#a674ff`, `#5fd35f`, `#f0c419`; :1626-1627 `#05080d`, `#04060a`; codex-compare-tray.component.ts:162-165 `color: #8fe5b5 … #5fd698`, :175 `background: #5fd698`; codex-list.component.ts:484 `--soon: #f0b44a`; fps-list.component.ts:404 `background: var(--field, #071520)` (grep `--field` over src: only this line); codex-category-icon.component.ts:66-84 twelve hex literals in CAT_COLORS (`shield: '#52c1e6'`, `power: '#f0c419'`, …); codex-status-banner.component.ts:96-97 `var(--sc-warning, #d29922)`; codex-compare-tray.component.ts:180 `var(--sc-warning, #ffc14d)`.
findings.fix: Define the damage-channel and category palette once in styles.scss (`--sc-dmg-thermal`, `--sc-dmg-distortion`, `--sc-dmg-bio`, `--sc-dmg-stun`, `--sc-cat-*`) next to `--sc-offense`, reference them from the five files, replace `var(--field, #071520)` with `var(--sc-bg-0)`, and drop the redundant `--sc-warning` fallbacks (the token exists in styles.scss:24).

findings.what: `npm run lint` is a no-op echo — no linter is configured for the web app (carry-over AUD-066, reported once here).
findings.evidence: package.json:30 `"lint": "echo 'no-op: add @angular-eslint and run ng lint'"`; no eslint.config.* / .eslintrc in the repo root.
findings.fix: `ng add @angular-eslint/schematics` (adds eslint.config.js + the `lint` architect target) and set `"lint": "ng lint"`; run it in the new web CI job.

findings.what: `--sc-accent-hot` (#ff5722) is used as small text colour at 31 sites; on the panel surface it measures 4.23:1 (below WCAG AA 4.5:1 for text under 18 px) and only passes on the canvas (4.93:1); most sites are uppercase labels ≤ 0.8 rem.
findings.evidence: node contrast (StarUI tokens): hot #ff5722 on --surface-panel #123246 = 4.23, on --surface-canvas-alt #103246 = 4.24, on --surface-canvas #0d2635 = 4.93. `grep -rnE 'color:\s*var\(--sc-accent-hot\)' src/app src/styles.scss | wc -l` = 31, e.g. src/app/desktop/uploader-access.component.ts:114 `letter-spacing: 0.08em; text-transform: uppercase; color: var(--sc-accent-hot);`, src/app/admin/feedback/feedback-composer.component.ts:435 `.draft-flag.warn { color: var(--sc-accent-hot); }`, src/app/admin/feedback/admin-feedback.component.ts:1189 `.baton.ask-question { color: var(--sc-accent-hot); }`.
findings.fix: Define a text-safe hot alias in src/styles.scss (e.g. `--sc-accent-hot-text: color-mix(in srgb, var(--sc-accent-hot) 85%, #fff)` ≥ 4.5:1 on --sc-bg-1) and use it for the small-text sites on panel surfaces; keep `--sc-accent-hot` for fills, borders and ≥ 18 px text.

findings.what: Craft/dismantle durations print minutes as 'm' ('1 h 1 m 1 s'), which is not the SI symbol for minute and collides with metres shown as 'm' / 'm/s' on the same pages.
findings.evidence: src/app/codex/codex-format.ts:975-987 `formatCraftTime`: `if (m > 0) parts.push(\`${m} m\`);` with doc example `3661 → "1 h 1 m 1 s"`; rendered as badges in codex-list.component.ts:257 `craftTimeLabel(r)`, blueprint-detail.component.ts:331-337 and codex-detail.component.ts:1004 `fmtCraft`. Metres: codex-detail :2760 `+ ' m'`, :3796 `num(flight?.scmSpeed, 'm/s')`.
findings.fix: Emit `min` for minutes in formatCraftTime (`${m} min`) and update the expectations in codex-format.spec.ts / blueprint-detail.component.spec.ts.

findings.what: Hover styles are almost never wrapped in `@media (hover: hover)`: 342 `:hover` rules across 89 component files, only starscape.component.ts wraps them — on touch targets a tapped card/button keeps its hover surface until the next tap.
findings.evidence: `grep -rcE ':hover'` → 342 rules in 89 files; `grep -rlE '@media \(hover:\s*hover\)'` → only src/app/starscape/starscape.component.ts. The one hover-only reveal found is covered: src/app/codex/holo/codex-holo-stage.component.ts:634-635 `.holo-table:hover .tools5 … { opacity: 1 }` plus `@media (hover: none) { .tools5 { opacity: 1; } }`.
findings.fix: Project-wide: wrap hover-only surface changes in `@media (hover: hover)` (R6 fix policy calls this mechanical, but 342 rules is a structural sweep — do it per feature, starting with card grids: codex-list, fps-list, news-list, hangar-dashboard).

findings.what: Hover styles are never wrapped in @media (hover: hover), so touch users get sticky hover states — including a translateY lift that stays after a tap. Project-wide convention; raised once.
findings.evidence: `grep -rn "hover: hover" src/app/admin` = 0, whole `src` = 1. Examples: src/app/admin/feedback/admin-feedback.component.ts:1173 `.sc-btn.micro:hover:not(:disabled), .link-btn:hover { transform: translateY(-1px); }`, admin.component.ts:761 `.table tbody tr:hover`, telemetry-stats.component.ts:443 `.product:hover`, feedback-attachments.component.ts:366 `.att-thumb:hover`.
findings.fix: Project-level: wrap the transform/colour hover rules in `@media (hover: hover)`, starting with the lifts at admin-feedback.component.ts:1173; add the convention to the auto-polish reference.

findings.what: The keybinds toolbar draws two different segmented-control styles side by side (device tabs vs DE|EN switch) instead of the app's `sc-segmented` (carry-over polish 'keybinds .devices onto sc-segmented' not applied).
findings.evidence: keybinds.component.ts:389-395 `.devices { … border-radius: 10px; … } .dev { … border-radius: 7px; … } .dev.active { background: var(--sc-accent) …}` vs :420-432 `.seg { … border-radius: 8px; … } .seg-btn { … border-right: 1px solid …}`; template :137-145 and :151-163 hand-roll both groups; `sc-segmented` is used by codex-list.component.ts:181-185 and imported from '../shared/segmented-control.component'.

findings.what: The feedback board fetches every topic and every reply of every topic on each 20 s idle poll, with the reply query carrying all topic ids in one `in(...)` list; nothing is paged server-side, so the request grows with the board and will eventually exceed URL limits.
findings.evidence: src/app/admin/feedback/admin-feedback.component.ts:2137-2142 `.from('admin_feedback').select(…).order(…)` (no limit/range), :2161-2165 `.from('admin_feedback_messages')….in('feedback_id', feedbackIds)` with `feedbackIds = rows.map(r => r.id)` (2148), :2207-2211 same for author messages; polled by useAutoRefresh (2121, 20 000 ms per src/app/core/auto-refresh.ts:17). Only the Geliefert band pages client-side (1535-1537).
findings.fix: Load delivered/archived topics older than N days lazily (range query on `processed_at`) and replace the id-list GET with an RPC/view `admin_feedback_threads(active_only boolean)` that returns messages joined server-side; keep the 20 s poll for active rows only.

findings.what: Three god components: the feedback board, its composer and the users page each bundle several screens' worth of template, styles, data access and state into one class.
findings.evidence: src/app/admin/feedback/admin-feedback.component.ts 2 672 lines (template ≈ 820, styles ≈ 330, class ≈ 1 300 covering data access, motion, search, filters, topic sheet, decline sheet, author channel, review gate); src/app/admin/feedback/feedback-composer.component.ts 1 297; src/app/admin/admin.component.ts 1 714 (users, reports, moderation, access requests, allowlist, invite, share link, 4 refresh loops). Compare the carry-over item 'component size (codex-detail 4.7k lines)'.
findings.fix: Split admin-feedback along its existing ng-template seams (`row`/`message`/`path` → sc-feedback-stream-card, the opened topic → sc-feedback-topic-sheet, filters → sc-feedback-filter-sheet) with the data layer in a FeedbackBoardService; extract the moderation card from admin.component into sc-admin-moderation.

findings.what: No workflow runs the web app's test suite, typecheck or build — `npm test`, `test:gate` and `test:assets-worker` only run on a developer machine through /ship; a PR that breaks the suite is not stopped by CI.
findings.evidence: .github/workflows/{browser-extension-build,data-uploader-build,edge-functions-deploy,readme-docs-sync,wallpaper-app-build}.yml — `grep -rn 'npm test\|ng test\|test:gate\|test:assets-worker'` hits only data-uploader-build.yml:34 (`run: npm test`, uploader package); edge-functions-deploy.yml:69 runs only `npm run check:edge-functions`; scripts/vercel-build.sh runs prebuild → build → postbuild, no tests; docs/feedback-routine.md:189 documents the web gate as a local command.
findings.fix: Add .github/workflows/web-app-ci.yml on pull_request/push to main: `npm ci`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm test` (ChromeHeadless is available on ubuntu-latest), plus `npm run test:gate` and `npm run test:assets-worker`.

findings.what: Two log tables grow without bound: `api_request_log` (the migration comment promises an 'autopurge cron' that no migration creates; the limiter only reads the last 60 s) and `telemetry_events` (no prune; each event may carry an unbounded `detail` jsonb from the client while every other field is clamped).
findings.evidence: supabase/migrations/20260529_public_api_tokens.sql:96 `-- For now (alpha, expected <100 req/min) a single table + autopurge cron is fine.`; `grep -rn api_request_log supabase/migrations` → only that file, `grep cron.schedule … | grep -i api_request_log\|telemetry` → 0. ingest-telemetry/index.ts:176 `detail: (isCrash ? ev.extra : ev.detail) ?? null,` (no size cap; cf. :167-170 clamp()).
findings.fix: New migration: pg_cron job `delete from api_request_log where ts < now() - interval '1 day'` (daily) and a retention for telemetry_events (e.g. 90 days); in ingest-telemetry cap `detail` (e.g. reject or truncate JSON.stringify(detail) > 4 kB).

findings.what: Error envelopes are inconsistent and some carry hard-coded German/English sentences that the admin UI prints verbatim, bypassing ngx-translate: the api uses `{error:{code,message}}`, most functions `{error:'<code>'}`, and several put prose or DE text into `error`/`message`.
findings.evidence: invite-user/index.ts:96 `json({ error: 'forbidden — admin role required' }, 403)`, :129 `'allowlist write failed: ' + allowErr.message`, :205 `message: 'Diese E-Mail ist bereits registriert. …'`; delete-user/index.ts:216 `'Dieser Account ist geschützt …'`, :235 `'Letzter Admin kann nicht gelöscht werden. …'`; uex-proxy/index.ts:249 `{ error: 'server not configured (UEX token missing)' }`; process-p4k/index.ts:355 `{ error: 'POST required' }`. Consumer: src/app/admin/admin.component.ts:1308 `text: payload.message ?? payload.error ?? error?.message ?? this.translate.instant(…)`.
findings.fix: Return stable snake_case codes only in `error` (keep `message` for operator context), and map codes to i18n keys in admin.component.ts (`admin.register.err.<code>`) instead of printing `payload.message`.

findings.what: Database errors are returned raw to public/anonymous callers (PostgREST `error.message` with table, column and constraint text) but mostly not logged server-side, so the operator sees nothing while a third-party API client gets schema internals.
findings.evidence: api/handlers/news.ts:255-258 `{ error: { code: 'query_failed', message: error.message } }` (no console); keybinds.ts:129-133 and :157-162 same; patch.ts:313-318; tokens.ts:552-555/573-578/606-610; desktop-latest/index.ts:256 and :268 `{ error: 'query_failed', message: error.message }` (release-token path, no session); check-bundle/index.ts:76. Only tokens.ts:551 logs (`console.error('create_token_failed', error)`).
findings.fix: In api/_router.ts `json()` callers: `console.error(code, { endpoint: ctx.endpoint, err: error.message })` and return a generic message (`'Database query failed.'`) for 5xx; same one-liner in desktop-latest/check-bundle.

findings.what: Every edge function copies the same CORS block, json() helper and admin gate; the shared helpers that exist are private to the `api` function.
findings.evidence: supabase/functions: 19 of 20 functions declare their own `const CORS`/`CORS_HEADERS` (ingest-catalog:46, starscape-summary:27, desktop-session:57, invite-user:53, delete-user:30, rsi-roadmap:41, ingest-bundle:33, ingest-telemetry:29, desktop-latest:37, concept-page:79, process-p4k:24, patch-stability-sample:62, readme-sync:41, uex-proxy:18, rsi-upcoming-ships:43, check-bundle:15, ingest-skins:73, ship-link:38, fetch-verse-news:68) and 14 declare `function json(body, status = 200)`; diff of invite-user vs ship-link CORS and json(): identical; the getUser→profiles.role==='admin'→403 gate is copied at invite-user:84-97, readme-sync:118-131, delete-user:72, concept-page:274, ship-link:187, api/handlers/tokens.ts:86; api/_cors.ts, api/_router.ts:182 (json) and api/_auth.ts exist only for the api function; no supabase/functions/_shared/ directory.
findings.fix: Create supabase/functions/_shared/http.ts (CORS constants, json(), preflight()) and _shared/admin-gate.ts (requireAdmin(req) → user | Response) and import them from each function (Supabase bundles `_shared` on deploy); leave api/ on its middleware.

findings.what: The same helpers are copy-pasted across functions with no `_shared/` folder: a CORS constant in 20 files, a `json()` response helper in 15 files, the `getUser + profiles.role` gate in 12 places, and the release-token validation in four functions (plus twice in desktop-latest) that the comments ask to keep 'in lockstep' by hand — the is_current regression (CHANGELOG 0.86.x) already hit all four at once.
findings.evidence: `grep -rn "Access-Control-Allow-Origin" supabase/functions --include=*.ts | grep -v test` → 20 files; `grep -rn "^function json\|function jsonResp\|export function json"` → 15 definitions; `grep -c "\['admin', 'collaborator'\]\|role !== 'admin'\|role === 'admin'"` → 12; release-token query at ingest-bundle/index.ts:97-107, ingest-catalog/index.ts:171-177, ingest-skins/index.ts:147-159, verify-release-token/index.ts:294-318, desktop-latest/index.ts:174-181 and :206-212 ("keep these in lockstep").
findings.fix: Create supabase/functions/_shared/{cors.ts,json.ts,auth.ts,release-token.ts} and import them (the deploy bundler includes relative imports); start with release-token.ts since it is the security-relevant copy.

findings.what: supabase-js is imported two different ways: 16 files pin `esm.sh/@supabase/supabase-js@2.45.4`, five use the floating `jsr:@supabase/supabase-js@2` (fetch-verse-news, patch-stability-sample, process-p4k, rsi-roadmap, rsi-upcoming-ships), so a deploy of those five can pick up a new minor/patch silently and two copies of the client ship in the bundles.
findings.evidence: `grep -rhn "supabase-js@" supabase/functions --include=*.ts | sed … | sort | uniq -c` → `16 2.45.4`, `5 2`; e.g. fetch-verse-news/index.ts:7 `from 'jsr:@supabase/supabase-js@2'` vs api/index.ts:20 `from 'https://esm.sh/@supabase/supabase-js@2.45.4'`.
findings.fix: Add supabase/functions/deno.json (or import_map) mapping `@supabase/supabase-js` to one pinned version and import it by bare specifier everywhere.

findings.what: No SQL-level test covers any RLS policy, guard trigger or RPC; the load-bearing invariants (my_feedback revoke/grant pair, hangar share guard, profiles_role_write_guard, prune_codex_builds keep-2/never-current) are verified only by comments and one-off 'red-team passes'.
findings.evidence: `ls supabase/tests` → no such directory; `find . -name '*.sql' -path '*test*'` (excluding node_modules) → none; package.json has no `supabase test db` script. Client-side, `codex_facet_values` has a direct spec (src/app/codex/codex.service.spec.ts:704-805) but `codex_armor_rating` is only exercised indirectly through src/app/codex/set/codex-set.component.spec.ts and prune_codex_builds has none.
findings.fix: Add a pgTAP suite under supabase/tests (run via `supabase test db` in CI) with one test per invariant: my_feedback INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE denied for authenticated, share-guard rejects follows_owner false→true, prune_codex_builds(2) keeps is_current and the two newest per channel, is_admin(uuid) not callable by anon.

findings.what: Feedback attachments (including screenshots in admin-only threads) are world-readable by URL and listable, because the feedback-images bucket is public with a bucket-wide anon/authenticated SELECT policy; the schema itself flags this as an open item that never got one.
findings.evidence: supabase/migrations/20260713000000_feedback_images_bucket.sql:30-35 `create policy "feedback_images_public_read" on storage.objects for select to anon, authenticated using (bucket_id = 'feedback-images');` and bucket `public = true` at :24-26; 20260726170000_user_feedback_channel.sql:37-43 'KNOWN, PRE-EXISTING GAP … attachments in ADMIN replies are not secret today either … Worth its own item.' Only later touch: 20260904040000 widens allowed_mime_types to NULL (:32-34), read side unchanged.
findings.fix: Make the bucket private and serve attachments through createSignedUrl (or a small proxy) in the feedback components; scope the storage SELECT policy to `public.is_admin() or (storage.foldername(name))[1] = auth.uid()::text`. Needs a migration plus client changes in the feedback composer/thread renderers.

findings.what: The build exit guard looks for the completion marker per stdout chunk, so a marker split across two `data` events is never seen; a hung ng build then waits the full 300 s hard ceiling instead of the 30 s grace before being killed (still exits 0 when index.html + ngsw.json exist).
findings.evidence: scripts/build-with-exit-guard.mjs:95 `if (!sawCompletion && chunk.toString('utf8').includes(COMPLETION_MARKER))`; :112-121 hard timer → `finish(0)` when `artefactsComplete()`; success definition = marker + grace + `dist/sc-companion/browser/{index.html,ngsw.json}` exist (:37-42), any non-zero ng exit propagates (:135), `code === null` (signal) counts as success when artefacts exist (:131-134).
findings.fix: Keep a rolling tail (`tail = (tail + text).slice(-2 * COMPLETION_MARKER.length)`) and test `tail.includes(COMPLETION_MARKER)` in `onOutput`; add a split-marker case to build-with-exit-guard.test.mjs.

findings.what: The ship rank card marks the weakest axis only by an amber ring on the radar and an amber bar fill — no text or aria twin says which axis is weakest.
findings.evidence: src/app/codex/codex-rank-card.component.ts:73-74 `@if (weakestAxisVertex(); as wv) { }`, :177 ``, :284 `.radar .weak-axis { stroke: var(--sc-warning) }`, :322 `.bar-fill.weak { background: var(--sc-warning); }`; `grep -n 'weak' codex-rank-card.component.ts` shows no i18n/sr-only text.

findings.what: Non-compositor transitions: two `transition: all` rules and a quality bar that animates `width`.

findings.what: src/app/codex holds 71 non-spec files flat (95 with subfolders) and src/app/news 34 flat; the file names already show the natural groups.
findings.evidence: find src/app/codex -maxdepth 1 non-spec .ts: 71 (29 components, 34 plain modules, 7 services, 1 types) beside detail/ (2), holo/ (9), set/ (8), stage/ (2), testing/ (1); basename prefixes: ship* 7, upcoming* 3, loadout* 3, keybind* 3, swap* 2, rank* 2, hardpoint* 2, fps* 2, kpi* 2, landing* 2, mission* 2, weapon* 2; news/ 34 flat (patch-* 20).

findings.what: codex-detail leaves two timers running past destroy (copy-link toast, deferred rank-cohort kick-off); the list components clear theirs in DestroyRef.onDestroy.
findings.evidence: codex-detail.component.ts:2111 `private linkCopiedTimer …`, :3111 `this.linkCopiedTimer = setTimeout(() => this.linkCopied.set(false), 2000);`, :2326 `setTimeout(() => void this.loadRankCohort(), 0);` — no `ngOnDestroy`/`DestroyRef.onDestroy` clearing them (grep `onDestroy|ngOnDestroy` in the file: none). findings.what: src/env.d.ts declares NG_APP_POSTHOG_PROJECT_TOKEN / NG_APP_POSTHOG_HOST on import.meta.env, but nothing reads import.meta.env (the PostHog key lives in environment.ts) — dead declaration that suggests a second key path that does not exist.

findings.what: Dead global CSS keeps a red channel pill alive: `.sc-pill.eptu` paints in --sc-accent-hot but no template uses .sc-pill with a channel class (only `.sc-pill.current` on release notes).
findings.evidence: src/styles.scss:710 `&.eptu { … color: var(--sc-accent-hot); border: 1px solid var(--sc-accent-hot); }`; grep `sc-pill` in src/app: only src/app/release-notes/release-notes.component.ts:25 `class="sc-pill current"`.

findings.what: Pending timers and a requestAnimationFrame retry loop outlive their components: the hangar picker's hover/collapse timers, the landing and bridge search debounce, and the Spot stage's 20-frame layout retry keep firing (and can start a search request) after navigation away.
findings.evidence: src/app/codex/stage/hangar-picker.component.ts:609-610 `private hoverTimer … private collapseTimer` with no DestroyRef/ngOnDestroy in the file (`grep -n 'DestroyRef\|ngOnDestroy\|onDestroy'` → none); src/app/codex/codex-landing.component.ts:565,919 `this.searchTimer = setTimeout(() => this.searchTerm.set(value), SEARCH_DEBOUNCE_MS)` never cleared on destroy (no DestroyRef), same in codex-bridge.component.ts:499,643; src/app/codex/stage/codex-stage.component.ts:352-360 `if ((stageW === 0 || stageH === 0) && attempts++ < 20) { requestAnimationFrame(run); return; }` with no destroyed guard.
findings.fix: Inject `DestroyRef` and clear the timers / set a `destroyed` flag in `onDestroy` (one line each).

findings.what: The Google Fonts stylesheet (10 weights across Orbitron and Inter) is loaded as a render-blocking `<link rel="stylesheet">` in the head; first paint waits on fonts.googleapis.com.
findings.evidence: src/index.html:66-69 `<link href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Orbitron:wght@400;500;600;700;900&family=Inter:wght@300;400;500;600;700&display=swap" rel="stylesheet" />` (preconnect present at :61-62; `display=swap` present). LCP impact not measured here — the live gate owns that number.

findings.what: expire_stale_friend_requests() is dead: service_role-only 'cron sugar' that no cron job, edge function or script ever calls.
findings.evidence: supabase/migrations/20260904020000_social_moderation_sharing.sql:111-124 `create or replace function public.expire_stale_friend_requests() … grant execute … to service_role;` with comment 'Housekeeping sweep for a cron'; `grep -rn expire_stale_friend_requests supabase/functions src scripts` → 0 hits; only two cron.schedule calls exist (20260906130000:32, 20260925010000:69). Enforcement is elsewhere (list_my_friend_edges / respond_friend_request), so no functional impact.

findings.what: ingest_bundle_atomic parses the JWT-claims GUC with a bare `::jsonb` cast, which raises 22P02 when the setting is present but empty, whereas every sibling guard uses nullif(…, '') first.

refuted.what: Icon buttons with fixed sizes under the 44 px touch minimum and no `--sc-tap-min` floor (the lists already use `max(32px, var(--sc-tap-min))`).
reason: All six selectors sit on `<button type="button">` elements (upcoming-grid:40,135; weapon-detail:89; component-modal:96; compare-tray:51; extension-promo:26). src/styles.scss:346-359 already applies `min-height: var(--sc-tap-min); min-width: var(--sc-tap-min);` (48px) to every `button`, `a`, `[role=button]` etc. under `@media (pointer: coarse)`. `min-width`/`min-height` always win over `width`/`height` regardless of selector specificity, so these controls already render at 48x48 on coarse pointers. The `.act { width: max(32px, var(--sc-tap-min)) }` contrast in codex-list is redundant belt-and-braces, not a missing guard. The finding's claim that there is 'no --sc-tap-min floor' rests on looking only at the component stylesheet.

All six selectors are <button type="button"> elements (upcoming-grid :40/:135, codex-weapon-detail :89, codex-component-modal :96, codex-compare-tray :51, extension-promo :26) with default Emulated encapsulation, so the global rule in src/styles.scss:349-361 applies: under @media (pointer: coarse) every `button` gets `min-height: var(--sc-tap-min); min-width: var(--sc-tap-min)` = 48px. CSS min-width/min-height always override a fixed width/height, so these buttons already have a 48px hit area on touch. On fine pointers --sc-tap-min is 0px (styles.scss:61), so the proposed `max(<px>, var(--sc-tap-min))` resolves to the current value. The fix is a no-op on both pointer types; the lists' explicit max() is belt-and-braces, not a required pattern.

refuted.what: The Supabase fake is re-implemented per spec file (`function fakeSupabase` four times plus `fakeSupabaseQueued`) instead of living next to frames.ts in src/app/testing/.
reason: The grep count is accurate (4x fakeSupabase + 1x fakeSupabaseQueued) but the premise that they are one fake 're-implemented' is not: the five functions model different Supabase surfaces with different signatures — admin-feedback builds a thenable PostgREST chain keyed by tables and records inserts/updates; routine-heartbeat takes a single `{data,error}` for `.select().eq().maybeSingle()`; role.service takes a `FakeSession|null` and exposes a `releaseSession` gate on `realClient.auth.getSession` to reproduce a boot race; fakeSupabaseQueued adds a call counter with per-call outcomes; impersonation-guards takes `(role, approved)` on `realClient`. A single `fakeSupabase(tables)` builder cannot replace the auth-shaped ones (they need `realClient.auth.*`, the gate, the counter) — the proposed fix would break role.service.spec and impersonation-guards.spec. The cited file hangar-role-slot.spec.ts defines no fakeSupabase at all (it inlines `{ client }` at :60). Only role.service.spec:40 and impersonation-guards.spec:39 share a near-identical realClient shape; a narrower 'share the auth realClient fake' finding could stand, but not this one.

The grep count is accurate but the premise is not: the four `fakeSupabase` functions are four different-shaped test doubles that only share a name. admin-feedback.component.spec.ts builds a tables-map chain that records inserts/updates and stubs storage; routine-heartbeat.service.spec.ts returns one fixed `maybeSingle` result; role.service.spec.ts and impersonation-guards.spec.ts stub `realClient.auth` (getSession gated on a promise to reproduce a boot race, onAuthStateChange, signOut spies) plus a role/is_approved row. None of them is a re-implementation of another, and the proposed single `fakeSupabase(tables)` builder cannot serve the auth specs at all. No project rule asks for a shared Supabase fake; src/app/testing/ holds only frames.ts (frame timing helper), not a doubles library. At most an observation.

refuted.what: A spec written after the frame-hygiene fix still awaits real view-transition frames, the same failure class REQ-28 removed.
reason: The spec already guards against exactly the hidden-page case: lines 164-167 `if (typeof document.startViewTransition !== 'function' || document.visibilityState !== 'visible' || reducedMotion()) { pending(...); return; }` — on a hidden Karma page it is marked pending, it never awaits `ready`/`finished`. The evidence omits the guard that sits right above the cited lines: the real-browser spec starts with `if (typeof document.startViewTransition !== 'function' || document.visibilityState !== 'visible' || reducedMotion()) { pending(...) }` (src/app/codex/set/set-arsenal-transition.spec.ts, 'SetArsenalTransition in a real browser transition'). refuted.what: Both desktop hand-off pages poll `auth.ready()` every 30 ms with no deadline; if auth never settles the page shows the "authorizing" dots forever with no error or retry.
reason: The cited line numbers do not exist (desktop-auth.component.ts is 247 lines, desktop-read-auth 232); the real `waitFor` is at :237-246 / :222-231, called at :159 / :149. The behaviour (30 ms poll, no deadline) is real, but it is the app-wide convention, not a desktop-page defect: auth.guard.ts:16-26, approved.guard.ts:77, public-only.guard.ts:38 use the identical `setInterval(..., 30)` wait with no timeout. `auth.ready()` settles in practice: AuthService.init() sets `_ready` from `getSession().then` (:50-53) AND from `onAuthStateChange` (:58-60), which supabase-js fires with INITIAL_SESSION on subscription, so 'auth never settles' has no realistic trigger the guards would not equally suffer. Adding a bespoke 15 s error path to two pages while every guard keeps polling forever is inconsistent; if the failure mode matters it belongs in a shared helper, which is a different, broader finding.

Evidence is accurate (unbounded 30 ms `setInterval`, no clearInterval on destroy, in both desktop hand-off pages), but the premise 'if auth never settles' has no observed instance: `AuthService.init()` sets `_ready` true in `getSession().then(...)` (which resolves with `{data,error}` rather than rejecting) and again on every `onAuthStateChange` event, so `ready()` settles within milliseconds in practice. The identical unbounded `waitForReady` poll is the app-wide convention in `src/app/auth/auth.guard.ts` (every gated route), so the desktop pages are not a special case — a local deadline in two pages would diverge from the guard rather than harden anything. The residual (interval keeps ticking after an early navigate-away) is a micro-leak with no user impact. Downgraded to info; if a deadline is wanted it belongs in AuthService once, as a separate issue.

refuted.what: `.mcp.json` always sends an Authorization header, so with SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN unset the Supabase MCP gets `Bearer ` and rejects the session (401) instead of falling back to OAuth — this is why the Supabase MCP was unavailable in this run.
reason: The behaviour is real (empty Bearer → 401, no OAuth fallback) but it is a documented, deliberate design decision, and the proposed fix is either already done or contradicts it. `.claude/deep-knowledge/supabase.md:265-278` ('Project-scoped MCP (.mcp.json) — PAT header, no OAuth') documents exactly this: the PAT header is used because the OAuth flow ended in 'Unauthorized' for this project on 2026-09-13 and a non-interactive scheduled-task session cannot run OAuth anyway; 'Missing variable → claude mcp get supabase says Failed to connect' is spelled out, as is the fallback (`scripts/routine-gate.mjs` reads the same token from Credential Manager). `scripts/set-supabase-env.ps1:1-8` already carries the header comment the fix asks for. The remaining gap is only that the note lives in supabase.md rather than local-dev.md; the cloud audit container simply has no SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN, which is an environment matter, not a repo defect.

Documented deliberate decision, not a defect. CHANGELOG 0.84.7 (line 1339-1347) records that the OAuth login via /mcp ended 'Unauthorized' for this project and that scheduled-task sessions cannot run it, so .mcp.json deliberately sends the CLI token from SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN and explicitly states 'ohne die Variable: Failed to connect, der Fallback greift wie bisher'. The env var is already documented in scripts/set-supabase-env.ps1:3-4, scripts/routine-gate.mjs:34 and docs/routine/tasks/nightly-admin-feedback/SKILL.md:18. The 401 in this cloud session is the documented behaviour when the variable is unset, and the proposed 'drop the headers block' would re-break the routine's MCP path.
